71753eeaf7eb4923e2b3.english: 21:21 Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword: * my only one from the hand of the dog.

72abcb313c592395aae8.latin: 21:22 Salva me ex ore leónis: * et a córnibus unicórnium humilitátem meam.
72abcb313c592395aae8.english: 21:22 Save me from the lion’s mouth; * and my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.

ce8a075b94fd46615bbe.latin: 21:23 Narrábo nomen tuum frátribus meis: * in médio ecclésiæ laudábo te.
ce8a075b94fd46615bbe.english: 21:23 I will declare thy name to my brethren: * in the midst of the church will I praise thee.

19180224bb799fd8e9d5.latin: 21:24 Qui timétis Dóminum, laudáte eum: * univérsum semen Iacob, glorificáte eum.
19180224bb799fd8e9d5.english: 21:24 Ye that fear the Lord, praise him: * all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him.

025406d0408f02d8e48c.latin: 21:25 Tímeat eum omne semen Israël: * quóniam non sprevit, neque despéxit deprecatiónem páuperis:
025406d0408f02d8e48c.english: 21:25 Let all the seed of Israel fear him: * because he hath not slighted nor despised the supplication of the poor man.

57fda367a4ffb8f89933.latin: 21:25 Nec avértit fáciem suam a me: * et cum clamárem ad eum, exaudívit me.
57fda367a4ffb8f89933.english: 21:25 Neither hath he turned away his face from me: * and when I cried to him he heard me.

e6fd1feab23de692fdec.latin: 21:26 Apud te laus mea in ecclésia magna: * vota mea reddam in conspéctu timéntium eum.
e6fd1feab23de692fdec.english: 21:26 With thee is my praise in a great church: * I will pay my vows in the sight of them that fear him.

4976fca58df0b063abc0.latin: 21:27 Edent páuperes, et saturabúntur: et laudábunt Dóminum qui requírunt eum: * vivent corda eórum in sǽculum sǽculi.
4976fca58df0b063abc0.english: 21:27 The poor shall eat and shall be filled: and they shall praise the Lord that seek him: * their hearts shall live for ever and ever.

abd4dd9e92593799fea8.latin: 21:28 Reminiscéntur et converténtur ad Dóminum * univérsi fines terræ:
abd4dd9e92593799fea8.english: 21:28 All the ends of the earth * shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord:

241d5e1f5b3430af7290.latin: 21:28 Et adorábunt in conspéctu eius * univérsæ famíliæ géntium.
241d5e1f5b3430af7290.english: 21:28 And all the kindreds of the Gentiles * shall adore in his sight.

29b2d2b7c60bef6e5c1b.latin: 21:29 Quóniam Dómini est regnum: * et ipse dominábitur géntium.
29b2d2b7c60bef6e5c1b.english: 21:29 For the kingdom is the Lord’s; * and he shall have dominion over the nations.

0fa09859fd1a77c7daa1.latin: 21:30 Manducavérunt et adoravérunt omnes pingues terræ: * in conspéctu eius cadent omnes qui descéndunt in terram.
0fa09859fd1a77c7daa1.english: 21:30 All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and have adored: * all they that go down to the earth shall fall before him.

b5b3e77bf65ffe5e9b3b.latin: 21:31 Et ánima mea illi vivet: * et semen meum sérviet ipsi.
b5b3e77bf65ffe5e9b3b.english: 21:31 And to him my soul shall live: * and my seed shall serve him.

1e9aca0b9a0eb96b9ee3.latin: 21:32 Annuntiábitur Dómino generátio ventúra: * et annuntiábunt cæli iustítiam eius pópulo qui nascétur, quem fecit Dóminus.
1e9aca0b9a0eb96b9ee3.english: 21:32 There shall be declared to the Lord a generation to come: * and the heavens shall shew forth his justice to a people that shall be born, which the Lord hath made.

831f83563f89d8ceba15.latin: Ant. Dómine in virtúte tua lætábitur rex.
831f83563f89d8ceba15.english: Ant. The king rejoices in Thy strength, O Lord.

ad9b7ad02aa4369b8948.latin: Ant. Dóminus regit me * et nihil mihi déerit: in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit. ‡
ad9b7ad02aa4369b8948.english: Ant. The Lord ruleth me * and I shall want nothing. He hath set me in a place of pasture. ‡

3a01146190dc6a03d560.latin: 22:1 Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
3a01146190dc6a03d560.english: 22:1 The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. He hath set me in a place of pasture.

4e750411cdc65cf37683.latin: 22:2 ‡ Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
4e750411cdc65cf37683.english: 22:2 ‡ He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.

09c0f13a946272447b41.latin: 22:3 Dedúxit me super sémitas iustítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
09c0f13a946272447b41.english: 22:3 He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.

64399f5fc46c34d9da14.latin: 22:4 Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
64399f5fc46c34d9da14.english: 22:4 For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.

8bad5f8205db744a555b.latin: 22:4 Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
8bad5f8205db744a555b.english: 22:4 Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.

ff296ce7d69510e327a9.latin: 22:5 Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
ff296ce7d69510e327a9.english: 22:5 Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.

b63769ff339f0a9ef1d3.latin: 22:5 Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!
b63769ff339f0a9ef1d3.english: 22:5 Thou hast anointed my head with oil; * and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!

fb264ee61ffd1eea56ad.latin: 22:6 Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
fb264ee61ffd1eea56ad.english: 22:6 And thy mercy will follow me * all the days of my life.

f72a2eee9f49290acfa4.latin: 22:6 Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.
f72a2eee9f49290acfa4.english: 22:6 And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord * unto length of days.

befbeb4b8368524f7434.latin: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
befbeb4b8368524f7434.english: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

047d239cf71b267ab076.latin: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
047d239cf71b267ab076.english: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

bac504803475b854847e.latin: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?
bac504803475b854847e.english: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

79acd2c11f659f225141.latin: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.
79acd2c11f659f225141.english: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

2f2f0153e56f8be856f6.latin: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
2f2f0153e56f8be856f6.english: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

514e91695808881a89ea.latin: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.
514e91695808881a89ea.english: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

d5ba10fcea0c0c7ba1ac.latin: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
d5ba10fcea0c0c7ba1ac.english: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

3a1a01d9b3f31571ee4e.latin: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
3a1a01d9b3f31571ee4e.english: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

f0763946dbbfe50663d6.latin: 23:9 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
f0763946dbbfe50663d6.english: 23:9 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

b332220e82404aab2350.latin: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
b332220e82404aab2350.english: 23:10 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

c5d9cb09191d577091b8.latin: Ant. Dóminus regit me et nihil mihi déerit: in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
c5d9cb09191d577091b8.english: Ant. The Lord ruleth me and I shall want nothing. He hath set me in a place of pasture.

a7ffbd94829e7099f993.latin: Ant. Óculi mei * semper ad Dóminum.
a7ffbd94829e7099f993.english: Ant. My eyes * are ever towards the Lord.

5d4f9745bae38f50e2e3.latin: 24:1 Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.
5d4f9745bae38f50e2e3.english: 24:1 To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

ec52ee744855c2a8179c.latin: 24:3 Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.
ec52ee744855c2a8179c.english: 24:3 Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.

a7efd567b977d57b1e3d.english: 24:4 Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.

9e05a5e1771e350ad081.latin: 24:4 Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.
9e05a5e1771e350ad081.english: 24:4 Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, * and teach me thy paths.

d692907bd5445a8f8c0e.latin: 24:5 Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.
d692907bd5445a8f8c0e.english: 24:5 Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.

d95dc81ed733642ad831.latin: 24:6 Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.
d95dc81ed733642ad831.english: 24:6 Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.

9e0d38419bdd09dc4be2.latin: 24:7 Delícta iuventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.
9e0d38419bdd09dc4be2.english: 24:7 The sins of my youth * and my ignorances do not remember.

6eb5245033b7ffa6640c.latin: 24:7 Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.
6eb5245033b7ffa6640c.english: 24:7 According to thy mercy remember thou me: * for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.

8e809f65d04e3ba2626b.latin: 24:8 Dulcis et rectus Dóminus: * propter hoc legem dabit delinquéntibus in via.
8e809f65d04e3ba2626b.english: 24:8 The Lord is sweet and righteous: * therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.

be99dd3684232616a5e9.latin: 24:9 Díriget mansuétos in iudício: * docébit mites vias suas.
be99dd3684232616a5e9.english: 24:9 He will guide the mild in judgment: * he will teach the meek his ways.

4d0035627e89b5c0f453.latin: 24:10 Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum eius et testimónia eius.
4d0035627e89b5c0f453.english: 24:10 All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, * to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.

406357cf21c07ade7003.latin: 24:11 Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.
406357cf21c07ade7003.english: 24:11 For thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin: * for it is great.

d81d9baf2881df19f6b5.latin: 24:12 Quis est homo qui timet Dóminum? * legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit.
d81d9baf2881df19f6b5.english: 24:12 Who is the man that feareth the Lord? * He hath appointed him a law in the way he hath chosen.

2e5b8dd530a63ed6ef1e.latin: 24:13 Ánima eius in bonis demorábitur: * et semen eius hereditábit terram.
2e5b8dd530a63ed6ef1e.english: 24:13 His soul shall dwell in good things: * and his seed shall inherit the land.

3b8499f81b6c4086b0f2.latin: 24:14 Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum: * et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.
3b8499f81b6c4086b0f2.english: 24:14 The Lord is a firmament to them that fear him: * and his covenant shall be made manifest to them.

850eeb75a28905793b44.latin: 24:15 Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum: * quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos.
850eeb75a28905793b44.english: 24:15 My eyes are ever towards the Lord: * for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare.

852917f5898a62e94f82.latin: 24:16 Réspice in me, et miserére mei: * quia únicus et pauper sum ego.
852917f5898a62e94f82.english: 24:16 Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me; * for I am alone and poor.

5a33e67524c8560fc1fa.latin: 24:17 Tribulatiónes cordis mei multiplicátæ sunt: * de necessitátibus meis érue me.
5a33e67524c8560fc1fa.english: 24:17 The troubles of my heart are multiplied: * deliver me from my necessities.

6c9487ef9e7e3b4bb3ba.latin: 24:18 Vide humilitátem meam, et labórem meum: * et dimítte univérsa delícta mea.
6c9487ef9e7e3b4bb3ba.english: 24:18 See my abjection and my labour; * and forgive me all my sins.

10165ab969cc6b962a30.latin: 24:19 Réspice inimícos meos quóniam multiplicáti sunt, * et ódio iníquo odérunt me.
10165ab969cc6b962a30.english: 24:19 Consider my enemies for they are multiplied, * and have hated me with an unjust hatred.

16b8f5f4e1031d6e2556.latin: 24:20 Custódi ánimam meam, et érue me: * non erubéscam quóniam sperávi in te.
16b8f5f4e1031d6e2556.english: 24:20 Keep thou my soul, and deliver me: * I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in thee.

8860bd368f752158d66d.latin: 24:21 Innocéntes et recti adhæsérunt mihi: * quia sustínui te.
8860bd368f752158d66d.english: 24:21 The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: * because I have waited on thee.

99c80050ba01fcf1c2dd.latin: 24:22 Líbera, Deus, Israël, * ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus suis.
99c80050ba01fcf1c2dd.english: 24:22 Deliver Israel, O God, * from all his tribulations.

bf40de40335cf9ca5772.latin: 25:1 Iúdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.
bf40de40335cf9ca5772.english: 25:1 Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: * and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.

86ba25eaa199001df36f.latin: 25:2 Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.
86ba25eaa199001df36f.english: 25:2 Prove me, O Lord, and try me; * burn my reins and my heart.

92817d4558da98020f9a.latin: 25:3 Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.
92817d4558da98020f9a.english: 25:3 For thy mercy is before my eyes; * and I am well pleased with thy truth.

c056edd042d56edbbe7a.latin: 25:4 Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.
c056edd042d56edbbe7a.english: 25:4 I have not sat with the council of vanity: * neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.

cadacff700fdc7a90a3d.latin: 25:5 Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.
cadacff700fdc7a90a3d.english: 25:5 I have hated the assembly of the malignant; * and with the wicked I will not sit.

98ceb47fdabaf6ef1833.latin: 25:6 Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
98ceb47fdabaf6ef1833.english: 25:6 I will wash my hands among the innocent; * and will compass thy altar, O Lord:

9d20f515db5cf8adf309.latin: 25:7 Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
9d20f515db5cf8adf309.english: 25:7 That I may hear the voice of thy praise: * and tell of all thy wondrous works.

2563a66c5a07b05176a0.latin: 25:8 Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
2563a66c5a07b05176a0.english: 25:8 I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; * and the place where thy glory dwelleth.

5f18fcbad28eaa74c5f4.latin: 25:9 Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
5f18fcbad28eaa74c5f4.english: 25:9 Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: * nor my life with bloody men:

29b12cf5650cf6c48e18.latin: 25:10 In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
29b12cf5650cf6c48e18.english: 25:10 In whose hands are iniquities: * their right hand is filled with gifts.

14ed733fd96646b7cf94.latin: 25:11 Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.
14ed733fd96646b7cf94.english: 25:11 But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: * redeem me, and have mercy on me.

d48de5902654ddbc428c.latin: 25:12 Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
d48de5902654ddbc428c.english: 25:12 My foot hath stood in the direct way: * in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.

44b820272cb5a52af5e4.latin: Ant. Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum.
44b820272cb5a52af5e4.english: Ant. My eyes are ever towards the Lord.

2f74f7a8f4c18169857f.latin: ℣. Memor fui nocte nóminis tui Dómine.
2f74f7a8f4c18169857f.english: ℣. In the night I have remembered thy name, O Lord:

5c81c22de819e25e6f73.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
5c81c22de819e25e6f73.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

a2216bfd670a03caba82.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
℟. Amen.
Lectio 1
Incipit liber primus Machabæórum
1 Mac 1:1-3
1 Et factum est, postquam percússit Alexánder Philíppi Mácedo, qui primus regnávit in Grǽcia, egréssus de terra Cethim, Daríum regem Persárum et Medórum,
2 Constítuit prǽlia multa et obtínuit ómnium munitiónes et interfécit reges terræ,
3 Et pertránsiit usque ad fines terræ et accépit spólia multitúdinis géntium, et síluit terra in conspéctu eius.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟. Adapériat Dóminus cor vestrum in lege sua et in præcéptis suis et fáciat pacem in diébus vestris:
* Concédat vobis salútem, et rédimat vos a malis.
℣. Exáudiat Dóminus oratiónes vestras, et reconciliétur vobis, nec vos déserat in témpore malo.
℟. Concédat vobis salútem, et rédimat vos a malis.
a2216bfd670a03caba82.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.
℟. Amen.
Reading 1
Lesson from the first book of Machabees
1 Mac 1:1-3
1 Now it came to pass, after that Alexander the son of Philip the Macedonian, who first reigned in Greece, coming out of the land of Cethim, had overthrown Darius king of the Persians and Medes:
2 He fought many battles, and took the strongholds of all, and slew the kings of the earth:
3 And he went through even to the ends of the earth, and took the spoils of many nations: and the earth was quiet before him.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟. The Lord open your hearts in His law and commandments, and send peace in your days.
* May He grant you salvation and redeem you out of all evil.
℣. The Lord hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in the time of trouble.
℟. May He grant you salvation and redeem you out of all evil.

264facf1a2be09cbe988.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
℟. Amen.
Lectio 2
1 Mac 1:4-7
4 Et congregávit virtútem et exércitum fortem nimis, et exaltátum est et elevátum cor eius,
5 Et obtínuit regiónes géntium et tyránnos, et facti sunt illi in tribútum.
6 Et post hæc décidit in lectum, et cognóvit quia morerétur,
7 Et vocávit púeros suos nóbiles, qui secum erant nutríti a iuventúte, et divísit illis regnum suum, cum adhuc víveret.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟. Exáudiat Dóminus oratiónes vestras, et reconciliétur vobis, nec vos déserat in témpore malo,
* Dóminus, Deus noster.
℣. Det vobis cor ómnibus, ut colátis eum et faciátis eius voluntátem.
℟. Dóminus, Deus noster.
264facf1a2be09cbe988.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.
℟. Amen.
Reading 2
1 Mac 1:4-7
4 And he gathered a power, and a very strong army: and his heart was exalted and lifted up.
5 And he subdued countries of nations, and princes: and they became tributaries to him.
6 And after these things, he fell down upon his bed, and knew that he should die.
7 And he called his servants the nobles that were brought up with him from his youth: and he divided his kingdom among them, while he was yet alive.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟. The Lord hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in the time of trouble
* Even He, the Lord our God.
℣. Give you all an heart to serve Him, and to do His will.
℟. Even He, the Lord our God.

8d8aa2becc1b4929488a.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
℟. Amen.
Lectio 3
1 Mac 1:8-11
8 Et regnávit Alexánder annis duódecim et mórtuus est.
9 Et obtinuérunt púeri eius regnum, unusquísque in loco suo,
10 Et imposuérunt omnes sibi diadémata post mortem eius, et fílii eórum post eos annis multis. Et multiplicáta sunt mala in terra.
11 Et éxiit ex eis radix peccátrix, Antíochus illústris, fílius Antíochi regis qui fúerat Romæ obses, et regnávit in anno centésimo trigésimo séptimo regni Græcórum.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟. Congregáti sunt inimíci nostri, et gloriántur in virtúte sua: cóntere fortitúdinem illórum, Dómine, et dispérge illos:
* Ut cognóscant quia non est álius qui pugnet pro nobis, nisi tu, Deus noster.
℣. Dispérge illos in virtúte tua, et déstrue eos, protéctor noster, Dómine.
℟. Ut cognóscant quia non est álius qui pugnet pro nobis, nisi tu, Deus noster.
8d8aa2becc1b4929488a.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.
℟. Amen.
Reading 3
1 Mac 1:8-11
8 And Alexander reigned twelve years, and he died.
9 And his servants made themselves kings every one in his place:
10 And they all put crowns upon themselves after his death, and their sons after them many years, and evils were multiplied in the earth.
11 And there came out of them a wicked root, Antiochus the Illustrious, the son of king Antiochus, who had been a hostage at Rome: and he reigned in the hundred and thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟. Our enemies are gathered together, and make their boast of their own strength. O Lord, break their power, and scatter them
* That they may know that there is none other that fighteth for us, but only Thou, O our God!
℣. Scatter them in thy strength, and destroy them, O Lord our Shield.
℟. That they may know that there is none other that fighteth for us, but only Thou, O our God!

c6642976550bf30104ee.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. In unitáte Sancti Spíritus, benedícat nos Pater et Fílius.
℟. Amen.
Lectio 4
1 Mac 1:12-16
12 In diébus illis exiérunt ex Israël fílii iníqui et suasérunt multis dicéntes: Eámus et disponámus testaméntum cum géntibus, quæ circa nos sunt, quia, ex quo recéssimus ab eis, invenérunt nos multa mala.
13 Et bonus visus est sermo in óculis eórum.
14 Et destinavérunt áliqui de pópulo, et abiérunt ad regem, et dedit illis potestátem ut fácerent iustítiam géntium;
15 Et ædificavérunt gymnásium in Ierosólymis secúndum leges natiónum,
16 Et fecérunt sibi præpútia et recessérunt a testaménto sancto, et iuncti sunt natiónibus, et venúmdati sunt ut fácerent malum.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟. Dixit Iudas Simóni fratri suo: Elige tibi viros et vade, líbera fratres tuos in Galilǽam; ego autem et Iónathas frater tuus íbimus in Galaadítim:
* Sicut fúerit volúntas in cælo, sic fiat.
℣. Accingímini, fílii poténtes, et estóte paráti: quóniam mélius est nobis, mori in bello, quam vidére mala gentis nostræ et sanctórum.
℟. Sicut fúerit volúntas in cælo, sic fiat.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Sicut fúerit volúntas in cælo, sic fiat.
c6642976550bf30104ee.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. In the unity of the Holy Ghost, may the Father and the Son bless us.
℟. Amen.
Reading 4
1 Mac 1:12-16
12 In those days there went out of Israel wicked men, and they persuaded many, saying: Let us go, and make a covenant with the heathens that are round about us: for since we departed from them, many evils have befallen us.
13 And the word seemed good in their eyes.
14 And some of the people determined to do this, and went to the king: and he gave them license to do after the ordinances of the heathens.
15 And they built a place of exercise in Jerusalem, according to the laws of the nations:
16 And they made themselves prepuces, and departed from the holy covenant, and joined themselves to the heathens, and were sold to do evil.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟. Judas said unto Simon his brother: Choose thee out men, and go, and deliver thy brethren that are in Galilee and I, and Jonathan thy brother, will go into the country of Galaad.
* As the Will is in heaven, so let it be.
℣. Arm yourselves, ye valiant men, and be in readiness for it is better for us to die in battle, than to behold the calamities of our people, and our sanctuary.
℟. As the Will is in heaven, so let it be.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. As the Will is in heaven, so let it be.

2ff51be75c60410185d1.english: Ant. The Lord is the defence * of my life.

b44951e713c9f24cf6bd.latin: 26:1 Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
b44951e713c9f24cf6bd.english: 26:1 The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?

afb2a48376ab69efe8da.latin: 26:1 Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
afb2a48376ab69efe8da.english: 26:1 The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?

cd04e0815b408783f214.latin: 26:2 Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:
cd04e0815b408783f214.english: 26:2 Whilst the wicked draw near against me, * to eat my flesh.

b1821cc2b4f26176b8dd.latin: 26:2 Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
b1821cc2b4f26176b8dd.english: 26:2 My enemies that trouble me, * have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.

3889649f0a30ba52f2e7.latin: 26:3 Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.
3889649f0a30ba52f2e7.english: 26:3 If armies in camp should stand together against me, * my heart shall not fear.

7fba1afe0c4e15baee67.latin: 26:3 Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.
7fba1afe0c4e15baee67.english: 26:3 If a battle should rise up against me, * in this will I be confident.

39aeddf43aadae57dddc.latin: 26:4 Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
39aeddf43aadae57dddc.english: 26:4 One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

f9c8a4ba0f1282ed9ee2.latin: 26:4 Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum eius.
f9c8a4ba0f1282ed9ee2.english: 26:4 That I may see the delight of the Lord, * and may visit his temple.

7cae0232f3dc7e69a8c2.latin: 26:5 Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
7cae0232f3dc7e69a8c2.english: 26:5 For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; * in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.

3b2d1de21ba500c647f6.latin: 26:6 In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
3b2d1de21ba500c647f6.english: 26:6 He hath exalted me upon a rock: * and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.

83f0bd9e2a768cc221aa.latin: 26:6 Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo eius hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
83f0bd9e2a768cc221aa.english: 26:6 I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: * I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

fe4fea3b2e472ff558d1.latin: 26:7 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.
fe4fea3b2e472ff558d1.english: 26:7 Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: * have mercy on me and hear me.

db5f3a5740737595b1a1.latin: 26:8 Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
db5f3a5740737595b1a1.english: 26:8 My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: * thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

56f4477cfb85d3ddbfe4.latin: 26:9 Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
56f4477cfb85d3ddbfe4.english: 26:9 Turn not away thy face from me; * decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.

d77e2f0076cacb549b16.latin: 26:9 Adiútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
d77e2f0076cacb549b16.english: 26:9 Be thou my helper, * forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

b96d0d82c3e4aee0c667.latin: 26:10 Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
b96d0d82c3e4aee0c667.english: 26:10 For my father and my mother have left me: * but the Lord hath taken me up.

7b843be5d737b821894c.latin: 26:11 Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
7b843be5d737b821894c.english: 26:11 Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, * and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

5939e3e0324fd61869a5.latin: 26:12 Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
5939e3e0324fd61869a5.english: 26:12 Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; * for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.

f3b1b0c8864cad8fa5b9.latin: 26:13 Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.
f3b1b0c8864cad8fa5b9.english: 26:13 I believe to see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.

c2723e5e23fd501484ba.latin: 26:14 Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
c2723e5e23fd501484ba.english: 26:14 Expect the Lord, do manfully, * and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

ae2095bba42e8a07e4a2.latin: 27:1 Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.
ae2095bba42e8a07e4a2.english: 27:1 Unto thee will I cry, O Lord: my God, be not thou silent to me: * lest if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

5f5f3f0aeb1249b6e33a.latin: 27:2 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.
5f5f3f0aeb1249b6e33a.english: 27:2 Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to thee; * when I lift up my hands to thy holy temple.

ddaac5e5d96ebbd2f642.latin: 27:3 Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.
ddaac5e5d96ebbd2f642.english: 27:3 Draw me not away together with the wicked; * and with the workers of iniquity destroy me not:

b0c793b4bbc1ed81dc82.latin: 27:3 Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.
b0c793b4bbc1ed81dc82.english: 27:3 Who speak peace with their neighbour, * but evils are in their hearts.

5addd28cdc4a8f54ea10.latin: 27:4 Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.
5addd28cdc4a8f54ea10.english: 27:4 Give them according to their works, * and according to the wickedness of their inventions.

90f2d1aa4326cbc5636b.latin: 27:4 Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: * redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.
90f2d1aa4326cbc5636b.english: 27:4 According to the works of their hands give thou to them: * render to them their reward.

6293f05c08aaf4805074.latin: 27:5 Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum eius * déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.
6293f05c08aaf4805074.english: 27:5 Because they have not understood the works of the Lord, and the operations of his hands: * thou shalt destroy them, and shalt not build them up.

77c051900edf9e400545.latin: 27:6 Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
77c051900edf9e400545.english: 27:6 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath heard the voice of my supplication.

b9ba82b27b7d05a4698d.latin: 27:7 Dóminus adiútor meus, et protéctor meus: * in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adiútus sum.
b9ba82b27b7d05a4698d.english: 27:7 The Lord is my helper and my protector: * in him hath my heart confided, and I have been helped.

e8156949492aa1a5d6f8.latin: 27:7 Et reflóruit caro mea: * et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.
e8156949492aa1a5d6f8.english: 27:7 And my flesh hath flourished again, * and with my will I will give praise to him.

6cfe1f4a5b61357e3aff.latin: 27:8 Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: * et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est.
6cfe1f4a5b61357e3aff.english: 27:8 The Lord is the strength of his people, * and the protector of the salvation of his anointed.

0a3f1ff70cd3b7f88cfc.latin: 27:9 Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: * et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
0a3f1ff70cd3b7f88cfc.english: 27:9 Save, O Lord, thy people, and bless thy inheritance: * and rule them and exalt them for ever.

d860aff8e0e2a53dfcd9.english: Ant. The Lord is the defence of my life.

6d66ab45ce3196a8a140.latin: Ant. Adoráte * Dóminum in aula sancta eius.
6d66ab45ce3196a8a140.english: Ant. Worship the Lord * in His holy courts.

41935a06fedc715da6f8.latin: 28:1 Afférte Dómino, fílii Dei: * afférte Dómino fílios aríetum.
41935a06fedc715da6f8.english: 28:1 Bring to the Lord, O ye children of God: * bring to the Lord the offspring of rams.

ff05676919b7ec472059.latin: 28:2 Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, afférte Dómino glóriam nómini eius: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto eius.
ff05676919b7ec472059.english: 28:2 Bring to the Lord glory and honour: bring to the Lord glory to his name: * adore ye the Lord in his holy court.

2c2fd7a0388ce0461e55.latin: 28:3 Vox Dómini super aquas, Deus maiestátis intónuit: * Dóminus super aquas multas.
2c2fd7a0388ce0461e55.english: 28:3 The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; the God of majesty hath thundered, * The Lord is upon many waters.

43c5ed72ab7929324ad1.latin: 28:4 Vox Dómini in virtúte: * vox Dómini in magnificéntia.
43c5ed72ab7929324ad1.english: 28:4 The voice of the Lord is in power; * the voice of the Lord in magnificence.

8af3ee1962963a9bb22a.latin: 28:5 Vox Dómini confringéntis cedros: * et confrínget Dóminus cedros Líbani:
8af3ee1962963a9bb22a.english: 28:5 The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars: * yea, the Lord shall break the cedars of Libanus.

a9c17c49fe052d655235.latin: 28:6 Et commínuet eas tamquam vítulum Líbani: * et diléctus quemádmodum fílius unicórnium.
a9c17c49fe052d655235.english: 28:6 And shall reduce them to pieces, as a calf of Libanus, * and as the beloved son of unicorns.

8d3edbd60b354b69c6f3.latin: 28:7 Vox Dómini intercidéntis flammam ignis: * vox Dómini concutiéntis desértum: et commovébit Dóminus desértum Cades.
8d3edbd60b354b69c6f3.english: 28:7 The voice of the Lord divideth the flame of fire: * The voice of the Lord shaketh the desert: and the Lord shall shake the desert of Cades.

8f7b84f3bcde2cc1443d.latin: 28:9 Vox Dómini præparántis cervos, et revelábit condénsa: * et in templo eius omnes dicent glóriam.
8f7b84f3bcde2cc1443d.english: 28:9 The voice of the Lord prepareth the stags: and he will discover the thick woods: * and in his temple all shall speak his glory.

e5bfb6ba6f6bb3deb829.latin: 28:10 Dóminus dilúvium inhabitáre facit: * et sedébit Dóminus Rex in ætérnum.
e5bfb6ba6f6bb3deb829.english: 28:10 The Lord maketh the flood to dwell: * and the Lord shall sit king for ever.

71c396b27ccafb0ec347.latin: 28:11 Dóminus virtútem pópulo suo dabit: * Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
71c396b27ccafb0ec347.english: 28:11 The Lord will give strength to his people: * the Lord will bless his people with peace.

2e92dc5ba76587e9bcb2.latin: 29:2 Exaltábo te, Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: * nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.
2e92dc5ba76587e9bcb2.english: 29:2 I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: * and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me.

98b0e8b064e37e781225.latin: 29:3 Dómine, Deus meus, clamávi ad te, * et sanásti me.
98b0e8b064e37e781225.english: 29:3 O Lord my God, I have cried to thee, * and thou hast healed me.

9c2dd9969844ba29e062.latin: 29:4 Dómine, eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam: * salvásti me a descendéntibus in lacum.
9c2dd9969844ba29e062.english: 29:4 Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell: * thou hast saved me from them that go down into the pit.

9ccdc283821336f919c0.latin: 29:5 Psállite Dómino, sancti eius: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis eius.
9ccdc283821336f919c0.english: 29:5 Sing to the Lord, O ye his saints: * and give praise to the memory of his holiness.

0521f6199d63711a6cb5.latin: 29:6 Quóniam ira in indignatióne eius: * et vita in voluntáte eius.
0521f6199d63711a6cb5.english: 29:6 For wrath is in his indignation; * and life in his good will.

f9791af1d896fcf5cd38.latin: 29:6 Ad vésperum demorábitur fletus: * et ad matutínum lætítia.
f9791af1d896fcf5cd38.english: 29:6 In the evening weeping shall have place, * and in the morning gladness.

567161d934704b754993.latin: 29:7 Ego autem dixi in abundántia mea: * Non movébor in ætérnum.
567161d934704b754993.english: 29:7 And in my abundance I said: * I shall never be moved.

3e6fe8bdb2d79a1ac4fa.latin: 29:8 Dómine, in voluntáte tua, * præstitísti decóri meo virtútem.
3e6fe8bdb2d79a1ac4fa.english: 29:8 O Lord, in thy favour, * thou gavest strength to my beauty.

cab06ee0be40a0f57a03.latin: 29:8 Avertísti fáciem tuam a me, * et factus sum conturbátus.
cab06ee0be40a0f57a03.english: 29:8 Thou turnedst away thy face from me, * and I became troubled.

fbab82b8ddf484165aa6.latin: 29:9 Ad te, Dómine, clamábo: * et ad Deum meum deprecábor.
fbab82b8ddf484165aa6.english: 29:9 To thee, O Lord, will I cry: * and I will make supplication to my God.

cd4261a1115caaa2f89d.latin: 29:10 Quæ utílitas in sánguine meo, * dum descéndo in corruptiónem?
cd4261a1115caaa2f89d.english: 29:10 What profit is there in my blood, * whilst I go down to corruption?

f0e110719ffcf613b2c5.latin: 29:10 Numquid confitébitur tibi pulvis, * aut annuntiábit veritátem tuam?
f0e110719ffcf613b2c5.english: 29:10 Shall dust confess to thee, * or declare thy truth?

1199aff2cb92307d8e8c.latin: 29:11 Audívit Dóminus, et misértus est mei: * Dóminus factus est adiútor meus.
1199aff2cb92307d8e8c.english: 29:11 The Lord hath heard, and hath had mercy on me: * the Lord became my helper.

2b4d000f04c75482ca64.latin: 29:12 Convertísti planctum meum in gáudium mihi: * conscidísti saccum meum, et circumdedísti me lætítia:
2b4d000f04c75482ca64.english: 29:12 Thou hast turned for me my mourning into joy: * thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness:

6ce839aa36dd1ea765a5.latin: 29:13 Ut cantet tibi glória mea, et non compúngar: * Dómine, Deus meus, in ætérnum confitébor tibi.
6ce839aa36dd1ea765a5.english: 29:13 To the end that my glory may sing to thee, and I may not regret: * O Lord my God, I will give praise to thee for ever.

408139d2bd29dc2f20ab.latin: Ant. Adoráte Dóminum in aula sancta eius.
408139d2bd29dc2f20ab.english: Ant. Worship the Lord in His holy courts.

fa914f739505e9a74d00.latin: Ant. In tua iustítia * líbera me, Dómine.
fa914f739505e9a74d00.english: Ant. Deliver me * in Thy righteousness.

ad80bfa9ffff73e3813b.latin: 30:2 In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me.
ad80bfa9ffff73e3813b.english: 30:2 In thee, O Lord, have I hoped, let me never be confounded: * deliver me in thy justice.

5e3e4e984f86b151499d.latin: 30:3 Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * accélera ut éruas me.
5e3e4e984f86b151499d.english: 30:3 Bow down thy ear to me: * make haste to deliver me.

756a0538bc029ba600e0.latin: 30:3 Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii: * ut salvum me fácias.
756a0538bc029ba600e0.english: 30:3 Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a house of refuge, * to save me.

3c21c44c5bd37bd41b9d.latin: 30:4 Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu: * et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.
3c21c44c5bd37bd41b9d.english: 30:4 For thou art my strength and my refuge; * and for thy name’s sake thou wilt lead me, and nourish me.

255dac640cfae263ccf9.latin: 30:5 Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.
255dac640cfae263ccf9.english: 30:5 Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they have hidden for me: * for thou art my protector.

c4ab61720fd9b3caf62e.latin: 30:6 In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.
c4ab61720fd9b3caf62e.english: 30:6 Into thy hands I commend my spirit: * thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, the God of truth.

7b83ad2f4d8862d3c95f.english: 30:7 Thou hast hated them that regard vanities, * to no purpose.

d6bd3f063c951f9b386e.latin: 30:7 Ego autem in Dómino sperávi: * exsultábo, et lætábor in misericórdia tua.
d6bd3f063c951f9b386e.english: 30:7 But I have hoped in the Lord: * I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy.

46714f667b122943c005.latin: 30:8 Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, * salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.
46714f667b122943c005.english: 30:8 For thou hast regarded my humility, * thou hast saved my soul out of distresses.

24f23aa5d18a29f4561c.latin: 30:9 Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: * statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.
24f23aa5d18a29f4561c.english: 30:9 And thou hast not shut me up in the hands of the enemy: * thou hast set my feet in a spacious place.

b7dcdc6dbca543569b26.latin: 30:10 Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor: * conturbátus est in ira óculus meus, ánima mea, et venter meus:
b7dcdc6dbca543569b26.english: 30:10 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted: * my eye is troubled with wrath, my soul, and my belly:

34846fe5ce3b2be416de.latin: 30:11 Quóniam defécit in dolóre vita mea: * et anni mei in gemítibus.
34846fe5ce3b2be416de.english: 30:11 For my life is wasted with grief: * and my years in sighs.

6a19598fb89bcfb4fb8e.latin: 30:11 Infirmáta est in paupertáte virtus mea: * et ossa mea conturbáta sunt.
6a19598fb89bcfb4fb8e.english: 30:11 My strength is weakened through poverty * and my bones are disturbed.

983a956944a8bacb7afb.latin: 30:12 Super omnes inimícos meos factus sum oppróbrium et vicínis meis valde: * et timor notis meis.
983a956944a8bacb7afb.english: 30:12 I am become a reproach among all my enemies, and very much to my neighbours; * and a fear to my acquaintance.

08450b9c07ceb4fe1529.latin: 30:12 Qui vidébant me, foras fugérunt a me: * oblivióni datus sum, tamquam mórtuus a corde.
08450b9c07ceb4fe1529.english: 30:12 They that saw me without fled from me. * I am forgotten as one dead from the heart.

998b1bca07ff16127491.latin: 30:13 Factus sum tamquam vas pérditum: * quóniam audívi vituperatiónem multórum commorántium in circúitu.
998b1bca07ff16127491.english: 30:13 I am become as a vessel that is destroyed. * For I have heard the blame of many that dwell round about.

6d67b2663744218e461e.latin: 30:14 In eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, * accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.
6d67b2663744218e461e.english: 30:14 While they assembled together against me, * they consulted to take away my life.

95c1ce20a1fcc6009d36.latin: 30:15 Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: * dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.
95c1ce20a1fcc6009d36.english: 30:15 But I have put my trust in thee, O Lord: * I said: Thou art my God. My lots are in thy hands.

c0be0c374b38a79964cc.latin: 30:16 Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, * et a persequéntibus me.
c0be0c374b38a79964cc.english: 30:16 Deliver me out of the hands of my enemies; * and from them that persecute me.

1969c4afee2fb71fcb46.latin: 30:17 Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: * Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.
1969c4afee2fb71fcb46.english: 30:17 Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; save me in thy mercy. * Let me not be confounded, O Lord, for I have called upon thee.

2e6ff03d9a7d3416074a.latin: 30:18 Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: * muta fiant lábia dolósa.
2e6ff03d9a7d3416074a.english: 30:18 Let the wicked be ashamed, and be brought down to hell. * Let deceitful lips be made dumb.

6f52e2f2163c2e8535ac.latin: 30:19 Quæ loquúntur advérsus iustum iniquitátem: * in supérbia, et in abusióne.
6f52e2f2163c2e8535ac.english: 30:19 Which speak iniquity against the just, * with pride and abuse.

0134300632d545c49f16.latin: 30:20 Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, * quam abscondísti timéntibus te.
0134300632d545c49f16.english: 30:20 How great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord, * which thou hast hidden for them that fear thee!

ed531e957b67e9eb807c.latin: 30:20 Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, * in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.
ed531e957b67e9eb807c.english: 30:20 Which thou hast wrought for them that hope in thee, * in the sight of the sons of men.

44c2e95379accd2a9a61.latin: 30:21 Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ * a conturbatióne hóminum.
44c2e95379accd2a9a61.english: 30:21 Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy face, * from the disturbance of men.

5edef0c18767225d3e07.latin: 30:21 Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo * a contradictióne linguárum.
5edef0c18767225d3e07.english: 30:21 Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle * from the contradiction of tongues.

4abfe2a3a72df8ea4f04.latin: 30:22 Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi in civitáte muníta.
4abfe2a3a72df8ea4f04.english: 30:22 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath shewn his wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city.

b38ca5e89abd25fd2d3e.latin: 30:23 Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: * Proiéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum.
b38ca5e89abd25fd2d3e.english: 30:23 But I said in the excess of my mind: * I am cast away from before thy eyes.

128d8b072254adb0150b.latin: 30:23 Ídeo exaudísti vocem oratiónis meæ, * dum clamárem ad te.
128d8b072254adb0150b.english: 30:23 Therefore thou hast heard the voice of my prayer, * when I cried to thee.

5b7b3907122423829ad9.latin: 30:24 Dilígite Dóminum omnes sancti eius: * quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.
5b7b3907122423829ad9.english: 30:24 O love the Lord, all ye his saints: * for the Lord will require truth, and will repay them abundantly that act proudly.

6396df05827aabd9fd20.latin: 30:25 Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, * omnes, qui sperátis in Dómino.
6396df05827aabd9fd20.english: 30:25 Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, * all ye that hope in the Lord.

9c577420db1b4b9c252b.latin: 31:1 Beáti quorum remíssæ sunt iniquitátes: * et quorum tecta sunt peccáta.
9c577420db1b4b9c252b.english: 31:1 Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven * and whose sins are covered.

9759fe5ab1a0653d8dad.latin: 31:2 Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum, * nec est in spíritu eius dolus.
9759fe5ab1a0653d8dad.english: 31:2 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin, * and in whose spirit there is no guile.

da425b67b9b0e820a5df.latin: 31:3 Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.
da425b67b9b0e820a5df.english: 31:3 Because I was silent my bones grew old; * whilst I cried out all the day long.

94fccc854d4691dc39f9.latin: 31:4 Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.
94fccc854d4691dc39f9.english: 31:4 For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: * I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened.

2c23bae4cb9a920a8fb6.latin: 31:5 Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et iniustítiam meam non abscóndi.
2c23bae4cb9a920a8fb6.english: 31:5 I have acknowledged my sin to thee, * and my injustice I have not concealed.

497f6a0ce3102ed56e83.latin: 31:5 Dixi: Confitébor advérsum me iniustítiam meam Dómino: * et tu remisísti impietátem peccáti mei.
497f6a0ce3102ed56e83.english: 31:5 I said I will confess against myself my injustice to the Lord: * and thou hast forgiven the wickedness of my sin.

e8b1f5603815769d7e3c.latin: 31:6 Pro hac orábit ad te omnis sanctus, * in témpore opportúno.
e8b1f5603815769d7e3c.english: 31:6 For this shall every one that is holy pray to thee * in a seasonable time.

bcf80b2649d78066764f.latin: 31:6 Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.
bcf80b2649d78066764f.english: 31:6 And yet in a flood of many waters, * they shall not come nigh unto him.

39567974921ab7b78484.latin: 31:7 Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.
39567974921ab7b78484.english: 31:7 Thou art my refuge from the trouble which hath encompassed me: * my joy, deliver me from them that surround me.

ef106bf1326e880feef0.latin: 31:8 Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.
ef106bf1326e880feef0.english: 31:8 I will give thee understanding, and I will instruct thee in this way, in which thou shalt go: * I will fix my eyes upon thee.

948f32219dea05f4baf6.latin: 31:9 Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.
948f32219dea05f4baf6.english: 31:9 Do not become like the horse and the mule, * who have no understanding.

0dd18c532e85e04d5465.latin: 31:9 In camo et freno maxíllas eórum constrínge, * qui non appróximant ad te.
0dd18c532e85e04d5465.english: 31:9 With bit and bridle bind fast their jaws, * who come not near unto thee.

9f9486ab990d489b2213.latin: 31:10 Multa flagélla peccatóris, * sperántem autem in Dómino misericórdia circúmdabit.
9f9486ab990d489b2213.english: 31:10 Many are the scourges of the sinner, * but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.

f25d130abc056bd97982.latin: 31:11 Lætámini in Dómino et exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.
f25d130abc056bd97982.english: 31:11 Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just, * and glory, all ye right of heart.

3caad3c637624b5b1729.english: Ant. Deliver me in Thy righteousness.

a0fb47f412fbf5463897.english: ℣. I rose at midnight to give praise to thee.

3e83c16d9a2eab367fc6.english: ℟. For the judgments of thy justification.

0ab312b9d11b5a4b474e.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.
℟. Amen.
Lectio 5
Ex libro Officiórum sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi
Lib. 1, Cap. 40
Fortásse áliquos béllica defíxos glória tenet, ut putent solam esse præliárem fortitúdinem; et ídeo me ad ista deflexísse, quia illa nostris déforet. Quam fortis Iesus Nave, ut uno prǽlio quinque reges captos stérneret cum pópulis suis! Deínde cum advérsum Gabaonítas urgéret prǽlium, et vererétur ne nox impedíret victóriam, magnitúdine mentis et fídei clamávit: Stet sol, et stetit, donec victória consummarétur. Gédeon in trecéntis viris de ingénti pópulo et acérbo hoste revéxit triúmphum. Iónathas adoléscens virtútem magnam fecit in prǽlio.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟. Impetum inimicórum ne timuéritis: mémores estóte, quómodo salvi facti sunt patres nostri:
* Et nunc clamémus in cælum et miserébitur nostri Deus noster.
℣. Mementóte mirabílium eius, quæ fecit pharaóni et exercítui eius in Mari Rubro.
℟. Et nunc clamémus in cælum et miserébitur nostri Deus noster.
0ab312b9d11b5a4b474e.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. May God the Father Omnipotent, be to us merciful and clement.
℟. Amen.
Reading 5
From the Book upon Duties written by St. Ambrose, Bishop (of Milan).
Bk. i. ch. 40
There may perchance be some who are so blinded by the glory of war as to think there is no valour but warlike valour, and that the reason why I have taken up other subjects is that among us there is no warlike valour whereof to speak. But what was the valour of Josue the son of Nun, when in one battle he laid low five nations, and took prisoners their kings when he was fighting against the Gibeonites, and feared lest the closing in of night should cut short his victory, he cried aloud in the greatness of his mind and of his faith? And he said, in the sight of Israel: Sun stand thou still over against Gibeon, and thou Moon over against the valley of Ajalon and the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies Josue x. 12, 13. Gideon, with three hundred men, won the victory over the vast people, and the savage enemy. The lad Jonathan waxed valiant in fight.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟. Be ye not afraid of the assault of the enemy; remember how our fathers were delivered.
* Now, therefore, let us cry unto heaven, and our God will have mercy upon us.
℣. Remember His marvellous works that He hath done unto Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea.
℟. Now, therefore, let us cry unto heaven, and our God will have mercy upon us.

01c2693a8f6dff162ec1.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. Christus perpétuæ det nobis gáudia vitæ.
℟. Amen.
Lectio 6
Quid de Machabǽis loquar? Sed prius de pópulo dicam patrum; qui cum essent paráti ad repugnándum pro templo Dei et pro legítimis suis, dolo hóstium die lacessíti sábbati, maluérunt vulnéribus offérre nuda córpora, quam repugnáre, ne violárent sábbatum. Itaque omnes læti se obtulérunt morti. Sed Machabǽi considerántes quod hoc exémplo gens omnis posset períre, sábbato étiam, cum ipsi in bellum provocaréntur, ulti sunt innocéntium necem fratrum suórum. Unde póstea stimulátus rex Antíochus, cum bellum accénderet per duces suos Lýsiam, Nicánorem, Górgiam, ita cum Orientálibus suis et Assýriis attrítus est cópiis, ut quadragínta et octo míllia in médio campi a tribus míllibus prosterneréntur.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟. Congregátæ sunt gentes in multitúdine, ut dímicent contra nos, et ignorámus quid ágere debeámus:
* Dómine Deus, ad te sunt óculi nostri, ne pereámus.
℣. Tu scis quæ cógitant in nos: quómodo potérimus subsístere ante fáciem illórum, nisi tu ádiuves nos?
℟. Dómine Deus, ad te sunt óculi nostri, ne pereámus.
01c2693a8f6dff162ec1.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. May Christ to all His people give, for ever in His sight to live.
℟. Amen.
Reading 6
Shall I speak of the Maccabees But before I speak of them, I will speak of their fathers, even of them who, when they were ready to fight for the Temple of God and for their own rights, were assailed by a trick of their enemies upon the Sabbath day, and were willing rather to offer their bodies naked to the sword than to strike back again and break the Sabbath, and so they gave themselves up gladly to death but when the Maccabees bethought them that the whole nation might thus perish, avenged the innocent blood of their brethren even upon the Sabbath day when they were provoked to battle, and afterward, when King Antiochus had been stirred up to make war on them by his generals, even Lysias and Nicanor and Gorgias, he and his Eastern and Assyrian forces were so crushed that forty and eight thousand were laid low on the field by three thousand.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟. The heathen are assembled together to fight against us, and we know not what we should do.
* Our eyes look unto thee, O Lord our God, that we should not perish.
℣. What things they imagine against us, Thou knowest. How shall we be able to stand against them, except Thou be our help.
℟. Our eyes look unto thee, O Lord our God, that we should not perish.

9da69e33d24c156f8695.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. Ignem sui amóris accéndat Deus in córdibus nostris.
℟. Amen.
Lectio 7
Virtútem ducis Iudæ Machabǽi de uno eius mílite consideráte. Namque Eleázarus, cum supereminéntem céteris elephántem loríca vestítum régia advérteret, arbitrátus quod in eo esset rex, cursu cóncito in médium legiónis se prorúpit: et, abiécto clýpeo, utráque manu interficiébat, donec perveníret ad béstiam, atque intrávit sub eam, et subiécto gládio interémit eam. Itaque cadens béstia oppréssit Eleázarum, atque ita mórtuus est.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟. Tua est poténtia, tuum regnum, Dómine: tu es super omnes gentes:
* Da pacem, Dómine, in diébus nostris.
℣. Creátor ómnium, Deus, terríbilis et fortis, iustus et miséricors.
℟. Da pacem, Dómine, in diébus nostris.
9da69e33d24c156f8695.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. May the Spirit's fire Divine in our hearts enkindled shine.
℟. Amen.
Reading 7
What was the valour of Judas the Maccabean leader we may judge by the type of one of his men. When Eleazar saw an elephant bigger than the rest, and adorned with the King's harness, he thought that the King was riding thereon, and he threw himself into the midst of the enemy, and cast away his shield and slew on either hand until he was come to the beast, and ran underneath it, and killed it with his sword, and so the beast fell upon Eleazar and crushed him, and he died.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟. Thine, O Lord, is the power, thine is the kingdom, O Lord, and Thou art exalted above all the heathen.
* Give peace in our time, O Lord.
℣. O Lord God, Creator of all things, Who art fearful and strong, righteous and merciful.
℟. Give peace in our time, O Lord.

c3a4c7dae4b301702a78.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. A cunctis vítiis et peccátis absólvat nos virtus sanctæ Trinitátis.
℟. Amen.
Lectio 8
Quanta ígitur virtus ánimi! primo, ut mortem non timéret; deínde, ut circumfúsus legiónibus inimicórum, in confértos raperétur hostes, médium penetráret agmen, et contémpta morte ferócior, abiécto clýpeo, utráque manu vulnerátæ molem béstiæ subíret ac sustinéret: post infra ipsam succéderet, quo plenióri feríret ictu; cuius ruína inclúsus magis quam oppréssus, suo est sepúltus triúmpho.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟. Ornavérunt fáciem templi corónis áureis, et dedicavérunt altáre Dómino:
* Et facta est lætítia magna in pópulo.
℣. In hymnis et confessiónibus benedicébant Dóminum.
℟. Et facta est lætítia magna in pópulo.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Et facta est lætítia magna in pópulo.
c3a4c7dae4b301702a78.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. Of all faults and sins may the power of the holy Trinity absolve us.
℟. Amen.
Reading 8
What valour was here To begin with, he feared not to die, and when the enemy surrounded him he cast himself into the midst of their ranks, pierced their column, and becoming all the fiercer through his mockery of death, he threw away his shield and upheld with both hands the huge bulk of the wounded monster beneath which he had gone the better to spite it, so that when he died with it he might well have been said not so much to be crushed as to be swallowed up in victory.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟. They decked the fore-front of the Temple with crowns of gold, and dedicated the Altar unto the Lord.
* And there was very great gladness among the people.
℣. They praised the Lord with Psalms and thanksgiving.
℟. And there was very great gladness among the people.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. And there was very great gladness among the people.

Nocturnus III
Ant. Allelúia, * allelúia, allelúia.
Canticum Isaiæ [13]
Isa 33:2-10
33:2 Dómine, miserére nostri, te enim exspectávimus; esto bráchium nostrum in mane, * et salus nostra in témpore tribulatiónis.
33:3 A voce Angeli fugérunt pópuli, * et ab exaltatióne tua dispérsæ sunt gentes.
33:4 Et congregabúntur spólia vestra sicut collígitur bruchus, * velut cum fossæ plenæ fúerint de eo.
33:5 Magnificátus est Dóminus, quóniam habitávit in excélso; * implévit Sion iudício et iustítia.
33:6 Et erit fides in tempóribus tuis: divítiæ salútis sapiéntia: * et sciéntia; timor Dómini ipse est thesáurus eius.
33:7 Ecce vidéntes clamábunt foris; * ángeli pacis amáre flebunt.
33:8 Dissipátæ sunt viæ, cessávit tránsiens per sémitam: írritum factum est pactum, * proiécit civitátes, non reputávit hómines.
33:9 Luxit et elánguit terra; * confúsus est Líbanus, et obsórduit.
33:9 Et factus est Saron sicut desértum, * et concússa est Basan, et Carmélus.
33:10 Nunc consúrgam, dicit Dóminus; * nunc exaltábor, nunc sublevábor.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
c90054571d63a896021c.english:
Nocturn III
Ant. Alleluia * alleluia, alleluia.
Canticum Isaiae [13]
Isa 33:2-10
33:2 O Lord, have mercy on us: for we have waited for thee: be thou our arm in the morning, and our salvation in the time of trouble.
33:3 At the voice of the angel the people fled, and at the lifting up thyself the nations are scattered.
33:4 And your spoils shall be gathered together as the locusts are gathered, as when the ditches are full of them.
33:5 The Lord is magnified, for he hath dwelt on high: he hath filled Sion with judgment and justice.
33:6 And there shall be faith in thy times: riches of salvation, wisdom and knowledge: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.
33:7 Behold they that see shall cry without, the angels of peace shall weep bitterly.
33:8 The ways are made desolate, no one passeth by the road, the covenant is made void, he hath rejected the cities, he hath not regarded the men.
33:9 The land hath mourned, and languished: Libanus is confounded and become foul, and Saron is become as a desert: and Basan and Carmel are shaken.
33:10 Now will I rise up, saith the Lord: now will I be exalted, now will I lift up myself.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

c4e60b6d110bc24d507e.latin:

Isa 33:13-18
33:13 Audíte, qui longe estis, quæ fécerim; * et cognóscite, vicíni, fortitúdinem meam.
33:14 Contérriti sunt in Sion peccatóres; * possédit tremor hypócritas.
33:14 Quis póterit habitáre de vobis cum igne devoránte? * quis habitábit ex vobis cum ardóribus sempitérnis?
33:15 Qui ámbulat in iustítiis et lóquitur veritátem, qui próicit avarítiam ex calúmnia, * et éxcutit manus suas ab omni múnere,
33:16 Qui obtúrat aures suas ne áudiat sánguinem, * et claudit óculos suos ne vídeat malum.
33:17 Iste in excélsis habitábit; muniménta saxórum sublímitas eius: * panis ei datus est, aquæ eius fidéles sunt.
33:18 Regem in decóre suo vidébunt óculi eius, cernent terram de longe. * Cor tuum meditábitur timórem.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
c4e60b6d110bc24d507e.english:
Canticum Isaiae [14]
Isa 33:13-18
33:13 Hear, you that are far off, what I have done, and you that are near know my strength.
33:14 The sinners in Sion are afraid, trembling hath seized upon the hypocrites. Which of you can dwell with devouring fire? which of you shall dwell with everlasting burnings?
33:15 He that walketh in justices, and speaketh truth, that casteth away avarice by oppression, and shaketh his hands from all bribes, that stoppeth his ears lest he hear blood, and shutteth his eyes that he may see no evil.
33:16 He shall dwell on high, the fortifications of rocks shall be his highness: bread is given him, his waters are sure.
33:17 His eyes shall see the king in his beauty, they shall see the land far off.
33:18 Thy heart shall meditate fear: where is the learned? where is he that pondereth the words of the law? where is the teacher of little ones?
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Eccli 36:14-19

Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum
Matt 22:1-14
In illo témpore: Loquebátur Iesus princípibus sacerdótum et pharisǽis in parábolis, dicens: Símile factum est regnum cælórum hómini regi, qui fecit núptias fílio suo. Et réliqua.
Homilía sancti Gregórii Papæ
Homilia 38 in Evangelia, post initium
Sæpe iam me dixísse mémini, quod plerúmque in sancto Evangélio regnum cælórum præsens Ecclésia nominátur: congregátio quippe iustórum, regnum cælórum dícitur. Quia enim per prophétam Dóminus dicit: Cælum mihi sedes est; et Sálomon ait: Anima iusti sedes sapiéntiæ; Paulus étiam dicit Christum Dei virtútem, et Dei sapiéntiam: líquido collígere debémus, quia si Deus sapiéntia, ánima autem iusti, sedes sapiéntiæ, dum cælum dícitur sedes Dei, cælum ergo est ánima iusti. Hinc per Psalmístam de sanctis prædicatóribus dícitur: Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei.

Homily by Pope St. Gregory the Great.
38th on the Gospels
I remember that I have often said that, in the Holy Gospel, the Church as she now is, is called the kingdom of heaven, for the kingdom of heaven is indeed the assembly of the righteous. The Lord hath said by the mouth of His Prophet: The heaven is My throne. Isa. lxvi. 1. Solomon saith: The throne of wisdom is the soul of the righteous. And Paul saith that Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God. 1 Cor. i. 24. From these passages we may clearly gather that if wisdom be God, and wisdom's throne be the soul of the righteous, and God's throne be the heaven, then the soul of the righteous is heaven. Hence also the Psalmist saith, speaking of holy preachers: The heavens declare the glory of God. xviii. 2.

The kingdom of heaven, therefore, is the Church of the righteous, even of them whose hearts seek not for anything upon earth, but who sigh so continually after the things which are above, that God doth already reign in them as He doth in heaven. Reading 12
We profess concerning Him that He is of, and in two natures, but we shrink from the blasphemy of saying that He is compounded of two persons. It will therefore be clearer and safer to say that the marriage which the Father made for His Royal Son was the wedding Him, through the mystery of the Incarnation, to His mystic Bride the Holy Church. The womb of the Maiden Mother was the marriage chamber in which this union took place. Hence it is that the Psalmist saith: In the sun hath He set His tabernacle, Who is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber. xviii. 6.2

Hymn
Maker of all, eternal King,
Who day and night about dost bring:
Who weary mortals to relieve,
Dost in their times the seasons give:
Now the shrill cock proclaims the day,
And calls the sun’s awak’ning ray
The wand’ring pilgrim’s guiding light,
That marks the watches night by night.
Roused at the note, the morning star
Heaven’s dusky veil uplifts afar:
Night’s vagrant bands no longer roam,
But from their dark ways hie them home.
The encouraged sailor’s fears are o’er,
The foaming billows rage no more:
Lo! e’en the very Church’s rock
Melts at the crowing of the cock.
O let us then like men arise;
The cock rebukes our slumbering eyes,
Bestirs who still in sleep would lie,
And shames who would their Lord deny.
New hope his clarion-note awakes,
Sickness the feeble frame forsakes,
The robber sheathes his lawless sword,
Faith to the fallen is restored.
Look on us, Jesu, when we fall,
And with thy look our souls recall:
If thou but look, our sins are gone,
And with due tears our pardon won.
Shed through our hearts thy piercing ray,
Our souls’ dull slumber drive away:
Thy name be first on every tongue,
To thee our earliest praises sung.
All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, Eternal Son, to thee,
All glory, as is ever meet,
To God the holy Paraclete.
Amen.
℣. The Lord reigns, he is clothed with beauty.
℟. The Lord is clothed with strength, and has girded Himself with power.
