℟. Thanks be to God.
℟.br. Óculi Dómini * Super metuéntes eum.
℟. Óculi Dómini * Super metuéntes eum.
℣. Et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia ejus.
℟. Super metuéntes eum.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Óculi Dómini * Super metuéntes eum.
Hymn
Inclytos Christi fámulos canámus,
Quos, fide claros nitidísque gestis,
Hac die tellus sociáta cælo
Láudibus ornat.
Quippe qui mites, húmiles, pudíci,
Nésciam culpæ coluére vitam,
Donec e terris ánimus volávit
Liber ad astra.
Inde jam gaudent míseris adésse,
Fléntium tergunt lácrimas, medéntur
Méntium plagis, vitiáta reddunt
Membra salúti.
Nostra laus ergo résonet benígnis
His Dei servis referátque grates,
Qui pia pergant ope nos juváre
Rebus in arctis.
Sit Deo soli decus et potéstas,
Laus in excélsis honor ac perénnis,
Qui suis totum móderans gubérnat
Légibus orbem.
Amen.
℣. Justi confitebúntur nómini tuo, Dómine.
℟. Et habitábunt recti cum vultu tuo.

61777c059c04d390932c.latin: Ant. A sǽculo * non audiérunt, neque áuribus percepérunt: óculus non vidit, Deus, absque te, quæ præparásti exspectántibus te.

3140c29f2d868d06242b.latin: Ant. A sǽculo non audiérunt, neque áuribus percepérunt: óculus non vidit, Deus, absque te, quæ præparásti exspectántibus te.

fd2afa0a264bb22bdadf.english: Ant. Let us make a joyful noise to * the God of our salvation.

9cb2275198f8d5350a29.english: Ant. the God of our salvation.

85063da886b6d2e0c564.latin:
Consors patérni lúminis,
Lux ipse lucis, et dies,
Noctem canéndo rúmpimus:
Assíste postulántibus.
Aufer ténebras méntium,
Fuga catérvas dǽmonum,
Expélle somnoléntiam,
Ne pigritántes óbruat.
Sic, Christe, nobis ómnibus
Indúlgeas credéntibus,
Ut prosit exorántibus,
Quod præcinéntes psállimus.
Præsta, Pater piíssime,
Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
85063da886b6d2e0c564.english:
O Light of Light, O Day-spring bright,
Co-equal in thy Father’s light:
Assist us, as with prayer and psalm
Thy servants break the twilight calm.
All darkness from our minds dispel,
And turn to flight the hosts of hell:
Bid sleepfulness our eyelids fly,
Lest overwhelmed in sloth we lie.
Jesu, thy pardon, kind and free,
Bestow on us who trust in thee:
And as thy praises we declare,
O with acceptance hear our prayer.
O Father, that we ask be done,
Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;
Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.
Amen.

4cd0277c2c5b5bb86a8c.english: Ant. God is our help * in trouble.

6cacfaca37d7f5c6476e.latin: 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adiútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
6cacfaca37d7f5c6476e.english: 45:2 Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

4e06af9acb2358fc3cf5.latin: 45:3 Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
4e06af9acb2358fc3cf5.english: 45:3 Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

f1be885e962f3f28b482.latin: 45:4 Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine eius.
f1be885e962f3f28b482.english: 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.

d66524a26a7df5284304.latin: 45:5 Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
d66524a26a7df5284304.english: 45:5 The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.

3e4c297743f205211f10.latin: 45:6 Deus in médio eius, non commovébitur: * adiuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
3e4c297743f205211f10.english: 45:6 God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.

3b003193c9d37d61d182.latin: 45:7 Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
3b003193c9d37d61d182.english: 45:7 Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.

22e5bb0fc5cae4c884db.latin: 45:8 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Iacob.
22e5bb0fc5cae4c884db.english: 45:8 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

8f815c9e2f7cd6d18f11.latin: 45:9 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
8f815c9e2f7cd6d18f11.english: 45:9 Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.

fc0ddb3741621381bf66.latin: 45:10 Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
fc0ddb3741621381bf66.english: 45:10 He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.

7ff6b12cdbc4da73142b.latin: 45:11 Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
7ff6b12cdbc4da73142b.english: 45:11 Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

2680cf5c2000d5f78a59.latin: 45:12 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Iacob.
2680cf5c2000d5f78a59.english: 45:12 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

576d5d1919ef8b088c3b.latin: 46:2 Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * iubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.
576d5d1919ef8b088c3b.english: 46:2 O clap your hands, all ye nations: * shout unto God with the voice of joy,

86597bc43fef4f67e97b.latin: 46:3 Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.
86597bc43fef4f67e97b.english: 46:3 For the Lord is high, terrible: * a great king over all the earth.

1bd77625fc2c7516c983.latin: 46:4 Subiécit pópulos nobis: * et gentes sub pédibus nostris.
1bd77625fc2c7516c983.english: 46:4 He hath subdued the people under us; * and the nations under our feet.

a4b6de56e97b05ba6189.latin: 46:5 Elégit nobis hereditátem suam: * spéciem Iacob, quam diléxit.
a4b6de56e97b05ba6189.english: 46:5 He hath chosen for us his inheritance, * the beauty of Jacob which he hath loved.

d1c849b4d37b3ab41280.latin: 46:6 Ascéndit Deus in iúbilo: * et Dóminus in voce tubæ.
d1c849b4d37b3ab41280.english: 46:6 God is ascended with jubilee, * and the Lord with the sound of trumpet.

34daed721519365e5d74.latin: 46:7 Psállite Deo nostro, psállite: * psállite Regi nostro, psállite.
34daed721519365e5d74.english: 46:7 Sing praises to our God, sing ye: * sing praises to our king, sing ye.

824773529d87d3eeb425.latin: 46:8 Quóniam Rex omnis terræ Deus: * psállite sapiénter.
824773529d87d3eeb425.english: 46:8 For God is the king of all the earth: * sing ye wisely.

434bca4f163e2002b9f8.latin: 46:9 Regnábit Deus super gentes: * Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam.
434bca4f163e2002b9f8.english: 46:9 God shall reign over the nations: * God sitteth on his holy throne.

c674d3bc4db754f502ff.latin: 46:10 Príncipes populórum congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham: * quóniam dii fortes terræ veheménter eleváti sunt.
c674d3bc4db754f502ff.english: 46:10 The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham: * for the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted.

2d0fa9551b11966ffeb8.english: Ant. God is our help in trouble.

d147f118636cf05baa3b.latin: Ant. Magnus Dóminus * et laudábilis nimis. ‡
d147f118636cf05baa3b.english: Ant. Great is the Lord, * and greatly to be praised.

e4b89e0083234f15e93b.latin: 47:2 Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis * ‡ in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto eius.
e4b89e0083234f15e93b.english: 47:2 Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised * in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.

8df900a900fa5c68704c.latin: 47:3 Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
8df900a900fa5c68704c.english: 47:3 With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, * on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.

0b4ad4f09501970a6b67.latin: 47:4 Deus in dómibus eius cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.
0b4ad4f09501970a6b67.english: 47:4 In her houses shall God be known, * when he shall protect her.

f918fc90d9f8a8eb6f21.latin: 47:5 Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.
f918fc90d9f8a8eb6f21.english: 47:5 For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: * they gathered together.

7bd8978fe8e61f7c9c71.latin: 47:6 Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.
7bd8978fe8e61f7c9c71.english: 47:6 So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: * trembling took hold of them.

9a3c46b0b403edcc545d.latin: 47:7 Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
9a3c46b0b403edcc545d.english: 47:7 There were pains as of a woman in labour; * with a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

c3e1c06e606d0f165827.latin: 47:9 Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
c3e1c06e606d0f165827.english: 47:9 As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: * God hath founded it for ever.

ee52b2e9005b01cf3761.latin: 47:10 Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.
ee52b2e9005b01cf3761.english: 47:10 We have received thy mercy, O God, * in the midst of thy temple.

c7dc08fc67b77945f5c3.latin: 47:11 Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * iustítia plena est déxtera tua.
c7dc08fc67b77945f5c3.english: 47:11 According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: * thy right hand is full of justice.

79c9c861afeb2077837b.latin: 47:12 Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Iudæ: * propter iudícia tua, Dómine.
79c9c861afeb2077837b.english: 47:12 Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

6be88e8a9ca2fc11a480.latin: 47:13 Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus eius.
6be88e8a9ca2fc11a480.english: 47:13 Surround Sion, and encompass her: * tell ye in her towers.

15f2efb07c1f1479b01e.latin: 47:14 Pónite corda vestra in virtúte eius: * et distribúite domos eius, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
15f2efb07c1f1479b01e.english: 47:14 Set your hearts on her strength; and distribute her houses, * that ye may relate it in another generation.

b525edcd450d8b241223.latin: 47:15 Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi: * ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
b525edcd450d8b241223.english: 47:15 For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: * he shall rule us for evermore.

c5f4174061bd95de3db8.latin: 48:2 Audíte hæc, omnes gentes: * áuribus percípite omnes, qui habitátis orbem:
c5f4174061bd95de3db8.english: 48:2 Hear these things, all ye nations: * give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.

e81046f51c86d8dc0323.latin: 48:3 Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum: * simul in unum dives et pauper.
e81046f51c86d8dc0323.english: 48:3 All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: * both rich and poor together.

363c0602af88e4b30267.latin: 48:4 Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: * et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
363c0602af88e4b30267.english: 48:4 My mouth shall speak wisdom: * and the meditation of my heart understanding.

1b52ba1fb5f5067c76f3.latin: 48:5 Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam: * apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.
1b52ba1fb5f5067c76f3.english: 48:5 I will incline my ear to a parable; * I will open my proposition on the psaltery.

fd14d798ecf228df5996.latin: 48:6 Cur timébo in die mala? * iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me:
fd14d798ecf228df5996.english: 48:6 Why shall I fear in the evil day? * the iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.

47bf77085752420696b8.latin: 48:7 Qui confídunt in virtúte sua: * et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.
47bf77085752420696b8.english: 48:7 They that trust in their own strength, * and glory in the multitude of their riches,

06cb67360320076b94e8.latin: 48:8 Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo: * non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.
06cb67360320076b94e8.english: 48:8 No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: * he shall not give to God his ransom,

0f0ccfaa1421a8dd43c8.latin: 48:9 Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ: * et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.
0f0ccfaa1421a8dd43c8.english: 48:9 Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: * and shall labour for ever, and shall still live unto the end.

81280e60b949d4359ad4.latin: 48:11 Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes: * simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt.
81280e60b949d4359ad4.english: 48:11 He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: * the senseless and the fool shall perish together:

921377d859bdb80ef318.latin: 48:11 Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas: * et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.
921377d859bdb80ef318.english: 48:11 And they shall leave their riches to strangers: * and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever.

7bbaf0450b6b7d4f1491.latin: 48:12 Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie: * vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.
7bbaf0450b6b7d4f1491.english: 48:12 Their dwelling places to all generations: * they have called their lands by their names.

8457274f8fc66bf451e1.latin: 48:13 Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
8457274f8fc66bf451e1.english: 48:13 And man when he was in honour did not understand; * he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.

7f0a06893aa2d0b95fb2.latin: 48:14 Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis: * et póstea in ore suo complacébunt.
7f0a06893aa2d0b95fb2.english: 48:14 This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them: * and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.

fbefa384e25bfe42b7ee.latin: 48:15 Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt: * mors depáscet eos.
fbefa384e25bfe42b7ee.english: 48:15 They are laid in hell like sheep: * death shall feed upon them.

21be140e0fa2f6f091da.latin: 48:15 Et dominabúntur eórum iusti in matutíno: * et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.
21be140e0fa2f6f091da.english: 48:15 And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning; * and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.

446f3f815a9c0c220892.latin: 48:16 Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi: * cum accéperit me.
446f3f815a9c0c220892.english: 48:16 But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, * when he shall receive me.

c56f168075b88861020c.latin: 48:17 Ne timúeris, cum dives factus fúerit homo: * et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus eius.
c56f168075b88861020c.english: 48:17 Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich, * and when the glory of his house shall be increased.

b52a7c85fc51d48b400d.latin: 48:18 Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia: * neque descéndet cum eo glória eius.
b52a7c85fc51d48b400d.english: 48:18 For when he shall die he shall take nothing away; * nor shall his glory descend with him.

daa05e5fd345bc5d7076.latin: 48:19 Quia ánima eius in vita ipsíus benedicétur: * confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.
daa05e5fd345bc5d7076.english: 48:19 For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: * and he will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him.

570ab48dfec669949df4.latin: 48:20 Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum: * et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.
570ab48dfec669949df4.english: 48:20 He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: * and he shall never see light.

89c4bacad33ddefbe776.latin: 48:21 Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
89c4bacad33ddefbe776.english: 48:21 Man when he was in honour did not understand: * he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.

a22bdef24ca60b779d17.latin: Ant. Magnus Dóminus et laudábilis nimis.
a22bdef24ca60b779d17.english: Ant. Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised.

0e502ebc95ee25a19c11.latin: Ant. Deus deórum * Dóminus locútus est. ‡
0e502ebc95ee25a19c11.english: Ant. The God of gods * the Lord hath spoken. ‡

3a07fe3b1d570d7f192f.latin: 49:1 Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est: * ‡ et vocávit terram,
3a07fe3b1d570d7f192f.english: 49:1 The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: * ‡ and he hath called the earth.

c71fe77b19d835f9fd17.latin: 49:1 A solis ortu usque ad occásum: * ex Sion spécies decóris eius.
c71fe77b19d835f9fd17.english: 49:1 From the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof: * out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty.

62e33f7b2d9038a6e926.latin: 49:3 Deus maniféste véniet: * Deus noster et non silébit.
62e33f7b2d9038a6e926.english: 49:3 God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, * and shall not keep silence.

2229fbab20465ee28231.latin: 49:3 Ignis in conspéctu eius exardéscet: * et in circúitu eius tempéstas válida.
2229fbab20465ee28231.english: 49:3 A fire shall burn before him: * and a mighty tempest shall be round about.

22f545ea7d964adba6f2.latin: 49:4 Advocábit cælum desúrsum: * et terram discérnere pópulum suum.
22f545ea7d964adba6f2.english: 49:4 He shall call heaven from above, * and the earth, to judge his people.

3c84c84f691336ca317e.latin: 49:5 Congregáte illi sanctos eius: * qui órdinant testaméntum eius super sacrifícia.
3c84c84f691336ca317e.english: 49:5 Gather ye together his saints to him: * who set his covenant before sacrifices.

7dc0eca8497b6d89b1a8.latin: 49:6 Et annuntiábunt cæli iustítiam eius: * quóniam Deus iudex est.
7dc0eca8497b6d89b1a8.english: 49:6 And the heavens shall declare his justice: * for God is judge.

d601e393709dc5e180e1.latin: 49:7 Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar: Israël, et testificábor tibi: * Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.
d601e393709dc5e180e1.english: 49:7 Hear, O my people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: * I am God, thy God.

b509d202e95c60eb2745.latin: 49:8 Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te: * holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.
b509d202e95c60eb2745.english: 49:8 I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: * and thy burnt offerings are always in my sight.

b7fe7eebcaaa025f512d.latin: 49:9 Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos: * neque de grégibus tuis hircos.
b7fe7eebcaaa025f512d.english: 49:9 I will not take calves out of thy house: * nor he goats out of thy flocks.

5e248654b3e19baa445d.latin: 49:10 Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum: * iuménta in móntibus et boves.
5e248654b3e19baa445d.english: 49:10 For all the beasts of the woods are mine: * the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.

309d454e631b6d2d1899.latin: 49:11 Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli: * et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.
309d454e631b6d2d1899.english: 49:11 I know all the fowls of the air: * and with me is the beauty of the field.

37f011f389b0f808ae9c.latin: 49:12 Si esuríero, non dicam tibi: * meus est enim orbis terræ, et plenitúdo eius.
37f011f389b0f808ae9c.english: 49:12 If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: * for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.

9057d7580d56082770ac.latin: 49:13 Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum? * aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?
9057d7580d56082770ac.english: 49:13 Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? * or shall I drink the blood of goats?

fa0cedda6eddd2d7ccff.latin: 49:14 Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis: * et redde Altíssimo vota tua.
fa0cedda6eddd2d7ccff.english: 49:14 Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: * and pay thy vows to the most High.

281dfaea73efc481315b.latin: 49:15 Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis: * éruam te, et honorificábis me.
281dfaea73efc481315b.english: 49:15 And call upon me in the day of trouble: * I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.

06586dfb73e3d3e0646d.latin: 49:16 Peccatóri autem dixit Deus: * Quare tu enárras iustítias meas, et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum?
06586dfb73e3d3e0646d.english: 49:16 But to the sinner God hath said: * Why dost thou declare my justices, and take my covenant in thy mouth?

5c71d8bfaaef9bb19480.latin: 49:17 Tu vero odísti disciplínam: * et proiecísti sermónes meos retrórsum:
5c71d8bfaaef9bb19480.english: 49:17 Seeing thou hast hated discipline: * and hast cast my words behind thee.

d48564d199da75b7be40.latin: 49:18 Si vidébas furem, currébas cum eo: * et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas.
d48564d199da75b7be40.english: 49:18 If thou didst see a thief thou didst run with him: * and with adulterers thou hast been a partaker.

f1a1b4bfb2980018a7ba.latin: 49:19 Os tuum abundávit malítia: * et lingua tua concinnábat dolos.
f1a1b4bfb2980018a7ba.english: 49:19 Thy mouth hath abounded with evil, * and thy tongue framed deceits.

bf7a55b16fa4c17be059.latin: 49:20 Sedens advérsus fratrem tuum loquebáris, et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum: * hæc fecísti, et tácui.
bf7a55b16fa4c17be059.english: 49:20 Sitting thou didst speak against thy brother, and didst lay a scandal against thy mother’s son: * these things hast thou done, and I was silent.

3c27ae3d11efcd9aa612.latin: 49:21 Existimásti, iníque, quod ero tui símilis: * árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam.
3c27ae3d11efcd9aa612.english: 49:21 Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: * but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.

defa81f52af3bf80449b.latin: 49:22 Intellégite hæc, qui obliviscímini Deum: * nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat.
defa81f52af3bf80449b.english: 49:22 Understand these things, you that forget God; * lest he snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.

5ed1bc144d944020cb03.latin: 49:23 Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me: * et illic iter, quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei.
5ed1bc144d944020cb03.english: 49:23 The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: * and there is the way by which I will shew him the salvation of God.

bcd949c0ff5948db7d16.latin: 51:3 Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?
bcd949c0ff5948db7d16.english: 51:3 Why dost thou glory in malice, * thou that art mighty in iniquity?

33d3c874afdd2460e9d8.latin: 51:4 Tota die iniustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
33d3c874afdd2460e9d8.english: 51:4 All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: * as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.

dc79dc4bda26f7affe30.latin: 51:5 Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
dc79dc4bda26f7affe30.english: 51:5 Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: * and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.

5f4c8a1e1752104946c3.latin: 51:6 Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.
5f4c8a1e1752104946c3.english: 51:6 Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, * O deceitful tongue.

782f92274323232490af.latin: 51:7 Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
782f92274323232490af.english: 51:7 Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: * he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.

40bc1d63d203f8c7e8fd.latin: 51:8 Vidébunt iusti, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adiutórem suum:
40bc1d63d203f8c7e8fd.english: 51:8 The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say: * Behold the man that made not God his helper:

cf13b24649cd66b0718d.latin: 51:9 Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
cf13b24649cd66b0718d.english: 51:9 But trusted in the abundance of his riches: * and prevailed in his vanity.

015d0dce8683e947670c.latin: 51:10 Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.
015d0dce8683e947670c.english: 51:10 But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, * have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever.

462d584bc4fc6f9525f3.latin: 51:11 Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
462d584bc4fc6f9525f3.english: 51:11 I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: * and I will wait on thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.

612142a10d2c9aed4566.latin: Ant. Deus deórum Dóminus locútus est.
612142a10d2c9aed4566.english: Ant. The God of gods the Lord hath spoken.

498b1cfe384d897e44fa.english: ℣. Offer to God the sacrifice of praise.

ce4d5ecdd4f423d10650.english: ℟. And pay thy vows to the most High.

93af104868bc762dc7f0.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. A cunctis vítiis et peccátis absólvat nos virtus sanctæ Trinitátis.
℟. Amen.
Lectio brevis
Prov 3:19-20
Dóminus sapiéntia fundávit terram: stabilívit cælos prudéntia. Sapiéntia illíus erupérunt abýssi, et nubes rore concréscunt.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟.br. Deus, in nómine tuo * Salvum me fac.
℟. Deus, in nómine tuo * Salvum me fac.
℣. Et in misericórdia tua líbera me.
℟. Salvum me fac.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Deus, in nómine tuo * Salvum me fac.
93af104868bc762dc7f0.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. Of all faults and sins may the power of the holy Trinity absolve us.
℟. Amen.
Short reading
Prov 3:19-20
The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth, hath established the heavens by prudence. By his wisdom the depths have broken out, and the clouds grow thick with dew.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟.br. Save me, O God, * by thy name.
℟. Save me, O God, * by thy name.
℣. And deliver me in your mercy.
℟. Save me, O God.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟.br. Save me, O God, by thy name.

fab7c431541863ca0830.latin: 52:1 Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.
fab7c431541863ca0830.english: 52:1 The fool said in his heart: * There is no God.

6e148363935b74964eff.latin: 52:2 Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.
6e148363935b74964eff.english: 52:2 They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: * there is none that doth good.

1a3e84cae53c0e3d3573.latin: 52:3 Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
1a3e84cae53c0e3d3573.english: 52:3 God looked down from heaven on the children of men: * to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God.

16b23964fc011e00cd9e.latin: 52:4 Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
16b23964fc011e00cd9e.english: 52:4 All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together, * there is none that doth good, no not one.

bfc88fefaf0e38a5d01a.latin: 52:5 Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?
bfc88fefaf0e38a5d01a.english: 52:5 Shall not all the workers of iniquity know, * who eat up my people as they eat bread?

351446b9658e8779d577.latin: 52:6 Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
351446b9658e8779d577.english: 52:6 They have not called upon God: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.

ad0e79a161472ed34618.latin: 52:6 Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.
ad0e79a161472ed34618.english: 52:6 For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men: * they have been confounded, because God hath despised them.

5530b919ec12b70a55e4.latin: 52:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.
5530b919ec12b70a55e4.english: 52:7 Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

5a7bb4ded0787d0faa9a.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
5a7bb4ded0787d0faa9a.english: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

3db89ba4e310d4acf349.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
3db89ba4e310d4acf349.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

2979ba6caaa76b965cea.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
2979ba6caaa76b965cea.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

4f3af38f29543656df9f.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
4f3af38f29543656df9f.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

f3810e46152394c1803d.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
f3810e46152394c1803d.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

0a63c52087a10305376e.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
0a63c52087a10305376e.english: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

b14d12a9c8a6a4aaffe2.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
b14d12a9c8a6a4aaffe2.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

cf19bc2896821e90d96c.latin: 54:2 Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam, et ne despéxeris deprecatiónem meam: * inténde mihi, et exáudi me.
cf19bc2896821e90d96c.english: 54:2 Hear, O God, my prayer, and despise not my supplication: * be attentive to me and hear me.

0711bbd7d13241e7ef9d.latin: 54:3 Contristátus sum in exercitatióne mea: * et conturbátus sum a voce inimíci, et a tribulatióne peccatóris.
0711bbd7d13241e7ef9d.english: 54:3 I am grieved in my exercise; * and am troubled, at the voice of the enemy, and at the tribulation of the sinner.

1d1f6722d5dd705556f9.latin: 54:4 Quóniam declinavérunt in me iniquitátes: * et in ira molésti erant mihi.
1d1f6722d5dd705556f9.english: 54:4 For they have cast iniquities upon me; * and in wrath they were troublesome to me.

e5938455912af92a4eb4.latin: 54:5 Cor meum conturbátum est in me: * et formído mortis cécidit super me.
e5938455912af92a4eb4.english: 54:5 My heart is troubled within me: * and the fear of death is fallen upon me.

9a974f918ec7227a0b7c.latin: 54:6 Timor et tremor venérunt super me: * et contexérunt me ténebræ.
9a974f918ec7227a0b7c.english: 54:6 Fear and trembling are come upon me: * and darkness hath covered me.

84296ef2dcdc302e35d3.latin: 54:7 Et dixi: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ, * et volábo, et requiéscam?
84296ef2dcdc302e35d3.english: 54:7 And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, * and I will fly and be at rest?

1907d777312b1367ee2f.latin: 54:8 Ecce, elongávi fúgiens: * et mansi in solitúdine.
1907d777312b1367ee2f.english: 54:8 Lo, I have gone far off flying away; * and I abode in the wilderness.

4c43837a8d35d6129fc9.latin: 54:9 Exspectábam eum, qui salvum me fecit * a pusillanimitáte spíritus et tempestáte.
4c43837a8d35d6129fc9.english: 54:9 I waited for him that hath saved me * from pusillanimity of spirit, and a storm.

e87f72a11d6bab5cc0a5.latin: 54:10 Præcípita, Dómine, dívide linguas eórum: * quóniam vidi iniquitátem, et contradictiónem in civitáte.
e87f72a11d6bab5cc0a5.english: 54:10 Cast down, O Lord, and divide their tongues; * for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city.

754959534148ff74c1c9.latin: 54:11 Die ac nocte circúmdabit eam super muros eius iníquitas: * et labor in médio eius, et iniustítia.
754959534148ff74c1c9.english: 54:11 Day and night shall iniquity surround it upon its walls: * and in the midst thereof are labour, and injustice.

477e15516e1eea7bbb57.latin: 54:12 Et non defécit de platéis eius * usúra, et dolus.
477e15516e1eea7bbb57.english: 54:12 And usury and deceit * have not departed from its streets.

81a2986d804f6c6313ab.latin: 54:13 Quóniam si inimícus meus maledixísset mihi, * sustinuíssem útique.
81a2986d804f6c6313ab.english: 54:13 For if my enemy had reviled me, * I would verily have borne with it.

43a1926f7f8666596bc8.latin: 54:13 Et si is, qui óderat me, super me magna locútus fuísset, * abscondíssem me fórsitan ab eo.
43a1926f7f8666596bc8.english: 54:13 And if he that hated me had spoken great things against me, * I would perhaps have hidden myself from him.

46131bc851182d598eb3.latin: 54:14 Tu vero, homo unánimis: * dux meus, et notus meus:
46131bc851182d598eb3.english: 54:14 But thou a man of one mind, * my guide, and my familiar.

a1872773a39791094d7d.latin: 54:15 Qui simul mecum dulces capiébas cibos: * in domo Dei ambulávimus cum consénsu.
a1872773a39791094d7d.english: 54:15 Who didst take sweetmeats together with me: * in the house of God we walked with consent.

2a403aa7134edcf0ccc5.latin: 54:16 Véniat mors super illos: * et descéndant in inférnum vivéntes:
2a403aa7134edcf0ccc5.english: 54:16 Let death come upon them, * and let them go down alive into hell.

a3485b0180ff543ddadd.latin: 54:16 Quóniam nequítiæ in habitáculis eórum: * in médio eórum.
a3485b0180ff543ddadd.english: 54:16 For there is wickedness in their dwellings: * in the midst of them.

70355ea2be26ab2d481f.latin: 54:17 Ego autem ad Deum clamávi: * et Dóminus salvábit me.
70355ea2be26ab2d481f.english: 54:17 But I have cried to God: * and the Lord will save me.

45120981049485d8b053.latin: 54:18 Véspere, et mane, et merídie narrábo et annuntiábo: * et exáudiet vocem meam.
45120981049485d8b053.english: 54:18 Evening and morning, and at noon I will speak and declare: * and he shall hear my voice.

8dbb46a6d8cbd7087192.latin: 54:19 Rédimet in pace ánimam meam ab his, qui appropínquant mihi: * quóniam inter multos erant mecum.
8dbb46a6d8cbd7087192.english: 54:19 He shall redeem my soul in peace from them that draw near to me: * for among many they were with me.

5d119cb0510c75e1977d.latin: 54:20 Exáudiet Deus, et humiliábit illos, * qui est ante sǽcula.
5d119cb0510c75e1977d.english: 54:20 God shall hear, * and the Eternal shall humble them.

a6d9f156a4271f6d676f.latin: 54:20 Non enim est illis commutátio, et non timuérunt Deum: * exténdit manum suam in retribuéndo.
a6d9f156a4271f6d676f.english: 54:20 For there is no change with them, and they have not feared God: * he hath stretched forth his hand to repay.

0fb3c82dc9bb714869ae.latin: 54:21 Contaminavérunt testaméntum eius, divísi sunt ab ira vultus eius: * et appropinquávit cor illíus.
0fb3c82dc9bb714869ae.english: 54:21 They have defiled his covenant, they are divided by the wrath of his countenance, * and his heart hath drawn near.

7c9557fb042a4502c87c.latin: 54:22 Mollíti sunt sermónes eius super óleum: * et ipsi sunt iácula.
7c9557fb042a4502c87c.english: 54:22 His words are smoother than oil, * and the same are darts.

6af527483baab3763746.latin: 54:23 Iacta super Dóminum curam tuam, et ipse te enútriet: * non dabit in ætérnum fluctuatiónem iusto.
6af527483baab3763746.english: 54:23 Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: * he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever.

d46c9b90877fd217522c.latin: 54:24 Tu vero, Deus, dedúces eos, * in púteum intéritus.
d46c9b90877fd217522c.english: 54:24 But thou, O God, shalt bring them down * into the pit of destruction.

4e8430f4b64513dea50c.latin: 54:24 Viri sánguinum, et dolósi non dimidiábunt dies suos: * ego autem sperábo in te, Dómine.
4e8430f4b64513dea50c.english: 54:24 Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; * but I will trust in thee, O Lord.

4c61967aee1657a67050.latin: 55:2 Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.
4c61967aee1657a67050.english: 55:2 Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot; * all the day long he hath afflicted me fighting against me.

fbeef1d2fc8f9a791feb.latin: 55:3 Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.
fbeef1d2fc8f9a791feb.english: 55:3 My enemies have trodden on me all the day long; * for they are many that make war against me.

ff65032d928df38b9e4a.latin: 55:4 Ab altitúdine diéi timébo: * ego vero in te sperábo.
ff65032d928df38b9e4a.english: 55:4 From the height of the day I shall fear: * but I will trust in thee.

920e9e8713867362215e.latin: 55:5 In Deo laudábo sermónes meos, in Deo sperávi: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro.
920e9e8713867362215e.english: 55:5 In God I will praise my words, in God I have put my trust: * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.

d13a2ffdf7b121e93a8f.latin: 55:6 Tota die verba mea exsecrabántur: * advérsum me omnes cogitatiónes eórum in malum.
d13a2ffdf7b121e93a8f.english: 55:6 All the day long they detested my words: * all their thoughts were against me unto evil.

c9882aed684144424067.latin: 55:7 Inhabitábunt et abscóndent: * ipsi calcáneum meum observábunt.
c9882aed684144424067.english: 55:7 They will dwell and hide themselves: * they will watch my heel.

cc0a8d2b12f38c019e74.latin: 55:8 Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam, pro níhilo salvos fácies illos: * in ira pópulos confrínges.
cc0a8d2b12f38c019e74.english: 55:8 As they have waited for my soul, for nothing shalt thou save them: * in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces.

c39a40f89b84e0896b3a.latin: 55:9 Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi: * posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
c39a40f89b84e0896b3a.english: 55:9 O God, I have declared to thee my life: * thou hast set my tears in thy sight,

9948b3295f3e6202d770.latin: 55:9 Sicut et in promissióne tua: * tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum:
9948b3295f3e6202d770.english: 55:9 As also in thy promise. * Then shall my enemies be turned back.

3ba03287a2f54bb9f4f4.latin: 55:10 In quacúmque die invocávero te: * ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es.
3ba03287a2f54bb9f4f4.english: 55:10 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * behold I know thou art my God.

b1fc662f17c01940595e.latin: 55:11 In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem: * in Deo sperávi, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
b1fc662f17c01940595e.english: 55:11 In God will I praise the word, in the Lord will I praise his speech. * In God have I hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me.

d6d36991967e8fb66ce4.latin: 55:12 In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, * quæ reddam, laudatiónes tibi.
d6d36991967e8fb66ce4.english: 55:12 In me, O God, are vows to thee, * which I will pay, praises to thee:

f0667241a97a2b459563.latin: 55:13 Quóniam eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu: * ut pláceam coram Deo in lúmine vivéntium.
f0667241a97a2b459563.english: 55:13 Because thou hast delivered my soul from death, my feet from falling: * that I may please in the sight of God, in the light of the living.

b870a41d848f1d658edb.latin: 57:2 Si vere útique iustítiam loquímini: * recta iudicáte, fílii hóminum.
b870a41d848f1d658edb.english: 57:2 If in very deed you speak justice: * judge right things, ye sons of men.

27de371e930cb9b79984.latin: 57:3 Étenim in corde iniquitátes operámini: * in terra iniustítias manus vestræ concínnant.
27de371e930cb9b79984.english: 57:3 For in your heart you work iniquity: * your hands forge injustice in the earth.

9cbe8c6d62ea7b7e080b.latin: 57:4 Alienáti sunt peccatóres a vulva, erravérunt ab útero: * locúti sunt falsa.
9cbe8c6d62ea7b7e080b.english: 57:4 The wicked are alienated from the womb; they have gone astray from the womb: * they have spoken false things.

69f3b6e7a796a77984a0.latin: 57:5 Furor illis secúndum similitúdinem serpéntis: * sicut áspidis surdæ, et obturántis aures suas,
69f3b6e7a796a77984a0.english: 57:5 Their madness is according to the likeness of a serpent: * like the deaf asp that stoppeth her ears:

b1681d27d42ff1a1c519.latin: 57:6 Quæ non exáudiet vocem incantántium: * et venéfici incantántis sapiénter.
b1681d27d42ff1a1c519.english: 57:6 Which will not hear the voice of the charmers; * nor of the wizard that charmeth wisely.

4ecca1ddcf8d9c2e500d.latin: 57:7 Deus cónteret dentes eórum in ore ipsórum: * molas leónum confrínget Dóminus.
4ecca1ddcf8d9c2e500d.english: 57:7 God shall break in pieces their teeth in their mouth: * the Lord shall break the grinders of the lions.

b82e63b9f786d96a0a18.latin: 57:8 Ad níhilum devénient tamquam aqua decúrrens: * inténdit arcum suum donec infirméntur.
b82e63b9f786d96a0a18.english: 57:8 They shall come to nothing, like water running down; * he hath bent his bow till they be weakened.

44105de3aede64666710.latin: 57:9 Sicut cera, quæ fluit, auferéntur: * supercécidit ignis, et non vidérunt solem.
44105de3aede64666710.english: 57:9 Like wax that melteth they shall be taken away: * fire hath fallen on them, and they shall not see the sun.

5bc9beb1e5eccdf0aae9.latin: 57:10 Priúsquam intellégerent spinæ vestræ rhamnum: * sicut vivéntes, sic in ira absórbet eos.
5bc9beb1e5eccdf0aae9.english: 57:10 Before your thorns could know the brier; he swalloweth them up, * as alive, in his wrath.

575171f6d1b1383a0c48.latin: 57:11 Lætábitur iustus cum víderit vindíctam: * manus suas lavábit in sánguine peccatóris.
575171f6d1b1383a0c48.english: 57:11 The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge: * he shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner.

63d90f6ab8fea7f4d527.latin: 57:12 Et dicet homo: Si útique est fructus iusto: * útique est Deus iúdicans eos in terra.
63d90f6ab8fea7f4d527.english: 57:12 And man shall say: If indeed there be fruit to the just: * there is indeed a God that judgeth them on the earth.

324afa7ef9a06aec41ab.latin: 58:2 Éripe me de inimícis meis, Deus meus: * et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.
324afa7ef9a06aec41ab.english: 58:2 Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; * and defend me from them that rise up against me.

aeac393eaedb6bd622e2.latin: 58:3 Éripe me de operántibus iniquitátem: * et de viris sánguinum salva me.
aeac393eaedb6bd622e2.english: 58:3 Deliver me from them that work iniquity, * and save me from bloody men.

6913eac296c01848969c.latin: 58:4 Quia ecce cepérunt ánimam meam: * irruérunt in me fortes.
6913eac296c01848969c.english: 58:4 For behold they have caught my soul: * the mighty have rushed in upon me:

e79b7abbe8a5257a257a.latin: 58:5 Neque iníquitas mea, neque peccátum meum, Dómine: * sine iniquitáte cucúrri, et diréxi.
e79b7abbe8a5257a257a.english: 58:5 Neither is it my iniquity, nor my sin, O Lord: * without iniquity have I run, and directed my steps.

c00710abcec717fff160.latin: 58:6 Exsúrge in occúrsum meum, et vide: * et tu, Dómine, Deus virtútum, Deus Israël,
c00710abcec717fff160.english: 58:6 Rise up thou to meet me, and behold: * even thou, O Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel.

cf4e3830d4bdb5bc554a.latin: 58:6 Inténde ad visitándas omnes gentes: * non misereáris ómnibus, qui operántur iniquitátem.
cf4e3830d4bdb5bc554a.english: 58:6 Attend to visit all the nations: * have no mercy on all them that work iniquity.

00e98a0d3fbbc87cb380.latin: 58:7 Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, * et circuíbunt civitátem.
00e98a0d3fbbc87cb380.english: 58:7 They shall return at evening, and shall suffer hunger like dogs: * and shall go round about the city.

c471e321ee17212f4e2d.latin: 58:8 Ecce, loquéntur in ore suo, et gládius in lábiis eórum: * quóniam quis audívit?
c471e321ee17212f4e2d.english: 58:8 Behold they shall speak with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips: * for who, say they, hath heard us?

e7f39eba0f618da6f360.latin: 58:9 Et tu, Dómine, deridébis eos: * ad níhilum dedúces omnes gentes.
e7f39eba0f618da6f360.english: 58:9 But thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them: * thou shalt bring all the nations to nothing.

e60ebdae3f53b2274a28.latin: 58:10 Fortitúdinem meam ad te custódiam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: * Deus meus, misericórdia eius prævéniet me.
e60ebdae3f53b2274a28.english: 58:10 I will keep my strength to thee: for thou art my protector: * my God, his mercy shall prevent me.

3fe0aa34782961d7c0f1.latin: 58:12 Deus osténdet mihi super inimícos meos, ne occídas eos: * nequándo obliviscántur pópuli mei.
3fe0aa34782961d7c0f1.english: 58:12 God shall let me see over my enemies: slay them not, * lest at any time my people forget.

88973f63cf3c04d1141c.latin: 58:12 Dispérge illos in virtúte tua: * et depóne eos, protéctor meus, Dómine:
88973f63cf3c04d1141c.english: 58:12 And scatter them by thy power; * and bring them down, O Lord, my protector:

a8f144e35e420b2969ea.latin: 58:13 Delíctum oris eórum, sermónem labiórum ipsórum: * et comprehendántur in supérbia sua.
a8f144e35e420b2969ea.english: 58:13 For the sin of their mouth, and the word of their lips: * and let them be taken in their pride.

cb841e268c9d174c2aba.latin: 58:13 Et de exsecratióne et mendácio annuntiabúntur in consummatióne: * in ira consummatiónis, et non erunt.
cb841e268c9d174c2aba.english: 58:13 And for their cursing and lying they shall be talked of, when they are consumed: * when they are consumed by thy wrath, and they shall be no more.

0806eeed2ee63f3dc143.latin: 58:14 Et scient quia Deus dominábitur Iacob: * et fínium terræ.
0806eeed2ee63f3dc143.english: 58:14 And they shall know that God will rule Jacob, * and all the ends of the earth.

07719f5d603c2da05a41.latin: 58:15 Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, * et circuíbunt civitátem.
07719f5d603c2da05a41.english: 58:15 They shall return at evening and shall suffer hunger like dogs: * and shall go round about the city.

d4194f49043c1b4ba4d4.latin: 58:16 Ipsi dispergéntur ad manducándum: * si vero non fúerint saturáti, et murmurábunt.
d4194f49043c1b4ba4d4.english: 58:16 They shall be scattered abroad to eat, * and shall murmur if they be not filled.

9bec46683e04dac00bdd.latin: 58:17 Ego autem cantábo fortitúdinem tuam: * et exsultábo mane misericórdiam tuam.
9bec46683e04dac00bdd.english: 58:17 But I will sing thy strength: * and will extol thy mercy in the morning.

14a0d27d8b871da10a26.latin: 58:17 Quia factus es suscéptor meus, * et refúgium meum, in die tribulatiónis meæ.
14a0d27d8b871da10a26.english: 58:17 For thou art become my support, * and my refuge, in the day of my trouble.

c67adf9937ffd553365e.latin: 58:18 Adiútor meus, tibi psallam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: * Deus meus, misericórdia mea.
c67adf9937ffd553365e.english: 58:18 Unto thee, O my helper, will I sing, for thou art God my defence: * my God my mercy.

4bb0c4aa537f24cda0f4.latin:
1 Cor 16:13-14
Vigiláte, state in fide, viríliter ágite, et confortámini. Ómnia vestra in caritáte fiant.
℟. Deo grátias.
℣. Beáti qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine.
℟. In sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.
4bb0c4aa537f24cda0f4.english:
1 Cor 16:13-14
Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, do manfully, and be strengthened. Let all your things be done in charity.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℣. Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord:
℟. They shall praise thee for ever and ever.

9215b207c6b7d0050f5d.english: Ant. Blot out, O Lord my iniquity.

a55c44a35175444d70f5.english: Ant. The salvation of my countenance * and my God.

d1c99c1d7e52a9174b92.latin: 42:1 Iúdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta, * ab hómine iníquo, et dolóso érue me.
d1c99c1d7e52a9174b92.english: 42:1 Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy: * deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

a064e4ae6177037e58e8.latin: 42:2 Quia tu es, Deus, fortitúdo mea: * quare me repulísti? et quare tristis incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
a064e4ae6177037e58e8.english: 42:2 For thou art God my strength: * why hast thou cast me off? and why do I go sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?

14a4200faead5bf32dc2.latin: 42:3 Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam: * ipsa me deduxérunt, et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum, et in tabernácula tua.
14a4200faead5bf32dc2.english: 42:3 Send forth thy light and thy truth: * they have conducted me, and brought me unto thy holy hill, and into thy tabernacles.

74f0b961f95fc0b186f1.latin: 42:4 Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: * ad Deum, qui lætíficat iuventútem meam.
74f0b961f95fc0b186f1.english: 42:4 And I will go in to the altar of God: * to God who giveth joy to my youth.

be81f173da5fec343fdb.latin: 42:5 Confitébor tibi in cíthara, Deus, Deus meus: * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
be81f173da5fec343fdb.english: 42:5 To thee, O God my God, I will give praise upon the harp: * why art thou sad, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

269c9bb63c91e808d2f1.latin: 42:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
269c9bb63c91e808d2f1.english: 42:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

0ee54ef749e661234632.latin: Ant. Salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
0ee54ef749e661234632.english: Ant. The salvation of my countenance and my God.

4e32a8266ca8a51b4fba.latin: Ant. Quóniam * in te confídit ánima mea.
4e32a8266ca8a51b4fba.english: Ant. For in thee * my soul trusteth.

11e1c6f9dc275eeab54d.latin: 56:2 Miserére mei, Deus, miserére mei: * quóniam in te confídit ánima mea.
11e1c6f9dc275eeab54d.english: 56:2 Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me: * for my soul trusteth in thee.

df35fbe706528b8a054d.latin: 56:2 Et in umbra alárum tuárum sperábo, * donec tránseat iníquitas.
df35fbe706528b8a054d.english: 56:2 And in the shadow of thy wings will I hope, * until iniquity pass away.

387c95c4230b24d47434.latin: 56:3 Clamábo ad Deum altíssimum: * Deum qui benefécit mihi.
387c95c4230b24d47434.english: 56:3 I will cry to God the most High; * to God who hath done good to me.

ebef09a9ba734ceb7d5f.latin: 56:4 Misit de cælo, et liberávit me: * dedit in oppróbrium conculcántes me.
ebef09a9ba734ceb7d5f.english: 56:4 He hath sent from heaven and delivered me: * he hath made them a reproach that trod upon me.

4362d4389117d113f1fe.latin: 56:4 Misit Deus misericórdiam suam, et veritátem suam, * et erípuit ánimam meam de médio catulórum leónum: dormívi conturbátus.
4362d4389117d113f1fe.english: 56:4 God hath sent his mercy and his truth, * and he hath delivered my soul from the midst of the young lions. I slept troubled.

fb2c99a38646c9c34ae1.latin: 56:5 Fílii hóminum dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: * et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
fb2c99a38646c9c34ae1.english: 56:5 The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons and arrows, * and their tongue a sharp sword.

8d45f6cc197ef54ed986.latin: 56:6 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, * et in omnem terram glória tua.
8d45f6cc197ef54ed986.english: 56:6 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, * and thy glory above all the earth.

fa24e09117bacc77ad14.latin: 56:7 Láqueum paravérunt pédibus meis: * et incurvavérunt ánimam meam.
fa24e09117bacc77ad14.english: 56:7 They prepared a snare for my feet; * and they bowed down my soul.

418acfe3a1c7f4756a65.latin: 56:7 Fodérunt ante fáciem meam fóveam: * et incidérunt in eam.
418acfe3a1c7f4756a65.english: 56:7 They dug a pit before my face, * and they are fallen into it.

f17d80376721e7676bc9.latin: 56:8 Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam.
f17d80376721e7676bc9.english: 56:8 My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and rehearse a psalm.

a6bae57d2135531e77de.latin: 56:9 Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.
a6bae57d2135531e77de.english: 56:9 Arise, O my glory, arise psaltery and harp: * I will arise early.

1085404826d1e5a7822f.latin: 56:10 Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psalmum dicam tibi in géntibus:
1085404826d1e5a7822f.english: 56:10 I will give praise to thee, O Lord, among the people: * I will sing a psalm to thee among the nations.

3db2e0737cdece87325f.latin: 56:11 Quóniam magnificáta est usque ad cælos misericórdia tua, * et usque ad nubes véritas tua.
3db2e0737cdece87325f.english: 56:11 For thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens: * and thy truth unto the clouds.

ce398ecb015f1fa53e07.latin: 56:12 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus: * et super omnem terram glória tua.
ce398ecb015f1fa53e07.english: 56:12 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: * and thy glory above all the earth.

9e788850fb263eaeeadb.english: Ant. For in thee my soul trusteth.

7d34ee0d95b026ca4f14.latin: Ant. Exaltáte * Regem sæculórum in opéribus vestris.
7d34ee0d95b026ca4f14.english: Ant. Give ye glory to him * in your works.

7aff6d6254794493c200.latin: 13:1 Magnus es, Dómine, in ætérnum, * et in ómnia sǽcula regnum tuum:
7aff6d6254794493c200.english: 13:1 Thou art great, O Lord, for ever, * and thy kingdom is unto all ages:

f91350e89aadf922a35b.latin: 13:2 Quóniam tu flagéllas, et salvas: dedúcis ad ínferos, et redúcis: * et non est qui effúgiat manum tuam.
f91350e89aadf922a35b.english: 13:2 For thou scourgest, and thou savest: thou leadest down to hell, and bringest up again: * and there is none that can escape thy hand.

d43026db6b94fb957362.latin: 13:3 Confitémini Dómino, fílii Israël, * et in conspéctu géntium laudáte eum:
d43026db6b94fb957362.english: 13:3 Give glory to the Lord, ye children of Israel, * and praise him in the sight of the Gentiles:

fb815a115c28e147810b.latin: 13:4 Quóniam ídeo dispérsit vos inter gentes, quæ ignórant eum, * ut vos enarrétis mirabília eius,
fb815a115c28e147810b.english: 13:4 Because he hath therefore scattered you among the Gentiles, who know not him, * that you may declare his wonderful works,

031d415da0a06a820f46.latin: 13:5 Et faciátis scire eos, * quia non est álius Deus omnípotens præter eum.
031d415da0a06a820f46.english: 13:5 And make them know * that there is no other almighty God besides him.

782a61aa336b57a5b859.latin: 13:6 Ipse castigávit nos propter iniquitátes nostras: * et ipse salvábit nos propter misericórdiam suam.
782a61aa336b57a5b859.english: 13:6 He hath chastised us for our iniquities: * and he will save us for his own mercy.

f3de6e55d599ee904d70.latin: 13:7 Aspícite ergo quæ fecit nobíscum, et cum timóre et tremóre confitémini illi: * Regémque sæculórum exaltáte in opéribus vestris.
f3de6e55d599ee904d70.english: 13:7 See then what he hath done with us, and with fear and trembling give ye glory to him: * and extol the eternal King of worlds in your works.

e3d84671e95ba134a501.latin: 13:8 Ego autem in terra captivitátis meæ confitébor illi: * quóniam osténdit maiestátem suam in gentem peccatrícem.
e3d84671e95ba134a501.english: 13:8 As for me, I will praise him in the land of my captivity: * because he hath shewn his majesty toward a sinful nation.

712137d90b8208b24c78.latin: 13:9 Convertímini ítaque, peccatóres, et fácite iustítiam coram Deo, * credéntes quod fáciat vobíscum misericórdiam suam:
712137d90b8208b24c78.english: 13:9 Be converted therefore, ye sinners, and do justice before God, * believing that he will shew his mercy to you.

882c393d31870706154f.latin: 13:10 Ego autem, et ánima mea * in eo lætábimur.
882c393d31870706154f.english: 13:10 And I and my soul * will rejoice in him.

b42fd5b4b77dea08be70.latin: 13:11 Benedícite Dóminum, omnes elécti eius: * ágite dies lætítiæ, et confitémini illi.
b42fd5b4b77dea08be70.english: 13:11 Bless ye the Lord, all his elect, * keep days of joy, and give glory to him.

4f11ab41b8cd61149564.english: Ant. Give ye glory to him in your works.

c1c3414733258397e0fb.english: Ant. Praise ye the Lord from the heavens, all His angels.

78aaf7a767927d4d4d12.latin:
Rom 13:12-13
Nox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit. Abiciámus ergo ópera tenebrárum, et induámur arma lucis. Sicut in die honéste ambulémus.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟.br. Sana ánimam meam, * Quia peccávi tibi.
℟. Sana ánimam meam, * Quia peccávi tibi.
℣. Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei
℟. Quia peccávi tibi.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Sana ánimam meam, * Quia peccávi tibi.
Hymnus
Ales diéi núntius
Lucem propínquam prǽcinit:
Nos excitátor méntium
Iam Christus ad vitam vocat.
Auférte, clamat, léctulos,
Ægro sopóre désides:
Castíque, recti, ac sóbrii
Vigiláte, iam sum próximus.
Iesum ciámus vócibus,
Flentes, precántes, sóbrii:
Inténta supplicátio
Dormíre cor mundum vetat.
Tu, Christe, somnum díscute:
Tu rumpe noctis víncula:
Tu solve peccátum vetus,
Novúmque lumen íngere.
Deo Patri sit glória,
Eiúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Et nunc, et in perpétuum.
Amen.
℣. Repléti sumus mane misericórdia tua.
℟. Exsultávimus, et delectáti sumus.
78aaf7a767927d4d4d12.english:
Rom 13:12-13
The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟.br. Heal my soul, * for I have sinned against thee.
℟. Heal my soul, * for I have sinned against thee.
℣. I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me
℟. For I have sinned against thee.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Heal my soul, * for I have sinned against thee.
Hymn
As the bird, whose clarion gay
Sounds before the dawn is grey,
Christ, who brings the spirit’s day,
Calls us, close at hand:
Wake! he cries, and for my sake,
From your eyes dull slumbers shake!
Sober, righteous, chaste, awake!
At the door I stand!
Lord, to thee we lift on high
Fervent prayer and bitter cry:
Hearts aroused to pray and sigh
May not slumber more:
Break the sleep of death and time,
Forged by Adam’s ancient crime;
And the light of Eden’s prime
To the world restore!
Unto God the Father, Son,
Holy Spirit, Three in One,
One in Three, be glory done,
Now and evermore.
Amen.

b3d3c068a7c95c60396e.latin:
Nonis Octóbris Luna vicésima quinta. Anno Dómini 2026
Festum sacratíssimi Rosárii beátæ Maríæ Vírginis; itémque sanctæ Maríæ de Victória commemorátio, quam sanctus Pius Quintus, Póntifex Máximus, ob insígnem victóriam a Christiánis bello naváli, eiúsdem sanctíssimæ Dei Genitrícis auxílio, hac ipsa die de Turcis reportátam, quotánnis fíeri instítuit.
Romæ, via Ardeatína, deposítio sancti Marci, Papæ et Confessóris.
In Província quæ nuncupátur Augústa Euphratésia, sanctórum Mártyrum Sérgii et Bacchi, nobílium Romanórum, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre. Ex his Bacchus támdiu nervis crudis cæsus est, quoadúsque, toto córpore discíssus, in Christi confessióne emítteret spíritum; Sérgius vero clavátis cothúrnis pedes indútus, et, cum in fide fixus manéret, data senténtia, iussus est decollári. Beáti autem Sérgii nómine locus ubi quiéscit, Sergiópolis appellátus est, et, ob præclára mirácula, frequénti Christianórum concúrsu honorátur.
Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Marcélli et Apuléii, qui prius quidem Simóni mago adhæsérunt; sed, vidéntes mirabília quæ per Apóstolum Petrum Dóminus operabátur, ambo, relícto Simóne, se doctrínæ Apostólicæ tradidérunt, ac, post passiónem Apostolórum, sub Aureliáno Consulári, corónam martýrii reportárunt, sepultíque sunt non longe ab Urbe.
Item apud Augústam Euphratésiam sanctæ Iúliæ Vírginis, quæ, sub Marciáno Prǽside, martýrium consummávit.
Patávii sanctæ Iustínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, a beáto Prosdócimo, sancti Petri discípulo, baptizáta, et, cum in fide Christi constánter persísteret, Máximi Prǽsidis iussu, transverberáta gládio, migrávit ad Dóminum.
Apud Bitúricas, in Aquitánia, sancti Augústi Presbýteri et Confessóris.
In pago Rheménsi sancti Heláni Presbýteri.
In Suécia Translátio córporis sanctæ Birgíttæ Víduæ.
℣. Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
℟. Deo grátias.
b3d3c068a7c95c60396e.english:
October 7th 2026, the 25th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
At Rome, upon the Ardeatine Way, (in the year 336,) the holy Confessor, Pope Mark, (who succeeded Sylvester I, and reigned 8 months and 20 days.)
In the district called Rasaphe, in Syria, the holy martyrs Sergius and Bacchus, noble Roman officers under the Emperor Maximian. Bacchus was lashed with strips of raw hide till his whole body was cut into ribbons, and so, still confessing Christ, gave up the ghost. Sergius had his legs tortured in the boots, but remaining firm in the faith, sentence was given on him that he should be beheaded. The place where he sleepeth was called after him Sergiopolis instead of Rasaphe, (by command of the Emperor Justinian,) and thither Christians do greatly resort on account of famous miracles.
At Rome, the holy martyrs Marcellus and Apuleius, who were first disciples of Simon Magus, but afterward, seeing the wonders which the Lord wrought by the Apostle Peter, became disciples of the Apostle, and, after he had suffered, won the crown of martyrdom under the Consular Aurelian. They are buried not far from the city.
At Rasaphe also, the holy Virgin Julia, who gained martyrdom under the President Marcian.
At Padua, the holy Virgin and martyr Justina, who was baptized by blessed Prosdocimus, a disciple of the holy Apostle Peter. Forasmuch as she stood firm in the faith of Christ, the President Maximus caused her to be run through with the sword, and she passed away hence to be ever with the Lord.
At Bourges, (about the year 560,) the holy Priest and Confessor Augustus.
At Reims, (in the sixth century,) the holy Priest Helanus.
Upon the same day is made the memorial of St. Mary, styled of Victory, the yearly observance of which memorial the Supreme Pontiff blessed Pius V. ordained on account of the famous victory gained by the Christians over the Turks upon this day in the sea-fight of Lepanto, by the help of the aforesaid Mother of God, and Gregory XIII instituted the yearly solemn feast of the same most Blessed Virgin to be kept upon the first Lord's Day in this present month of October.
℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
℟. Thanks be to God.

1d2cbc8f3a5c4d4433f7.english: 131:11 The Lord hath sworn truth to David, and he will not make it void: * of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne.

d117fe6eba912f836e93.latin: 131:12 Si custodíerint fílii tui testaméntum meum, * et testimónia mea hæc, quæ docébo eos:

2784cc8b18cbd5fc40e2.latin: 131:13 Quóniam elégit Dóminus Sion: * elégit eam in habitatiónem sibi.

ea3b6440badb0bb73f79.latin: 131:14 Hæc réquies mea in sǽculum sǽculi: * hic habitábo quóniam elégi eam.

e5929e28bc5b5afac369.latin: 131:18 Inimícos eius índuam confusióne: * super ipsum autem efflorébit sanctificátio mea.
e5929e28bc5b5afac369.english: 131:18 His enemies I will clothe with confusion: * but upon him shall my sanctification flourish.

54c1eb441cc4fe7aa7bf.latin:
2 Cor 1:3-4
Benedíctus Deus, et Pater Dómini nostri Iesu Christi, Pater misericordiárum, et Deus totíus consolatiónis, qui consolátur nos in omni tribulatióne nostra.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟.br. Benedícam Dóminum * In omni témpore.
℟. Benedícam Dóminum * In omni témpore.
℣. Semper laus eius in ore meo.
℟. In omni témpore.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Benedícam Dóminum * In omni témpore.
Hymnus
Tellúris ingens Cónditor,
Mundi solum qui éruens,
Pulsis aquæ moléstiis,
Terram dedísti immóbilem:
Ut germen aptum próferens,
Fulvis decóra flóribus,
Fecúnda fructu sísteret,
Pastúmque gratum rédderet.
Mentis perústæ vúlnera
Munda viróre grátiæ:
Ut facta fletu díluat,
Motúsque pravos átterat.
Iussis tuis obtémperet:
Nullis malis appróximet:
Bonis repléri gáudeat,
Et mortis actum nésciat.
Præsta, Pater piíssime,
Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
℣. Dirigátur, Dómine, orátio mea.
℟. Sicut incénsum in conspéctu tuo.
54c1eb441cc4fe7aa7bf.english:
2 Cor 1:3-4
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟.br. I will bless the Lord * at all times.
℟. I will bless the Lord * at all times.
℣. His praise shall be always in my mouth.
℟. At all times
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. I will bless the Lord * at all times.
Hymn
Earth's mighty Maker, whose command
Raised from the sea the solid land;
And drove each billowy heap away,
And bade the earth stand firm for aye:
That so, with flowers of golden hue,
The seeds of each it might renew;
And fruit-trees bearing fruit might yield,
And pleasant pasture of the field:
Our spirit’s rankling wounds efface
With dewy freshness of thy grace:
That grief may cleanse each deed of ill,
And o’er each lust may triumph still.
Let every soul thy law obey,
And keep from every evil way;
Rejoice each promised good to win,
And flee from every mortal sin.
Hear thou our prayer, Almighty King!
Hear thou our praises, while we sing,
Adoring with the heavenly host,
The Father, Son, and Holy Ghost!
Amen.
℣. O Lord, direct my prayer.
℟. As incense in thy sight.

dd6a339e9f0a1f8e045e.latin:
Cæléstis aulæ Núntius,
Arcána pandens Núminis,
Plenam salútat grátia
Dei Paréntem Vírginem.
Virgo propínquam sánguine
Matrem Ioánnis vísitat,
Qui, clausus alvo, géstiens
Adésse Christum núntiat.
Verbum, quod ante sǽcula
E mente Patris pródiit,
E Matris alvo Vírginis,
Mortális Infans, náscitur.
Templo puéllus sístitur,
Legíque paret Légifer,
Hic se Redémptor páupere
Prétio redémptus ímmolat.
Quem iam dolébat pérditum,
Mox læta Mater ínvenit
Ignóta doctis méntibus
Edisseréntem Fílium.
In monte olívis cónsito
Redémptor orans prócidit,
Mæret, pavéscit, déficit,
Sudóre manans sánguinis.
A proditóre tráditus
Raptátur in pœnas Deus,
Durísque vinctus néxibus,
Flagris cruéntis cǽditur.
Intéxta acútis séntibus,
Coróna contuméliæ,
Squalénti amíctum púrpura,
Regem corónat glóriæ.
Molis crucem ter árduæ,
Sudans, anhélans, cóncidens,
Ad montis usque vérticem
Gestáre vi compéllitur.
Confíxus atro stípite
Inter sceléstos ínnocens,
Orándo pro tortóribus,
Exsánguis efflat spíritum.
Glória tibi, Dómine,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
dd6a339e9f0a1f8e045e.english:
The messenger from God's high throne
His secret counsel making known
Hails Mary, child of David's race,
God's Virgin-Mother, full of grace.
The Mother-Maid with joyous feet
Her friend, John's mother, goes to greet;
He, stirring in the enclosing womb,
Declares that Christ his Lord has come.
The Word, who ere the worlds began,
From God the Father's thought forth ran,
Of Mary, Virgin undefiled,
For us is born a mortal child.
Christ to the temple courts they bring;
The King's own law subjects the King;
The world's Redeemer for a price
Is there redeemed, our sacrifice.
The joyful Mother finds once more
The Son she mourned as lost before;
While doctors by his speech were shown
The mysteries they had never known.
The Mount of Olives witnesseth
The awful agony of God:
His soul is sorrowful to death,
His sweat of blood bedews the sod.
And now the traitor's work is done:
The clamorous crowds around him surge;
Bound to pillar, God the Son
Quivers beneath the blood-red scourge.
Lo! clad in purple soiled and worn,
Meekly the Saviour waiteth now
While wretches plait the cruel thorn
To crown with shame his royal brow.
Sweating and sighing, faint with loss
Of what hath flowed from life's red fount,
He bears the exceeding heavy cross
Up to the verge of Calvary's mount.
Nailed to the wood of ancient curse,
Between two thieves the sinless one
Still praying for his murderers,
Breathes forth his soul, and all is done!
All honour, praise and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-Born, to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father, and to Paraclete.
Amen.

0c2a7b999f769d052285.english: Ant. Give us * help from trouble, O Lord.

de49a04ad0723a46207f.english: 59:3 God, thou hast cast us off, and hast destroyed us; * thou hast been angry, and hast had mercy on us.

1d4ab535f95c3c938b61.latin: 59:4 Commovísti terram, et conturbásti eam: * sana contritiónes eius, quia commóta est.
1d4ab535f95c3c938b61.english: 59:4 Thou hast moved the earth, and hast troubled it: * heal thou the breaches thereof, for it has been moved.

3d2453aab8ca88c60cd7.latin: 59:5 Ostendísti pópulo tuo dura: * potásti nos vino compunctiónis.
3d2453aab8ca88c60cd7.english: 59:5 Thou hast shewn thy people hard things; * thou hast made us drink the wine of sorrow.

10be08e1b02e05ea1fc0.latin: 59:6 Dedísti metuéntibus te significatiónem: * ut fúgiant a fácie arcus:
10be08e1b02e05ea1fc0.english: 59:6 Thou hast given a warning to them that fear thee: * that they may flee from before the bow:

9d3f67d5fe5ab65fb6e2.latin: 59:7 Ut liberéntur dilécti tui: * salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me.
9d3f67d5fe5ab65fb6e2.english: 59:7 That thy beloved may be delivered. * Save me with thy right hand, and hear me.

0621b5147bd265408347.latin: 59:8 Deus locútus est in sancto suo: * lætábor, et partíbor Síchimam: et convállem tabernaculórum metíbor.
0621b5147bd265408347.english: 59:8 God hath spoken in his holy place: * I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem; and will mete out the vale of tabernacles.

fb86b21c3cc0c8a28919.latin: 59:9 Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim fortitúdo cápitis mei.
fb86b21c3cc0c8a28919.english: 59:9 Galaad is mine, and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim is the strength of my head.

23d9d43b51bb7f3d961c.latin: 59:9 Iuda rex meus: * Moab olla spei meæ.
23d9d43b51bb7f3d961c.english: 59:9 Juda is my king: * Moab is the pot of my hope.

a253fc74670420b99fb6.latin: 59:10 In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ súbditi sunt.
a253fc74670420b99fb6.english: 59:10 Into Edom will I stretch out my shoe: * to me the foreigners are made subject.

0b8b7c04c81c645cfb83.latin: 59:11 Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?
0b8b7c04c81c645cfb83.english: 59:11 Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?

2fa688a8a7123026066b.latin: 59:12 Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos? * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
2fa688a8a7123026066b.english: 59:12 Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go out with our armies?

b3fdf06e749aa64f9479.latin: 59:13 Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.
b3fdf06e749aa64f9479.english: 59:13 Give us help from trouble: * for vain is the salvation of man.

0a87fc2cdec3e51c7fdd.latin: 59:14 In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet tribulántes nos.
0a87fc2cdec3e51c7fdd.english: 59:14 Through God we shall do mightily: * and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us.

c7eb0b1e3443b6f87759.latin: 60:2 Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: * inténde oratióni meæ.
c7eb0b1e3443b6f87759.english: 60:2 Hear, O God, my supplication: * be attentive to my prayer.

cef58e7a0dd44a849c1e.latin: 60:3 A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi: * dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.
cef58e7a0dd44a849c1e.english: 60:3 To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth: * when my heart was in anguish, thou hast exalted me on a rock.

995f546d5aac8015bbf2.latin: 60:4 Deduxísti me, quia factus es spes mea: * turris fortitúdinis a fácie inimíci.
995f546d5aac8015bbf2.english: 60:4 Thou hast conducted me; for thou hast been my hope: * a tower of strength against the face of the enemy.

cef8f336df9432e07c5b.latin: 60:5 Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula: * prótegar in velaménto alárum tuárum.
cef8f336df9432e07c5b.english: 60:5 In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever: * I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings.

055be86f728a83d2189e.latin: 60:6 Quóniam tu, Deus meus, exaudísti oratiónem meam: * dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum.
055be86f728a83d2189e.english: 60:6 For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer: * thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name.

e8996a11fd7a8739df27.latin: 60:7 Dies super dies regis adícies: * annos eius usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis.
e8996a11fd7a8739df27.english: 60:7 Thou wilt add days to the days of the king: * his years even to generation and generation.

91647a8bd3d2f0f0c752.latin: 60:8 Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei: * misericórdiam et veritátem eius quis requíret?
91647a8bd3d2f0f0c752.english: 60:8 He abideth for ever in the sight of God: * his mercy and truth who shall search?

b03a99a27c6a77ef4dec.latin: 60:9 Sic psalmum dicam nómini tuo in sǽculum sǽculi: * ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.
b03a99a27c6a77ef4dec.english: 60:9 So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever: * that I may pay my vows from day to day.

b280fe31ea06796d26d3.latin: Ant. Da nobis Dómine auxílium de tribulatióne.
b280fe31ea06796d26d3.english: Ant. Give us help from trouble, O Lord.

7ebd786013f57aebb23e.english: Ant. O bless our God * ye people.

93781f8182da1b4e9b85.latin: 61:2 Nonne Deo subiécta erit ánima mea? * ab ipso enim salutáre meum.
93781f8182da1b4e9b85.english: 61:2 Shall not my soul be subject to God? * for from him is my salvation.

bcb839de6f5c8e9714d2.latin: 61:3 Nam et ipse Deus meus, et salutáris meus: * suscéptor meus, non movébor ámplius.
bcb839de6f5c8e9714d2.english: 61:3 For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my protector, I shall be moved no more.

f11f74d0cf85f2dd92e0.latin: 61:4 Quoúsque irrúitis in hóminem? * interfícitis univérsi vos: tamquam paríeti inclináto et macériæ depúlsæ?
f11f74d0cf85f2dd92e0.english: 61:4 How long do you rush in upon a man? * you all kill, as if you were thrusting down a leaning wall, and a tottering fence.

81741b546fe9a56cca17.latin: 61:5 Verúmtamen prétium meum cogitavérunt repéllere, cucúrri in siti: * ore suo benedicébant, et corde suo maledicébant.
81741b546fe9a56cca17.english: 61:5 But they have thought to cast away my price; I ran in thirst: * they blessed with their mouth, but cursed with their heart.

c134fe8fe969b59d6921.latin: 61:6 Verúmtamen Deo subiécta esto, ánima mea: * quóniam ab ipso patiéntia mea.
c134fe8fe969b59d6921.english: 61:6 But be thou, O my soul, subject to God: * for from him is my patience.

ef4b382dd35247578176.latin: 61:7 Quia ipse Deus meus, et salvátor meus: * adiútor meus, non emigrábo.
ef4b382dd35247578176.english: 61:7 For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my helper, I shall not be moved.

647e2d0562a1ed1df079.latin: 61:8 In Deo salutáre meum, et glória mea: * Deus auxílii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.
647e2d0562a1ed1df079.english: 61:8 In God is my salvation and my glory: * he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.

7791bb59420b96605a0f.latin: 61:9 Speráte in eo omnis congregátio pópuli, effúndite coram illo corda vestra: * Deus adiútor noster in ætérnum.
7791bb59420b96605a0f.english: 61:9 Trust in him, all ye congregation of people: pour out your hearts before him. * God is our helper for ever.
