2b2d2de2ac303b4908ac.english: 61:10 But vain are the sons of men, the sons of men are liars in the balances: * that by vanity they may together deceive.

ceec8d27fdd60b00f162.latin: 61:11 Nolíte speráre in iniquitáte, et rapínas nolíte concupíscere: * divítiæ si áffluant, nolíte cor appónere.
ceec8d27fdd60b00f162.english: 61:11 Trust not in iniquity, and cover not robberies: * if riches abound, set not your heart upon them.

aac0842414bfa9deafe2.latin: 61:12 Semel locútus est Deus, duo hæc audívi, quia potéstas Dei est, et tibi, Dómine, misericórdia: * quia tu reddes unicuíque iuxta ópera sua.
aac0842414bfa9deafe2.english: 61:12 God hath spoken once, these two things have I heard, that power belongeth to God, and mercy to thee, O Lord; * for thou wilt render to every man according to his works.

3a320807a465035b85cf.latin: 65:1 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * date glóriam laudi eius.
3a320807a465035b85cf.english: 65:1 Shout with joy to God, all the earth, sing ye a psalm to his name; * give glory to his praise.

f831b5a75d18c9fe5e7b.latin: 65:3 Dícite Deo: Quam terribília sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * in multitúdine virtútis tuæ mentiéntur tibi inimíci tui.
f831b5a75d18c9fe5e7b.english: 65:3 Say unto God, How terrible are thy works, O Lord! * in the multitude of thy strength thy enemies shall lie to thee.

513bd0520560924ac6c3.latin: 65:4 Omnis terra adóret te, et psallat tibi: * psalmum dicat nómini tuo.
513bd0520560924ac6c3.english: 65:4 Let all the earth adore thee, * and sing to thee: let it sing a psalm to thy name.

3fafd3cafb4cc9f40146.latin: 65:5 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dei: * terríbilis in consíliis super fílios hóminum.
3fafd3cafb4cc9f40146.english: 65:5 Come and see the works of God; * who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men.

3e03d57f0d2aa3c007c8.latin: 65:6 Qui convértit mare in áridam, in flúmine pertransíbunt pede: * ibi lætábimur in ipso.
3e03d57f0d2aa3c007c8.english: 65:6 Who turneth the sea into dry land, in the river they shall pass on foot: * there shall we rejoice in him.

bc0583066f039e4f4fd1.latin: 65:7 Qui dominátur in virtúte sua in ætérnum, óculi eius super gentes respíciunt: * qui exásperant non exalténtur in semetípsis.
bc0583066f039e4f4fd1.english: 65:7 Who by his power ruleth for ever: his eyes behold the nations; * let not them that provoke him be exalted in themselves.

a6273bf57b58da2d1fa7.latin: 65:8 Benedícite, gentes, Deum nostrum: * et audítam fácite vocem laudis eius,
a6273bf57b58da2d1fa7.english: 65:8 O bless our God, ye Gentiles: * and make the voice of his praise to be heard.

2294abd894a5d1df862b.latin: 65:9 Qui pósuit ánimam meam ad vitam: * et non dedit in commotiónem pedes meos.
2294abd894a5d1df862b.english: 65:9 Who hath set my soul to live: * and hath not suffered my feet to be moved:

a2d3a86b2e48f858db99.latin: 65:10 Quóniam probásti nos, Deus: * igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum.
a2d3a86b2e48f858db99.english: 65:10 For thou, O God, hast proved us: * thou hast tried us by fire, as silver is tried.

992ca66f12275eb73b8e.latin: 65:11 Induxísti nos in láqueum, posuísti tribulatiónes in dorso nostro: * imposuísti hómines super cápita nostra.
992ca66f12275eb73b8e.english: 65:11 Thou hast brought us into a net, thou hast laid afflictions on our back: * thou hast set men over our heads.

2d63e459528a6355dfe5.latin: 65:12 Transívimus per ignem et aquam: * et eduxísti nos in refrigérium.
2d63e459528a6355dfe5.english: 65:12 We have passed through fire and water, * and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment.

9e5e0d920bc9dfadefaf.latin: 65:13 Introíbo in domum tuam in holocáustis: * reddam tibi vota mea, quæ distinxérunt lábia mea.
9e5e0d920bc9dfadefaf.english: 65:13 I will go into thy house with burnt offerings: * I will pay thee my vows, which my lips have uttered,

8746d819209f1e0fa23d.latin: 65:14 Et locútum est os meum, * in tribulatióne mea.
8746d819209f1e0fa23d.english: 65:14 And my mouth hath spoken, * when I was in trouble.

a792de9990f4a39a3ae7.latin: 65:15 Holocáusta medulláta ófferam tibi cum incénso aríetum: * ófferam tibi boves cum hircis.
a792de9990f4a39a3ae7.english: 65:15 I will offer up to thee holocausts full of marrow, with burnt offerings of rams: * I will offer to thee bullocks with goats.

9e2b053af1a6a5e720a5.latin: 65:16 Veníte, audíte, et narrábo, omnes, qui timétis Deum: * quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.
9e2b053af1a6a5e720a5.english: 65:16 Come and hear, all ye that fear God, * and I will tell you what great things he hath done for my soul.

baed3fb639824719f418.latin: 65:17 Ad ipsum ore meo clamávi, * et exaltávi sub lingua mea.
baed3fb639824719f418.english: 65:17 I cried to him with my mouth: * and I extolled him with my tongue.

685c7f98ae823a3ea7e8.latin: 65:18 Iniquitátem si aspéxi in corde meo, * non exáudiet Dóminus.
685c7f98ae823a3ea7e8.english: 65:18 If I have looked at iniquity in my heart, * the Lord will not hear me.

6a0b06d5b8215875f043.latin: 65:19 Proptérea exaudívit Deus, * et atténdit voci deprecatiónis meæ.
6a0b06d5b8215875f043.english: 65:19 Therefore hath God heard me, * and hath attended to the voice of my supplication.

34cc9bde5cae5d5e8e2c.latin: 65:20 Benedíctus Deus, * qui non amóvit oratiónem meam, et misericórdiam suam a me.
34cc9bde5cae5d5e8e2c.english: 65:20 Blessed be God, * who hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.

585c48dc2d505174e8f5.english: Ant. O bless our God ye people.

94584886de1cff384230.english: Ant. In the churches * bless ye the Lord.

330f0fd717b4177caf83.latin: 67:2 Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci eius, * et fúgiant qui odérunt eum, a fácie eius.
330f0fd717b4177caf83.english: 67:2 Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered: * and let them that hate him flee from before his face.

2b2ecf36c3414128cf45.latin: 67:3 Sicut déficit fumus, defíciant: * sicut fluit cera a fácie ignis, sic péreant peccatóres a fácie Dei.
2b2ecf36c3414128cf45.english: 67:3 As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away: * as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

e6eaf5430954b428d80a.latin: 67:4 Et iusti epuléntur, et exsúltent in conspéctu Dei: * et delecténtur in lætítia.
e6eaf5430954b428d80a.english: 67:4 And let the just feast, and rejoice before God: * and be delighted with gladness.

2dfe8e34ab4c2189cce8.latin: 67:5 Cantáte Deo, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum: (fit reverentia) Dóminus nomen illi.
2dfe8e34ab4c2189cce8.english: 67:5 Sing ye to God, sing a psalm to his name, * make a way for him who ascendeth upon the west: (bow head) the Lord is his name.

8403a735cf89f7ee58b2.latin: 67:5 Exsultáte in conspéctu eius: * turbabúntur a fácie eius, patris orphanórum et iúdicis viduárum.
8403a735cf89f7ee58b2.english: 67:5 Rejoice ye before him: * but the wicked shall be troubled at his presence, who is the father of orphans, and the judge of widows.

9ed2310519901b223771.latin: 67:6 Deus in loco sancto suo: * Deus, qui inhabitáre facit uníus moris in domo:
9ed2310519901b223771.english: 67:6 God in his holy place: * God who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house:

2288feb03e1e2f6fdc09.latin: 67:7 Qui edúcit vinctos in fortitúdine, * simíliter eos qui exásperant, qui hábitant in sepúlcris.
2288feb03e1e2f6fdc09.english: 67:7 Who bringeth out them that were bound in strength; * in like manner them that provoke, that dwell in sepulchres.

9ae66b20c13736958c14.latin: 67:8 Deus, cum egrederéris in conspéctu pópuli tui, * cum pertransíres in desérto:
9ae66b20c13736958c14.english: 67:8 O God, when thou didst go forth in the sight of thy people, * when thou didst pass through the desert:

fb6998bc0d347439a931.latin: 67:9 Terra mota est, étenim cæli distillavérunt a fácie Dei Sínai, * a fácie Dei Israël.
fb6998bc0d347439a931.english: 67:9 The earth was moved, and the heavens dropped at the presence of the God of Sinai, * at the presence of the God of Israel.

64679daaca54bde1e5db.latin: 67:10 Plúviam voluntáriam segregábis, Deus, hereditáti tuæ: * et infirmáta est, tu vero perfecísti eam.
64679daaca54bde1e5db.english: 67:10 Thou shalt set aside for thy inheritance a free rain, * O God: and it was weakened, but thou hast made it perfect.

b3eb39e1678d776bb8da.latin: 67:11 Animália tua habitábunt in ea: * parásti in dulcédine tua páuperi, Deus.
b3eb39e1678d776bb8da.english: 67:11 In it shall thy animals dwell; * in thy sweetness, O God, thou hast provided for the poor.

7a63557d26d1d81b309b.latin: 67:12 Dóminus dabit verbum evangelizántibus, * virtúte multa.
7a63557d26d1d81b309b.english: 67:12 The Lord shall give the word to them that preach good tidings, * with great power.

f92c4f70450b42dc64d4.latin: 67:13 Rex virtútum dilécti, dilécti: * et speciéi domus divídere spólia.
f92c4f70450b42dc64d4.english: 67:13 The king of powers is of the beloved, * of the beloved; and the beauty of the house shall divide spoils.

7babfd2b77746fc2ee8b.latin: 67:14 Si dormiátis inter médios cleros, pennæ colúmbæ deargentátæ, * et posterióra dorsi eius in pallóre auri.
7babfd2b77746fc2ee8b.english: 67:14 If you sleep among the midst of lots, you shall be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, * and the hinder parts of her back with the paleness of gold.

60ba9e667e27c6c08a7a.latin: 67:15 Dum discérnit cæléstis reges super eam, nive dealbabúntur in Selmon: * mons Dei, mons pinguis.
60ba9e667e27c6c08a7a.english: 67:15 When he that is in heaven appointeth kings over her, they shall be whited with snow in Selmon. * The mountain of God is a fat mountain,

d8d04f214db755652567.latin: 67:16 Mons coagulátus, mons pinguis: * ut quid suspicámini montes coagulátos?
d8d04f214db755652567.english: 67:16 a curdled mountain, a fat mountain; * Why suspect, ye curdled mountains?

c0f30fdfa11d257ade66.latin: 67:17 Mons, in quo beneplácitum est Deo habitáre in eo: * étenim Dóminus habitábit in finem.
c0f30fdfa11d257ade66.english: 67:17 A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell: * for there the Lord shall dwell unto the end.

5d97bd54a19e42eb95ae.latin: 67:18 Currus Dei decem míllibus múltiplex, míllia lætántium: * Dóminus in eis in Sina in sancto.
5d97bd54a19e42eb95ae.english: 67:18 The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands; thousands of them that rejoice: * the Lord is among them in Sinai, in the holy place.

87d520f74df26675b015.latin: 67:19 Ascendísti in altum, cepísti captivitátem: * accepísti dona in homínibus.
87d520f74df26675b015.english: 67:19 Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive; * thou hast received gifts in men.

2d4290a06af0d3cff64c.latin: 67:19 Étenim non credéntes, * inhabitáre Dóminum Deum.
2d4290a06af0d3cff64c.english: 67:19 Yea for those also that do not believe, * the dwelling of the Lord God.

30441878f07c5f572e0b.latin: 67:20 Benedíctus Dóminus die cotídie: * prósperum iter fáciet nobis Deus salutárium nostrórum.
30441878f07c5f572e0b.english: 67:20 Blessed be the Lord day by day: * the God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous to us.

cc6bf9a9b9342b6c15a1.latin: 67:21 Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: * et Dómini Dómini éxitus mortis.
cc6bf9a9b9342b6c15a1.english: 67:21 Our God is the God of salvation: * and of the Lord, of the Lord are the issues from death.

4c34490261b17c4ade7a.latin: 67:22 Verúmtamen Deus confrínget cápita inimicórum suórum: * vérticem capílli perambulántium in delíctis suis.
4c34490261b17c4ade7a.english: 67:22 But God shall break the heads of his enemies: * the hairy crown of them that walk on in their sins.

1838cedefefa873e84c2.latin: 67:23 Dixit Dóminus: Ex Basan convértam, * convértam in profúndum maris:
1838cedefefa873e84c2.english: 67:23 The Lord said: I will turn them from Basan, * I will turn them into the depth of the sea:

39ed6b39b5f0d4163918.latin: 67:24 Ut intingátur pes tuus in sánguine: * lingua canum tuórum ex inimícis, ab ipso.
39ed6b39b5f0d4163918.english: 67:24 That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thy enemies; * the tongue of thy dogs be red with the same.

614659fbec3ca0150aa9.latin: 67:25 Vidérunt ingréssus tuos, Deus: * ingréssus Dei mei: regis mei qui est in sancto.
614659fbec3ca0150aa9.english: 67:25 They have seen thy goings, O God, * the goings of my God: of my king who is in his sanctuary.

1c7259bd03116e18480e.latin: 67:26 Prævenérunt príncipes coniúncti psalléntibus: * in médio iuvenculárum tympanistriárum.
1c7259bd03116e18480e.english: 67:26 Princes went before joined with singers, * in the midst of young damsels playing on timbrels.

38b3c7e05dfa05edc3e3.latin: 67:27 In ecclésiis benedícite Deo Dómino, * de fóntibus Israël.
38b3c7e05dfa05edc3e3.english: 67:27 In the churches bless ye God the Lord, * from the fountains of Israel.

051942dc4b24d0da5cce.latin: 67:28 Ibi Béniamin adolescéntulus: * in mentis excéssu.
051942dc4b24d0da5cce.english: 67:28 There is Benjamin a youth, * in ecstasy of mind.

31f9f80087e0f65890d3.latin: 67:28 Príncipes Iuda, duces eórum: * príncipes Zábulon, príncipes Néphtali.
31f9f80087e0f65890d3.english: 67:28 The princes of Juda are their leaders: * the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali.

e676130b90c81397c947.latin: 67:29 Manda, Deus, virtúti tuæ: * confírma hoc, Deus, quod operátus es in nobis.
e676130b90c81397c947.english: 67:29 Command thy strength, O God: * confirm, O God, what thou hast wrought in us.

b35bf309342b6b514809.latin: 67:30 A templo tuo in Ierúsalem, * tibi ófferent reges múnera.
b35bf309342b6b514809.english: 67:30 From thy temple in Jerusalem, * kings shall offer presents to thee.

cda327f525e3e774c3e2.latin: 67:31 Íncrepa feras arúndinis, congregátio taurórum in vaccis populórum: * ut exclúdant eos, qui probáti sunt argénto.
cda327f525e3e774c3e2.english: 67:31 Rebuke the wild beasts of the reeds, the congregation of bulls with the kine of the people; * who seek to exclude them who are tried with silver.

d6aeceae59e17a8bc2d6.latin: 67:31 Díssipa gentes, quæ bella volunt: vénient legáti ex Ægýpto: * Æthiópia prævéniet manus eius Deo.
d6aeceae59e17a8bc2d6.english: 67:31 Scatter thou the nations that delight in wars: ambassadors shall come out of Egypt: * Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God.

0089c699490676480ce8.latin: 67:33 Regna terræ, cantáte Deo: * psállite Dómino.
0089c699490676480ce8.english: 67:33 Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth: * sing ye to the Lord:

9a28523eb47a905bd805.latin: 67:33 Psállite Deo, qui ascéndit super cælum cæli, * ad Oriéntem.
9a28523eb47a905bd805.english: 67:33 Sing ye to God, who mounteth above the heaven of heavens, * to the east.

09d276503d4402eed8fd.latin: 67:34 Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis, date glóriam Deo super Israël, * magnificéntia eius, et virtus eius in núbibus.
09d276503d4402eed8fd.english: 67:34 Behold he will give to his voice the voice of power: give ye glory to God for Israel, * his magnificence, and his power is in the clouds.

82bf4676fad09426dd17.latin: 67:36 Mirábilis Deus in sanctis suis, Deus Israël ipse dabit virtútem, et fortitúdinem plebi suæ, * benedíctus Deus.
82bf4676fad09426dd17.english: 67:36 God is wonderful in his saints: the God of Israel is he who will give power and strength to his people; * blessed be God.

1cc942a65eeb5757b380.english: Ant. In the churches bless ye the Lord.

7c119e54660e11998494.english: ℣. O bless our God, ye people.

fcfed015adcae40d883b.latin: ℟. Et audítam fácite vocem laudis eius.

74e7b556560d72eb42d0.latin:
℣. Iube, domne, benedícere.
Benedictio. Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Rex Angelórum.
℟. Amen.
Lectio unica
Homilía sancti Bernárdi Abbátis
Sermo de Aquæductu
Verbum caro factum est, et hábitat iam in nobis. Hábitat in memória nostra, hábitat in cogitatióne, quia usque ad ipsam descéndit imaginatiónem. Quonam modo, inquis? Nimírum iacens in præsépio, in virgináli grémio cubans, in monte prǽdicans, in oratióne pernóctans, in cruce pendens, in morte pallens, liber inter mórtuos et in inférno ímperans, seu étiam tértia die resúrgens, et Apóstolis loca clavórum, victóriæ signa, demónstrans, novíssime coram eis cæli secréta conscéndens. Quid horum non vere, non pie, non sancte cogitátur? Quidquid horum cógito, Deum cógito; et per ómnia est Deus meus. Hæc ego meditári dixi sapiéntiam, et prudéntiam iudicávi eructáre memóriam suavitátis; quóniam in huiuscémodi núcleis virga sacerdotális copiósa prodúxit, quam, in supérnis háuriens, ubérius nobis María refúdit. In supérnis plane et ultra Angelos, quæ Verbum ex ipso Patris corde suscépit.
℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟. Súmite psaltérium iucúndum in insígni die solemnitátis vestræ:
* Et exsultáte Vírgini adiutríci nostræ.
℣. Cantáte ei cánticum novum: annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam eius.
℟. Et exsultáte Vírgini adiutríci nostræ.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Et exsultáte Vírgini adiutríci nostræ.
74e7b556560d72eb42d0.english:
℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.
Benediction. May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.
℟. Amen.
Lectio unica
Homily by St. Bernard, Abbot (of Clairvaux)
Homily on the water course
The Word was made flesh, and dwelleth even now among us. He dwelleth in our memory. He dwelleth in our thought. He hath come down even unto our imagination; and how sayest thou doth he so? By lying in the manger, by nestling in His mother's breast, by preaching upon the mountain, by remaining all night in prayer to God, by hanging upon the Cross, by turning pale in death, by going down free among the dead and triumphing in hell, by rising again the third day, by showing to the Apostles the places of the nails the marks of his victory, by ascending up into heaven while they all beheld Him, of which of these things think we not with truth, with godliness, with holiness? If I think of any of these, I think of God, and He is my God through them all. To think of these things I have decreed to be wisdom, and to set forth the memory of their sweetness I have judged to be prudence. The rod of Aaron the Priest brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds; but these things are the almonds of that Rod which came forth out of the stem of Jesse, the Rod whereof sprang the flower, a Rod which was raised in Mary into places higher than the earthly tabernacle, higher indeed, even into places higher than angels, since she received the Word into herself out of the very heart of the Eternal Father.
℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟. Take the pleasant harp, in the time appointed, on your solemn feastday;
* And sing aloud unto the Virgin our strength.
℣. O sing unto her a new song, declare her glory among the heathen.
℟. And sing aloud unto the Virgin our strength.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. And sing aloud unto the Virgin our strength.

ac8e339ac7e586143bcc.latin: 68:2 Salvum me fac, Deus: * quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
ac8e339ac7e586143bcc.english: 68:2 Save me, O God: * for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

7991b3bb2bc4bbeacf38.latin: 68:3 Infíxus sum in limo profúndi: * et non est substántia.
7991b3bb2bc4bbeacf38.english: 68:3 I stick fast in the mire of the deep: * and there is no sure standing.

07ef7538027438b9810b.latin: 68:3 Veni in altitúdinem maris: * et tempéstas demérsit me.
07ef7538027438b9810b.english: 68:3 I am come into the depth of the sea: * and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.

46d287ddc76959320231.latin: 68:4 Laborávi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ: * defecérunt óculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum.
46d287ddc76959320231.english: 68:4 I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse: * my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God.

4b31ae6baf9f17462347.latin: 68:5 Multiplicáti sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, * qui odérunt me gratis.
4b31ae6baf9f17462347.english: 68:5 They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, * who hate me without cause.

6e32eb89b8962e72859f.latin: 68:5 Confortáti sunt qui persecúti sunt me inimíci mei iniúste: * quæ non rápui, tunc exsolvébam.
6e32eb89b8962e72859f.english: 68:5 My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me: * then did I pay that which I took not away.

a19a206d2cd50c2d1d42.latin: 68:6 Deus, tu scis insipiéntiam meam: * et delícta mea a te non sunt abscóndita.
a19a206d2cd50c2d1d42.english: 68:6 O God, thou knowest my foolishness; * and my offences are not hidden from thee.

494a9e10c9ffeb7d607f.latin: 68:7 Non erubéscant in me qui exspéctant te, Dómine, * Dómine virtútum.
494a9e10c9ffeb7d607f.english: 68:7 Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord, * the Lord of hosts.

05741e5149fe7bbeb6f2.latin: 68:7 Non confundántur super me * qui quærunt te, Deus Israël.
05741e5149fe7bbeb6f2.english: 68:7 Let them not be confounded on my account, * who seek thee, O God of Israel.

ff5e454a75976026dc5c.latin: 68:8 Quóniam propter te sustínui oppróbrium: * opéruit confúsio fáciem meam.
ff5e454a75976026dc5c.english: 68:8 Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; * shame hath covered my face.

3c1a99ff95fe39f8c986.latin: 68:9 Extráneus factus sum frátribus meis, * et peregrínus fíliis matris meæ.
3c1a99ff95fe39f8c986.english: 68:9 I am become a stranger to my brethren, * and an alien to the sons of my mother.

0371cd451c1952f77b54.latin: 68:10 Quóniam zelus domus tuæ comédit me: * et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.
0371cd451c1952f77b54.english: 68:10 For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up: * and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.

12bd61b222ac2ac4f501.latin: 68:11 Et opérui in ieiúnio ánimam meam: * et factum est in oppróbrium mihi.
12bd61b222ac2ac4f501.english: 68:11 And I covered my soul in fasting: * and it was made a reproach to me.

73db948f6cbbf4e3d0e8.latin: 68:12 Et pósui vestiméntum meum cilícium: * et factus sum illis in parábolam.
73db948f6cbbf4e3d0e8.english: 68:12 And I made haircloth my garment: * and I became a byword to them.

d8e5b4372403d5b5d218.latin: 68:13 Advérsum me loquebántur, qui sedébant in porta: * et in me psallébant qui bibébant vinum.
d8e5b4372403d5b5d218.english: 68:13 They that sat in the gate spoke against me: * and they that drank wine made me their song.

6bccad87751151404ce7.latin: 68:13 Ego vero oratiónem meam ad te, Dómine: * tempus benepláciti, Deus.
6bccad87751151404ce7.english: 68:13 But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord; * for the time of thy good pleasure, O God.

a313bf84a2706e16943a.latin: 68:14 In multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ exáudi me, * in veritáte salútis tuæ:
a313bf84a2706e16943a.english: 68:14 In the multitude of thy mercy hear me, * in the truth of thy salvation.

68b4fa7e63d032c61216.latin: 68:15 Éripe me de luto, ut non infígar: * líbera me ab iis, qui odérunt me, et de profúndis aquárum.
68b4fa7e63d032c61216.english: 68:15 Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast: * deliver me from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.

1af40f5e2b58b48307c9.latin: 68:16 Non me demérgat tempéstas aquæ, neque absórbeat me profúndum: * neque úrgeat super me púteus os suum.
1af40f5e2b58b48307c9.english: 68:16 Let not the tempest of water drown me, nor the deep swallow me up: * and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.

6dfd9c2f32047385ab03.latin: 68:17 Exáudi me, Dómine, quóniam benígna est misericórdia tua: * secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum réspice in me.
6dfd9c2f32047385ab03.english: 68:17 Hear me, O Lord, for thy mercy is kind; * look upon me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.

23affa696dc0f72c1aa7.latin: 68:18 Et ne avértas fáciem tuam a púero tuo: * quóniam tríbulor, velóciter exáudi me.
23affa696dc0f72c1aa7.english: 68:18 And turn not away thy face from thy servant: * for I am in trouble, hear me speedily.

5959a17466d34a58fd3f.latin: 68:19 Inténde ánimæ meæ, et líbera eam: * propter inimícos meos éripe me.
5959a17466d34a58fd3f.english: 68:19 Attend to my soul, and deliver it: * save me because of my enemies.

aa6c7659069e29a03c5a.latin: 68:20 Tu scis impropérium meum, et confusiónem meam, * et reveréntiam meam.
aa6c7659069e29a03c5a.english: 68:20 Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, * and my shame.

a24bc3e9cb918776eaa4.latin: 68:21 In conspéctu tuo sunt omnes qui tríbulant me: * impropérium exspectávit cor meum, et misériam.
a24bc3e9cb918776eaa4.english: 68:21 In thy sight are all they that afflict me; * my heart hath expected reproach and misery.

d1a66d6fcfb263ea86bb.latin: 68:21 Et sustínui qui simul contristarétur, et non fuit: * et qui consolarétur, et non invéni.
d1a66d6fcfb263ea86bb.english: 68:21 And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, * but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none.

3c2ea85320de6e7bb3cf.latin: 68:22 Et dedérunt in escam meam fel: * et in siti mea potavérunt me acéto.
3c2ea85320de6e7bb3cf.english: 68:22 And they gave me gall for my food, * and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

1ab61896db97135b6802.latin: 68:23 Fiat mensa eórum coram ipsis in láqueum, * et in retributiónes, et in scándalum.
1ab61896db97135b6802.english: 68:23 Let their table become as a snare before them, * and a recompense, and a stumblingblock.

a0ec273b99766324c024.latin: 68:24 Obscuréntur óculi eórum ne vídeant: * et dorsum eórum semper incúrva.
a0ec273b99766324c024.english: 68:24 Let their eyes be darkened that they see not; * and their back bend thou down always.

c29a4b4cd74191c1d328.latin: 68:25 Effúnde super eos iram tuam: * et furor iræ tuæ comprehéndat eos.
c29a4b4cd74191c1d328.english: 68:25 Pour out thy indignation upon them: * and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.

0799927bccdfbe24b401.latin: 68:26 Fiat habitátio eórum desérta: * et in tabernáculis eórum non sit qui inhábitet.
0799927bccdfbe24b401.english: 68:26 Let their habitation be made desolate: * and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles.

cac7f5a4fa204f34d2e7.latin: 68:27 Quóniam quem tu percussísti, persecúti sunt: * et super dolórem vúlnerum meórum addidérunt.
cac7f5a4fa204f34d2e7.english: 68:27 Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; * and they have added to the grief of my wounds.

5095ccba15fd51a16366.latin: 68:28 Appóne iniquitátem super iniquitátem eórum: * et non intrent in iustítiam tuam.
5095ccba15fd51a16366.english: 68:28 Add thou iniquity upon their iniquity: * and let them not come into thy justice.

3c2bcffb5d09be5c648a.latin: 68:29 Deleántur de libro vivéntium: * et cum iustis non scribántur.
3c2bcffb5d09be5c648a.english: 68:29 Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; * and with the just let them not be written.

b0f47442250fd8b5c56b.latin: 68:30 Ego sum pauper et dolens: * salus tua, Deus, suscépit me.
b0f47442250fd8b5c56b.english: 68:30 I am poor and sorrowful: * thy salvation, O God, hath set me up.

c9dc51a7de6bb3df0bfa.latin: 68:31 Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico: * et magnificábo eum in laude:
c9dc51a7de6bb3df0bfa.english: 68:31 I will praise the name of God with a canticle: * and I will magnify him with praise.

80baa70a30823651aab4.latin: 68:32 Et placébit Deo super vítulum novéllum: * córnua producéntem et úngulas.
80baa70a30823651aab4.english: 68:32 And it shall please God better than a young calf, * that bringeth forth horns and hoofs.

a82a94e4d2cfeb2dff74.latin: 68:33 Vídeant páuperes et læténtur: * quǽrite Deum, et vivet ánima vestra.
a82a94e4d2cfeb2dff74.english: 68:33 Let the poor see and rejoice: * seek ye God, and your soul shall live.

2c9a6503733e07b0a2fe.latin: 68:34 Quóniam exaudívit páuperes Dóminus: * et vinctos suos non despéxit.
2c9a6503733e07b0a2fe.english: 68:34 For the Lord hath heard the poor: * and hath not despised his prisoners.

b3c006550d6cd0023114.latin: 68:35 Laudent illum cæli et terra, * mare et ómnia reptília in eis.
b3c006550d6cd0023114.english: 68:35 Let the heavens and the earth praise him; * the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein.

8f059bea5cbd9a6be4f3.latin: 68:36 Quóniam Deus salvam fáciet Sion: * et ædificabúntur civitátes Iuda.
8f059bea5cbd9a6be4f3.english: 68:36 For God will save Sion, * and the cities of Juda shall be built up.

35a0d3148294d4d5b744.latin: 68:36 Et inhabitábunt ibi, * et hereditáte acquírent eam.
35a0d3148294d4d5b744.english: 68:36 And they shall dwell there, * and acquire it by inheritance.

9060e111676b5d91d36a.latin: 68:37 Et semen servórum eius possidébit eam: * et qui díligunt nomen eius, habitábunt in ea.
9060e111676b5d91d36a.english: 68:37 And the seed of his servants shall possess it; * and they that love his name shall dwell therein.

a25650c072cbad19d49b.latin: 69:2 Deus, in adiutórium meum inténde: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
a25650c072cbad19d49b.english: 69:2 O God, come to my assistance; * O Lord, make haste to help me.

8d42b3efc13ce7cb7081.latin: 69:3 Confundántur et revereántur, * qui quærunt ánimam meam.
8d42b3efc13ce7cb7081.english: 69:3 Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek my soul:

09f2deebe05577a9793b.latin: 69:4 Avertántur retrórsum, et erubéscant, * qui volunt mihi mala.
09f2deebe05577a9793b.english: 69:4 Let them be turned backward, and blush for shame * that desire evils to me:

bf2f8f569adac3208930.latin: 69:4 Avertántur statim erubescéntes, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
bf2f8f569adac3208930.english: 69:4 Let them be presently turned away blushing for shame * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

66213aebb29683301fde.latin: 69:5 Exsúltent et læténtur in te omnes qui quærunt te, * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
66213aebb29683301fde.english: 69:5 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

4e4f7ce0b869aee18134.latin: 69:6 Ego vero egénus, et pauper sum: * Deus, ádiuva me.
4e4f7ce0b869aee18134.english: 69:6 But I am needy and poor; * O God, help me.

3a5d9fc578360f9efebc.latin: 69:6 Adiútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu: * Dómine, ne moréris.
3a5d9fc578360f9efebc.english: 69:6 Thou art my helper and my deliverer: * O Lord, make no delay.

7a05897847ebeb749ebd.latin: 70:1 In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me, et éripe me.
7a05897847ebeb749ebd.english: 70:1 In thee, O Lord, I have hoped, let me never be put to confusion: * deliver me in thy justice, and rescue me.

677a089f7ef68f94aec0.latin: 70:2 Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * et salva me.
677a089f7ef68f94aec0.english: 70:2 Incline thy ear unto me, * and save me.

7c872596e70072caeb4c.latin: 70:3 Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in locum munítum: * ut salvum me fácias,
7c872596e70072caeb4c.english: 70:3 Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength: * that thou mayst make me safe.

3651030e6e7818705b76.latin: 70:3 Quóniam firmaméntum meum, * et refúgium meum es tu.
3651030e6e7818705b76.english: 70:3 For thou art my firmament * and my refuge.

d148fa10c2063f9ffd1f.latin: 70:4 Deus meus, éripe me de manu peccatóris, * et de manu contra legem agéntis et iníqui:
d148fa10c2063f9ffd1f.english: 70:4 Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the sinner, * and out of the hand of the transgressor of the law and of the unjust.

6958bd31a13f9fd7003e.latin: 70:5 Quóniam tu es patiéntia mea, Dómine: * Dómine, spes mea a iuventúte mea.
6958bd31a13f9fd7003e.english: 70:5 For thou art my patience, O Lord: * my hope, O Lord, from my youth.

efd3857c3f23f79527a8.latin: 70:6 In te confirmátus sum ex útero: * de ventre matris meæ tu es protéctor meus.
efd3857c3f23f79527a8.english: 70:6 By thee have I been confirmed from the womb: * from my mother’s womb thou art my protector.

077cb7c64847f36fdfdb.latin: 70:7 In te cantátio mea semper: * tamquam prodígium factus sum multis: et tu adiútor fortis.
077cb7c64847f36fdfdb.english: 70:7 Of thee shall I continually sing: * I am become unto many as a wonder, but thou art a strong helper.

84747fbe79ba92d416af.latin: 70:8 Repleátur os meum laude, ut cantem glóriam tuam: * tota die magnitúdinem tuam.
84747fbe79ba92d416af.english: 70:8 Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may sing thy glory; * thy greatness all the day long.

06c978137f019ff4dc24.latin: 70:9 Ne proícias me in témpore senectútis: * cum defécerit virtus mea, ne derelínquas me.
06c978137f019ff4dc24.english: 70:9 Cast me not off in the time of old age: * when my strength shall fail, do not thou forsake me.

115cf88a9ae963dfed57.latin: 70:10 Quia dixérunt inimíci mei mihi: * et qui custodiébant ánimam meam, consílium fecérunt in unum.
115cf88a9ae963dfed57.english: 70:10 For my enemies have spoken against me; * and they that watched my soul have consulted together,

e461c3db5e3aa27d53ca.latin: 70:11 Dicéntes: Deus derelíquit eum, persequímini, et comprehéndite eum: * quia non est qui erípiat.
e461c3db5e3aa27d53ca.english: 70:11 Saying: God hath forsaken him: pursue and take him, * for there is none to deliver him.

6ef049e99a93514227f7.latin: 70:12 Deus, ne elongéris a me: * Deus meus, in auxílium meum réspice.
6ef049e99a93514227f7.english: 70:12 O God, be not thou far from me: * O my God, make haste to my help.

b4dbf1220807777c28ac.latin: 70:13 Confundántur, et defíciant detrahéntes ánimæ meæ: * operiántur confusióne, et pudóre qui quærunt mala mihi.
b4dbf1220807777c28ac.english: 70:13 Let them be confounded and come to nothing that detract my soul; * let them be covered with confusion and shame that seek my hurt.

fe02029c405c974df232.latin: 70:14 Ego autem semper sperábo: * et adíciam super omnem laudem tuam.
fe02029c405c974df232.english: 70:14 But I will always hope; * and will add to all thy praise.

c21012316c42f5eea5bc.latin: 70:15 Os meum annuntiábit iustítiam tuam: * tota die salutáre tuum.
c21012316c42f5eea5bc.english: 70:15 My mouth shall shew forth thy justice; * thy salvation all the day long.

f3fa230a121d4db140c3.latin: 70:16 Quóniam non cognóvi litteratúram, introíbo in poténtias Dómini: * Dómine, memorábor iustítiæ tuæ solíus.
f3fa230a121d4db140c3.english: 70:16 Because I have not known learning, I will enter into the powers of the Lord: * O Lord, I will be mindful of thy justice alone.

04e6625b35ff50dcf808.latin: 70:17 Deus, docuísti me a iuventúte mea: * et usque nunc pronuntiábo mirabília tua.
04e6625b35ff50dcf808.english: 70:17 Thou hast taught me, O God, from my youth: * and till now I will declare thy wonderful works.

c23b5cdc9a2f1f18726a.latin: 70:18 Et usque in senéctam et sénium: * Deus, ne derelínquas me,
c23b5cdc9a2f1f18726a.english: 70:18 And unto old age and grey hairs: * O God, forsake me not,

5d42633efcc9c79e3bd5.latin: 70:18 Donec annúntiem brácchium tuum * generatióni omni, quæ ventúra est:
5d42633efcc9c79e3bd5.english: 70:18 Until I shew forth thy arm * to all the generation that is to come:

83c5ced9717da7fbf795.latin: 70:19 Poténtiam tuam, et iustítiam tuam, Deus, usque in altíssima, quæ fecísti magnália: * Deus, quis símilis tibi?
83c5ced9717da7fbf795.english: 70:19 Thy power, and thy justice, O God, even to the highest great things thou hast done: * O God, who is like to thee?

61377617cadde51c01f0.latin: 70:20 Quantas ostendísti mihi tribulatiónes multas et malas: et convérsus vivificásti me: * et de abýssis terræ íterum reduxísti me:
61377617cadde51c01f0.english: 70:20 How great troubles hast thou shewn me, many and grievous: and turning thou hast brought me to life, * and hast brought me back again from the depths of the earth:

4afb6ef662296122a690.latin: 70:21 Multiplicásti magnificéntiam tuam: * et convérsus consolátus es me.
4afb6ef662296122a690.english: 70:21 Thou hast multiplied thy magnificence; * and turning to me thou hast comforted me.

7e3c6c70a46892baddf0.latin: 70:22 Nam et ego confitébor tibi in vasis psalmi veritátem tuam: * Deus, psallam tibi in cíthara, Sanctus Israël.
7e3c6c70a46892baddf0.english: 70:22 For I will also confess to thee thy truth with the instruments of psaltery: * O God, I will sing to thee with the harp,

a4a1f376a24befaf1853.latin: 70:23 Exsultábunt lábia mea cum cantávero tibi: * et ánima mea, quam redemísti.
a4a1f376a24befaf1853.english: 70:23 My lips shall greatly rejoice, when I shall sing to thee; * and my soul which thou hast redeemed.

849f634d33e45a324234.latin: 70:24 Sed et lingua mea tota die meditábitur iustítiam tuam: * cum confúsi et revériti fúerint, qui quærunt mala mihi.
849f634d33e45a324234.english: 70:24 Yea and my tongue shall meditate on thy justice all the day; * when they shall be confounded and put to shame that seek evils to me.

e2b34de950d96ef9c15c.latin: 71:2 Deus, iudícium tuum regi da: * et iustítiam tuam fílio regis:
e2b34de950d96ef9c15c.english: 71:2 Give to the king thy judgment, O God: * and to the king’s son thy justice:

916a2142d53b0f00e2a0.latin: 71:2 Iudicáre pópulum tuum in iustítia, * et páuperes tuos in iudício.
916a2142d53b0f00e2a0.english: 71:2 To judge thy people with justice, * and thy poor with judgment.

e0aad75a75b0a126a6be.latin: 71:3 Suscípiant montes pacem pópulo: * et colles iustítiam.
e0aad75a75b0a126a6be.english: 71:3 Let the mountains receive peace for the people: * and the hills justice.

b5858c799d3975679aa9.latin: 71:4 Iudicábit páuperes pópuli, et salvos fáciet fílios páuperum: * et humiliábit calumniatórem.
b5858c799d3975679aa9.english: 71:4 He shall judge the poor of the people, and he shall save the children of the poor: * and he shall humble the oppressor.

f70b530d291fccc75b25.latin: 71:5 Et permanébit cum sole, et ante lunam, * in generatióne et generatiónem.
f70b530d291fccc75b25.english: 71:5 And he shall continue with the sun, and before the moon, * throughout all generations.

e15db267d9987f01c268.latin: 71:6 Descéndet sicut plúvia in vellus: * et sicut stillicídia stillántia super terram.
e15db267d9987f01c268.english: 71:6 He shall come down like rain upon the fleece; * and as showers falling gently upon the earth.

a8581c68177a3ac1b14d.latin: 71:7 Oriétur in diébus eius iustítia, et abundántia pacis: * donec auferátur luna.
a8581c68177a3ac1b14d.english: 71:7 In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace, * till the moon be taken away.

b48ee8231616503aba8c.latin: 71:8 Et dominábitur a mari usque ad mare: * et a flúmine usque ad términos orbis terrárum.
b48ee8231616503aba8c.english: 71:8 And he shall rule from sea to sea, * and from the river unto the ends of the earth.

25404b12093489d05000.latin: 71:9 Coram illo prócident Æthíopes: * et inimíci eius terram lingent.
25404b12093489d05000.english: 71:9 Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down: * and his enemies shall lick the ground.

68221828b7a67c8274da.latin: 71:10 Reges Tharsis, et ínsulæ múnera ófferent: * reges Árabum et Saba dona addúcent.
68221828b7a67c8274da.english: 71:10 The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents: * the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall bring gifts:

e8994758907748c59876.latin: 71:11 Et adorábunt eum omnes reges terræ: * omnes gentes sérvient ei:
e8994758907748c59876.english: 71:11 And all kings of the earth shall adore him: * all nations shall serve him.

612988344a7858e1f24c.latin: 71:12 Quia liberábit páuperem a poténte: * et páuperem, cui non erat adiútor.
612988344a7858e1f24c.english: 71:12 For he shall deliver the poor from the mighty: * and the needy that had no helper.

d7f8799fb943c6273fca.latin: 71:13 Parcet páuperi et ínopi: * et ánimas páuperum salvas fáciet.
d7f8799fb943c6273fca.english: 71:13 He shall spare the poor and needy: * and he shall save the souls of the poor.

c072cd6f9cb8feb5590d.latin: 71:14 Ex usúris et iniquitáte rédimet ánimas eórum: * et honorábile nomen eórum coram illo.
c072cd6f9cb8feb5590d.english: 71:14 He shall redeem their souls from usuries and iniquity: * and their names shall be honourable in his sight.

1757d1b8c3792ed9b6bd.latin: 71:15 Et vivet, et dábitur ei de auro Arábiæ, et adorábunt de ipso semper: * tota die benedícent ei.
1757d1b8c3792ed9b6bd.english: 71:15 And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Arabia, for him they shall always adore: * they shall bless him all the day.

3323e2204541d9fbcf3e.latin: 71:16 Et erit firmaméntum in terra in summis móntium, superextollétur super Líbanum fructus eius: * et florébunt de civitáte sicut fænum terræ.
3323e2204541d9fbcf3e.english: 71:16 And there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains, above Libanus shall the fruit thereof be exalted: * and they of the city shall flourish like the grass of the earth.

81f32bcc8bdc4ca9b038.latin: 71:17 Sit nomen eius benedíctum in sǽcula: * ante solem pérmanet nomen eius.
81f32bcc8bdc4ca9b038.english: 71:17 Let his name be blessed for evermore: * his name continueth before the sun.

06f09fd9972c85a11691.latin: 71:17 Et benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ: * omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
06f09fd9972c85a11691.english: 71:17 And in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: * all nations shall magnify him.

b8b1dbceace4564f9d70.latin: 71:18 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, * qui facit mirabília solus:
b8b1dbceace4564f9d70.english: 71:18 Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, * who alone doth wonderful things.

2d6d9115d0d021c33ee3.latin: 71:19 Et benedíctum nomen maiestátis eius in ætérnum: * et replébitur maiestáte eius omnis terra: fiat, fiat.
2d6d9115d0d021c33ee3.english: 71:19 And blessed be the name of his majesty for ever: * and the whole earth shall be filled with his majesty. So be it. So be it.

c480a8f207b34b040f2c.latin: 72:1 Quam bonus Israël Deus, * his, qui recto sunt corde!
c480a8f207b34b040f2c.english: 72:1 How good is God to Israel, * to them that are of a right heart!

8e18e1f5dde508237bcf.latin: 72:2 Mei autem pæne moti sunt pedes: * pæne effúsi sunt gressus mei.
8e18e1f5dde508237bcf.english: 72:2 But my feet were almost moved; * my steps had wellnigh slipped.

2701c673eb07de09fdac.latin: 72:3 Quia zelávi super iníquos, * pacem peccatórum videns.
2701c673eb07de09fdac.english: 72:3 Because I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked, * seeing the prosperity of sinners.

a3a5fb2907d896425d6d.latin: 72:4 Quia non est respéctus morti eórum: * et firmaméntum in plaga eórum.
a3a5fb2907d896425d6d.english: 72:4 For there is no regard to their death, * nor is there strength in their stripes.

a9df36324374f13dff31.latin: 72:5 In labóre hóminum non sunt, * et cum homínibus non flagellabúntur:
a9df36324374f13dff31.english: 72:5 They are not in the labour of men: * neither shall they be scourged like other men.

ae5f2b8e25ebefb5d7f1.latin: 72:6 Ídeo ténuit eos supérbia, * opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua.
ae5f2b8e25ebefb5d7f1.english: 72:6 Therefore pride hath held them fast: * they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness.

7314de3e2cb729a8edcd.latin: 72:7 Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum: * transiérunt in afféctum cordis.
7314de3e2cb729a8edcd.english: 72:7 Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: * they have passed into the affection of the heart.

4ba82d6af8f875374f75.latin: 72:8 Cogitavérunt, et locúti sunt nequítiam: * iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.
4ba82d6af8f875374f75.english: 72:8 They have thought and spoken wickedness: * they have spoken iniquity on high.

c9258d07c1a01f694209.latin: 72:9 Posuérunt in cælum os suum: * et lingua eórum transívit in terra.
c9258d07c1a01f694209.english: 72:9 They have set their mouth against heaven: * and their tongue hath passed through the earth.

ab1aea53f45c8fc0ff69.latin: 72:10 Ídeo convertétur pópulus meus hic: * et dies pleni inveniéntur in eis.
ab1aea53f45c8fc0ff69.english: 72:10 Therefore will my people return here * and full days shall be found in them.

bab4dd0446e131a72f60.latin: 72:11 Et dixérunt: Quómodo scit Deus, * et si est sciéntia in excélso?
bab4dd0446e131a72f60.english: 72:11 And they said: How doth God know? * and is there knowledge in the most High?

e8f6cc19bd0ab87ff512.latin: 72:12 Ecce, ipsi peccatóres, et abundántes in sǽculo, * obtinuérunt divítias.
e8f6cc19bd0ab87ff512.english: 72:12 Behold these are sinners; and yet abounding in the world * they have obtained riches.

66ded91d343811f2b71d.latin: 72:13 Et dixi: Ergo sine causa iustificávi cor meum, * et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas:
66ded91d343811f2b71d.english: 72:13 And I said: Then have I in vain justified my heart, * and washed my hands among the innocent.

e5395ad809138bdc00f1.latin: 72:14 Et fui flagellátus tota die, * et castigátio mea in matutínis.
e5395ad809138bdc00f1.english: 72:14 And I have been scourged all the day; * and my chastisement hath been in the mornings.

97204ed62275e083d577.latin: 72:15 Si dicébam: Narrábo sic: * ecce, natiónem filiórum tuórum reprobávi.
97204ed62275e083d577.english: 72:15 If I said: I will speak thus; * behold I should condemn the generation of thy children.

f23606c9d8495bf89904.latin: 72:16 Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc, * labor est ante me:
f23606c9d8495bf89904.english: 72:16 I studied that I might know this thing, * it is a labour in my sight:

58acafbb7ce5f04bbab6.latin: 72:17 Donec intrem in Sanctuárium Dei: * et intéllegam in novíssimis eórum.
58acafbb7ce5f04bbab6.english: 72:17 Until I go into the sanctuary of God, * and understand concerning their last ends.

8ab1744d370498faa506.latin: 72:18 Verúmtamen propter dolos posuísti eis: * deiecísti eos dum allevaréntur.
8ab1744d370498faa506.english: 72:18 But indeed for deceits thou hast put it to them: * when they were lifted up, thou hast cast them down.

f26c4d0de302bbeb925c.latin: 72:19 Quómodo facti sunt in desolatiónem, súbito defecérunt: * periérunt propter iniquitátem suam.
f26c4d0de302bbeb925c.english: 72:19 How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: * they have perished by reason of their iniquity.

aa1b88bab88671969042.latin: 72:20 Velut sómnium surgéntium, Dómine, * in civitáte tua imáginem ipsórum ad níhilum rédiges.
aa1b88bab88671969042.english: 72:20 As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; * so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing.

f984e62a0c6b718d8d16.latin: 72:21 Quia inflammátum est cor meum, et renes mei commutáti sunt: * et ego ad níhilum redáctus sum, et nescívi.
f984e62a0c6b718d8d16.english: 72:21 For my heart hath been inflamed, and my reins have been changed: * and I am brought to nothing, and I knew not.

4a620e47b2b280ffa583.latin: 72:23 Ut iuméntum factus sum apud te: * et ego semper tecum.
4a620e47b2b280ffa583.english: 72:23 I am become as a beast before thee: * and I am always with thee.

4cc03c9099be7f57f95b.latin: 72:24 Tenuísti manum déxteram meam: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me, * et cum glória suscepísti me.
4cc03c9099be7f57f95b.english: 72:24 Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me, * and with thy glory thou hast received me.

4e80bf9827cf1097b383.latin: 72:25 Quid enim mihi est in cælo? * et a te quid vólui super terram?
4e80bf9827cf1097b383.english: 72:25 For what have I in heaven? * and besides thee what do I desire upon earth?

f2c4857ad44179fefe0e.latin: 72:26 Defécit caro mea, et cor meum: * Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.
f2c4857ad44179fefe0e.english: 72:26 For thee my flesh and my heart hath fainted away: * thou art the God of my heart, and the God that is my portion for ever.

f97d6e06511b5571b961.latin: 72:27 Quia ecce, qui elóngant se a te, períbunt: * perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te.
f97d6e06511b5571b961.english: 72:27 For behold they that go far from thee shall perish: * thou hast destroyed all them that are disloyal to thee.

f4310e30e9faecee41b7.latin: 72:28 Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: * pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam:
f4310e30e9faecee41b7.english: 72:28 But it is good for me to adhere to my God, * to put my hope in the Lord God:

b228ce2649bae2df4ea4.latin: 72:28 Ut annúntiem omnes prædicatiónes tuas, * in portis fíliæ Sion.
b228ce2649bae2df4ea4.english: 72:28 That I may declare all thy praises, * in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

d03347791ed3fb4a18ad.latin:
Sir 39:19
Floréte flores quasi lílium et date odórem et frondéte in grátiam; collaudáte cánticum et benedícite Dóminum in opéribus suis.
℟. Deo grátias.
℣. Post partum, Virgo, invioláta permansísti.
℟. Dei Génetrix, intercéde pro nobis.
d03347791ed3fb4a18ad.english:
Sir 39:19
Send forth flowers, as the lily, and yield a smell, and bring forth leaves in grace, and praise with canticles, and bless the Lord in his works.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℣. After childbirth thou still remainest a virgin.
℟. Mother of God, pray for us.

56a9969b58805b77cd83.latin: Deus, cuius Unigénitus per vitam, mortem et resurrectiónem suam nobis salútis ætérnæ prǽmia comparávit: concéde, quǽsumus; ut hæc mystéria sacratíssimo beátæ Maríæ Vírginis Rosário recoléntes, et imitémur quod cóntinent, et quod promíttunt, assequámur.
56a9969b58805b77cd83.english: O God, Whose only-begotten Son, by His life, death and resurrection, has merited for us the grace of eternal salvation, grant, we beseech You, that, meditating upon those mysteries in the most holy Rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary, we may imitate what they contain and obtain what they promise.

d232d2a865c48d01ea43.latin: Per eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
d232d2a865c48d01ea43.english: Through the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

9a52bab5f3df40985034.latin: Ant. Lætáre, * Virgo Mater; surréxit Christus de sepúlcro.
9a52bab5f3df40985034.english: Ant. Rejoice, O Virgin Mother, * Christ is risen from the grave.

83748c41182e49de9571.latin: Ant. Lætáre, Virgo Mater; surréxit Christus de sepúlcro.
83748c41182e49de9571.english: Ant. Rejoice, O Virgin Mother, Christ is risen from the grave.

af965b9d188ee93272f8.latin: Ant. Ascéndit Deus * in iubilatióne, et Dóminus in voce tubæ.
af965b9d188ee93272f8.english: Ant. God is gone up with a shout, * and the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.

121d015d694180f7d254.latin: Ant. Ascéndit Deus in iubilatióne, et Dóminus in voce tubæ.
121d015d694180f7d254.english: Ant. God is gone up with a shout, and the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.

1800ab35183598e189ff.latin: Ant. Spíritus Dómini * replévit orbem terrárum.
1800ab35183598e189ff.english: Ant. The spirit of the Lord * hath filled the world.

9aec8d80ea29bfa36436.latin: Ant. Spíritus Dómini replévit orbem terrárum.
9aec8d80ea29bfa36436.english: Ant. The spirit of the Lord hath filled the world.

378b77412b1df8c6ae2a.latin: Ant. Assúmpta est * María in cælum: gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum, allelúia.
378b77412b1df8c6ae2a.english: Ant. Mary hath been taken to heaven. * The angels rejoice; they praise and bless the Lord. Alleluia.

10b9d515833d3f3b4fff.latin: Ant. Assúmpta est María in cælum: gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum, allelúia.
10b9d515833d3f3b4fff.english: Ant. Mary hath been taken to heaven. The angels rejoice; they praise and bless the Lord. Alleluia.

4d625e15c2a46865a1f2.latin: Ant. Exaltáta est * Virgo María super choros Angelórum, et in cápite eius coróna stellárum duódecim.
4d625e15c2a46865a1f2.english: Ant. The Virgin Mary * hath been exalted over choirs of angels, and upon her head there is a crown of twelve stars.

e238d0862cd75c39477f.latin: Ant. Exaltáta est Virgo María super choros Angelórum, et in cápite eius coróna stellárum duódecim.
e238d0862cd75c39477f.english: Ant. The Virgin Mary hath been exalted over choirs of angels, and upon her head there is a crown of twelve stars.

8387f9671afbeb6deddd.latin:
Sir 24:25; 39:17
In me grátia omnis viæ et veritátis, in me omnis spes vitæ et virtútis. Ego, quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum, fructificávi.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟.br. Speciósa facta es * Et suávis.
℟. Speciósa facta es * Et suávis.
℣. In delíciis tuis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
℟. Et suávis.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Speciósa facta es * Et suávis.
Hymnus
Iam morte, victor, óbruta,
Ab ínferis Christus redit,
Fractísque culpæ vínculis,
Cæli reclúdit límina.
Visus satis mortálibus
Ascéndit ad cæléstia,
Dextrǽque Patris ássidet
Consors patérnæ glóriæ.
Quem iam suis promíserat,
Sanctum datúrus Spíritum,
Linguis amóris ígneis
Mæstis alúmnis ímpluit.
Solúta carnis póndere
Ad astra Virgo tóllitur,
Excépta cæli iúbilo
Et Angelórum cánticis.
Bis sena cingunt sídera
Almæ paréntis vérticem:
Throno propínqua Fílii
Cunctis creátis ímperat.
Glória tibi, Dómine,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
℣. Elégit eam Deus, et præelégit eam.
℟. Et habitáre eam fecit in tabernáculo suo.
8387f9671afbeb6deddd.english:
Sir 24:25; 39:17
In me is all grace of the way and of the truth; in me is all hope of life and virtue; I have flowered forth like a rose planted by the brooks of water.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟.br. O Holy * Mother of God.
℟. O Holy * Mother of God.
℣. Thou art become beautiful and gentle in thy gladness.
℟. Mother of God.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. O Holy * Mother of God.
Hymn
Now Christ, the conqueror of death,
Breaks sin's enslaving chain,
And rising from the tomb returns,
And opens heaven again.
Awhile beheld by mortal men,
He rises from their sight;
Ascending to the Father's throne,
He reigns in equal light.
His promised gift unto his own
He sends forth from above,
And rains the Holy Spirit down
In fiery tongues of love.
The Virgin, freed of mortal weight,
Is borne than stars yet higher,
And with glad melody is hailed
By each angelic choir.
Our Mother's gentle brow now shines
With crown in starry sheen,
As nigh her Son, in light enthroned,
She reigns creation's Queen.
O Jesu, born of Virgin bright,
All glory be to thee,
With Father and with Paraclete,
Through all eternity.
Amen.
℣. God hath chosen her and forechosen her,
℟. And hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.

8761d4a922dde52358c9.latin: Ant. Solemnitátem hodiérnam * sacratíssimi Rosárii Genetrícis Dei Maríæ devóte celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Iesum Christum.
8761d4a922dde52358c9.english: Ant. Let us this day keep * right heartily the solemn Feast of the Most Holy Rosary of Mary the Mother of God, that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

f7bc9a8cd6e75e464523.latin: Ant. Solemnitátem hodiérnam sacratíssimi Rosárii Genetrícis Dei Maríæ devóte celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Iesum Christum.
f7bc9a8cd6e75e464523.english: Ant. Let us this day keep right heartily the solemn Feast of the Most Holy Rosary of Mary the Mother of God, that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

9ebbbb9aa224ecf37f4f.latin: 9:20 Exsúrge, Dómine, non confortétur homo: * iudicéntur gentes in conspéctu tuo.
9ebbbb9aa224ecf37f4f.english: 9:20 Arise, O Lord, let not man be strengthened: * let the Gentiles be judged in thy sight.

b37088fccc28ee381f94.latin: 9:21 Constítue, Dómine, legislatórem super eos: * ut sciant gentes quóniam hómines sunt.
b37088fccc28ee381f94.english: 9:21 Appoint, O Lord, a lawgiver over them: * that the Gentiles may know themselves to be but men.

fe3794c87be98d355425.latin: 9:22 Ut quid, Dómine, recessísti longe, * déspicis in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne?
fe3794c87be98d355425.english: 9:22 Why, O Lord, hast thou retired afar off? * why dost thou slight us in our wants, in the time of trouble?

e8e72e3c504fd589a94e.latin: 9:23 Dum supérbit ímpius, incénditur pauper: * comprehendúntur in consíliis quibus cógitant.
e8e72e3c504fd589a94e.english: 9:23 Whilst the wicked man is proud, the poor is set on fire: * they are caught in the counsels which they devise.

8fff1189f5d969d2f524.latin: 9:24 Quóniam laudátur peccátor in desidériis ánimæ suæ: * et iníquus benedícitur.
8fff1189f5d969d2f524.english: 9:24 For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul: * and the unjust man is blessed.

625e3ad2261fac5c5bcf.latin: 9:25 Exacerbávit Dóminum peccátor, * secúndum multitúdinem iræ suæ non quæret.
625e3ad2261fac5c5bcf.english: 9:25 The sinner hath provoked the Lord, * according to the multitude of his wrath he will not seek him.

1e523376ef216f0872ce.latin: 9:26 Non est Deus in conspéctu eius: * inquinátæ sunt viæ illíus in omni témpore.
1e523376ef216f0872ce.english: 9:26 God is not before his eyes: * his ways are filthy at all times.

d5e86545d97a02b6ff44.latin: 9:26 Auferúntur iudícia tua a fácie eius: * ómnium inimicórum suórum dominábitur.
d5e86545d97a02b6ff44.english: 9:26 Thy judgments are removed from his sight: * he shall rule over all his enemies.

cf4bf2af94fc97c4284f.latin: 9:27 Dixit enim in corde suo: * Non movébor a generatióne in generatiónem sine malo.
cf4bf2af94fc97c4284f.english: 9:27 For he hath said in his heart: * I shall not be moved from generation to generation, and shall be without evil.

8b907308c05216237f89.latin: 9:28 Cuius maledictióne os plenum est, et amaritúdine, et dolo: * sub lingua eius labor et dolor.
8b907308c05216237f89.english: 9:28 His mouth is full of cursing, and of bitterness, and of deceit: * under his tongue are labour and sorrow.

b97d51cb072855723f2a.latin: 9:29 Sedet in insídiis cum divítibus in occúltis: * ut interfíciat innocéntem.
b97d51cb072855723f2a.english: 9:29 He sitteth in ambush with the rich, in private places, * that he may kill the innocent.

be7d6327a1b40bcb6a07.latin: 9:30 Óculi eius in páuperem respíciunt: * insidiátur in abscóndito, quasi leo in spelúnca sua.
be7d6327a1b40bcb6a07.english: 9:30 His eyes are upon the poor man: * he lieth in wait, in secret, like a lion in his den.

5a48cb19b54632c95e63.latin: 9:30 Insidiátur ut rápiat páuperem: * rápere páuperem, dum áttrahit eum.
5a48cb19b54632c95e63.english: 9:30 He lieth in ambush, that he may catch the poor man: * so catch the poor, whilst he draweth him to him.

e5ddb921c1ab0c322abf.latin: 9:31 In láqueo suo humiliábit eum: * inclinábit se, et cadet, cum dominátus fúerit páuperum.
e5ddb921c1ab0c322abf.english: 9:31 In his net he will bring him down, * he will crouch and fall, when he shall have power over the poor.

82f4a7961568352c13b8.latin: 9:32 Dixit enim in corde suo: Oblítus est Deus, * avértit fáciem suam ne vídeat in finem.
82f4a7961568352c13b8.english: 9:32 For he hath said in his heart: God hath forgotten, * he hath turned away his face, not to see to the end.

c7daa538bf434020a28c.latin: 9:33 Exsúrge, Dómine Deus, exaltétur manus tua: * ne obliviscáris páuperum.
c7daa538bf434020a28c.english: 9:33 Arise, O Lord God, let thy hand be exalted: * forget not the poor.

cb7d809ad293f2fa2b7d.latin: 9:34 Propter quid irritávit ímpius Deum? * dixit enim in corde suo: Non requíret.
cb7d809ad293f2fa2b7d.english: 9:34 Wherefore hath the wicked provoked God? * for he hath said in his heart: He will not require it.

004be632b285858f660d.latin: 9:35 Vides quóniam tu labórem et dolórem consíderas: * ut tradas eos in manus tuas.
004be632b285858f660d.english: 9:35 Thou seest it, for thou considerest labour and sorrow: * that thou mayst deliver them into thy hands.

7b3dbb6f0f0c5f2be1c7.latin: 9:35 Tibi derelíctus est pauper: * órphano tu eris adiútor.
7b3dbb6f0f0c5f2be1c7.english: 9:35 To thee is the poor man left: * thou wilt be a helper to the orphan.

9e6cd404d3433c341199.latin: 9:36 Cóntere brácchium peccatóris et malígni: * quærétur peccátum illíus, et non inveniétur.
9e6cd404d3433c341199.english: 9:36 Break thou the arm of the sinner and of the malignant: * his sin shall be sought, and shall not be found.

34e6fb7c0b80c25a26b6.latin: 9:37 Dóminus regnábit in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * períbitis, gentes, de terra illíus.
34e6fb7c0b80c25a26b6.english: 9:37 The Lord shall reign to eternity, yea, for ever and ever: * ye Gentiles shall perish from his land.

ad193189faaa493240bf.latin: 9:38 Desidérium páuperum exaudívit Dóminus: * præparatiónem cordis eórum audívit auris tua.
ad193189faaa493240bf.english: 9:38 The Lord hath heard the desire of the poor: * thy ear hath heard the preparation of their heart.

6ee190f37f1186408d3d.latin: 9:39 Iudicáre pupíllo et húmili, * ut non appónat ultra magnificáre se homo super terram.
6ee190f37f1186408d3d.english: 9:39 To judge for the fatherless and for the humble, * that man may no more presume to magnify himself upon earth.

61cf77ecb043c6f70528.latin: 10:2 In Dómino confído: quómodo dícitis ánimæ meæ: * Tránsmigra in montem sicut passer?
61cf77ecb043c6f70528.english: 10:2 In the Lord I put my trust: how then do you say to my soul: * Get thee away from hence to the mountain, like a sparrow?

ab21baa24b9935a4272c.latin: 10:3 Quóniam ecce peccatóres intendérunt arcum, paravérunt sagíttas suas in pháretra, * ut sagíttent in obscúro rectos corde.
ab21baa24b9935a4272c.english: 10:3 For, lo, the wicked have bent their bow: they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, * to shoot in the dark the upright of heart.

cebd1cd7899c3e7a39b8.latin: 10:4 Quóniam quæ perfecísti, destruxérunt: * iustus autem quid fecit?
cebd1cd7899c3e7a39b8.english: 10:4 For they have destroyed the things which thou hast made: * but what has the just man done?

8aa96dfcbfcb98c475b0.latin: 10:5 Dóminus in templo sancto suo, * Dóminus in cælo sedes eius.
8aa96dfcbfcb98c475b0.english: 10:5 The Lord is in his holy temple, * the Lord’s throne is in heaven.

dd4fe2791dda68255c1b.latin: 10:5 Óculi eius in páuperem respíciunt: * pálpebræ eius intérrogant fílios hóminum.
dd4fe2791dda68255c1b.english: 10:5 His eyes look on the poor man: * his eyelids examine the sons of men.

a8555225e00f77bbd22b.latin: 10:6 Dóminus intérrogat iustum et ímpium: * qui autem díligit iniquitátem, odit ánimam suam.
a8555225e00f77bbd22b.english: 10:6 The Lord trieth the just and the wicked: * but he that loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul.

c33740d6cfef64ed2167.latin: 10:7 Pluet super peccatóres láqueos: * ignis, et sulphur, et spíritus procellárum pars cálicis eórum.
c33740d6cfef64ed2167.english: 10:7 He shall rain snares upon sinners: * fire and brimstone, and storms of winds, shall be the portion of their cup.

44691db8e70190a97cab.latin: 10:8 Quóniam iustus Dóminus, et iustítias diléxit: * æquitátem vidit vultus eius.
44691db8e70190a97cab.english: 10:8 For the Lord is just, and hath loved justice: * his countenance hath beheld righteousness.

0f7151f6aef3f3fcfc2d.latin: 11:2 Salvum me fac, Dómine, quóniam defécit sanctus: * quóniam diminútæ sunt veritátes a fíliis hóminum.
0f7151f6aef3f3fcfc2d.english: 11:2 Save me, O Lord, for there is now no saint: * truths are decayed from among the children of men.

93551197fd5b920aac45.latin: 11:3 Vana locúti sunt unusquísque ad próximum suum: * lábia dolósa, in corde et corde locúti sunt.
93551197fd5b920aac45.english: 11:3 They have spoken vain things every one to his neighbour: * with deceitful lips, and with a double heart have they spoken.

0f8a7d6d479cc84a0d58.latin: 11:4 Dispérdat Dóminus univérsa lábia dolósa, * et linguam magníloquam.
0f8a7d6d479cc84a0d58.english: 11:4 May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips, * and the tongue that speaketh proud things.

ad37f24f18e1408bed5c.latin: 11:5 Qui dixérunt: Linguam nostram magnificábimus, lábia nostra a nobis sunt, * quis noster Dóminus est?
ad37f24f18e1408bed5c.english: 11:5 Who have said: We will magnify our tongue; our lips are our own; * who is Lord over us?

9ec0c96a187376b10d5c.latin: 11:6 Propter misériam ínopum, et gémitum páuperum, * nunc exsúrgam, dicit Dóminus.
9ec0c96a187376b10d5c.english: 11:6 By reason of the misery of the needy, and the groans of the poor, * now will I arise, saith the Lord.

d238026bb254b682a09c.latin: 11:6 Ponam in salutári: * fiduciáliter agam in eo.
d238026bb254b682a09c.english: 11:6 I will set him in safety; * I will deal confidently in his regard.

d33751e4f47fed6b442b.latin: 11:7 Elóquia Dómini, elóquia casta: * argéntum igne examinátum, probátum terræ purgátum séptuplum.
d33751e4f47fed6b442b.english: 11:7 The words of the Lord are pure words: * as silver tried by the fire, purged from the earth, refined seven times.

385b7f15bd336d4a978c.latin: 11:8 Tu, Dómine, servábis nos: et custódies nos * a generatióne hac in ætérnum.
385b7f15bd336d4a978c.english: 11:8 Thou, O Lord, wilt preserve us: and keep us * from this generation for ever.

b66773e7acfdba13d2f5.latin: 11:9 In circúitu ímpii ámbulant: * secúndum altitúdinem tuam multiplicásti fílios hóminum.
b66773e7acfdba13d2f5.english: 11:9 The wicked walk round about: * according to thy highness, thou hast multiplied the children of men.

47104755577e0ba77ebe.latin: Octávo Idus Octóbris Luna vicésima sexta. Anno Dómini 2026
47104755577e0ba77ebe.english: October 8th 2026, the 26th day of the Moon,

2f3c8ba069844eca769b.latin: Sanctæ Birgíttæ Víduæ, cuius dies natális décimo Kaléndas Augústi, ac Translátio Nonis Octóbris recensétur.
2f3c8ba069844eca769b.english: On the 8th day of October we keep the Feast of the holy Widow Bridget, (Princess of Nericia.) After many pilgrimages to holy places she died at Rome, full of the Spirit of God, upon the 23rd day of July, (in the year 1373) But her body was taken to Sweden upon the 7th day of October.

fa23a70d88896caf57c7.latin: Eódem die natális beáti Simeónis senis, qui in Evangélio Dóminum Iesum, præsentátum in Templo, suis in ulnis accepísse ac de illo prophetásse légitur.
fa23a70d88896caf57c7.english: Upon the same 8th day of October, were born into the better life:

686a6dc98a2e513c5303.latin: Laodicéæ, in Phrýgia, sancti Artémonis Presbýteri, qui per ignem, sub Diocletiáno, martýrii corónam accépit.
686a6dc98a2e513c5303.english: The holy old man Simeon, of whom it is written in the Gospel that he took the Lord Jesus up in his arms.

6f2c7935ff9e801f99ed.latin: Thessalonícæ sancti Demétrii Procónsulis, qui, cum plúrimos ad Christi fidem perdúceret, ídeo, Maximiáni Imperatóris iussu lánceis confóssus, martýrium consummávit.
6f2c7935ff9e801f99ed.english: At Caesarea, in Palestine, the holy Virgin and martyr Reparata. Forasmuch as she would not offer sacrifice to idols, she was put to diverse torments, and then beheaded, under the Emperor Decius. Her soul was seen to leave her body and soar heavenward in a bodily shape like a dove.

08fa7e83edced5c06858.english: At Thessalonica, the holy Proconsul Demetrius, who brought many to believe in Christ, and was martyred by being pierced through with lances, by command of the Emperor Maximian. There also the holy martyr Nestor.

6e4dc153f9682fa4651c.latin: Híspali, in Hispánia, sancti Petri Mártyris.
6e4dc153f9682fa4651c.english: At Seville, in Spain, the holy martyr Peter.

7ac50b550a09c54c3063.latin: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, pássio sanctæ Reparátæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, cum nollet idólis sacrificáre, sub Décio Imperatóre, váriis tormentórum genéribus cruciátur, ac demum gládio percútitur. Ipsíus autem ánima, in colúmbæ spécie, de córpore égredi cælúmque conscéndere visa est.
7ac50b550a09c54c3063.english: At Laodicea, the holy Priest Artemon, who under the Emperor Diocletian received the crown of martyrdom by fire.

ddd7baf6336b4eb7e476.latin: In território Laudunénsi natális sanctæ Benedíctæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
ddd7baf6336b4eb7e476.english: In the country of Lyons, the holy Virgin and martyr Benedicta.

a793e47e8c2c67793276.latin: Ancónæ sanctárum Palatiátis et Lauréntiæ, quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Dióne Prǽside, in exsílium deportátæ, labóribus et ærúmnis conféctæ sunt.
a793e47e8c2c67793276.english: At Ancona, holy Palatias and Laurentia, who were carried into exile by command of the President Dion, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, and died of exhaustion and suffering.

2bef296b889badb0716a.latin: Rotómagi sancti Evódii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
2bef296b889badb0716a.english: At Rouen, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Evodius, Bishop (of that see.)

b8a0cd8f92959561a7de.english: At Jerusalem, (about the year 460,) holy Pelagia, surnamed the Penitent.

5b943222a489a99f5fd3.latin: Nonus humilitátis gradus est, si linguam ad loquéndum prohíbeat mónachus et taciturnitátem habens, usque ad interrogatiónem non loquátur, monstránte Scriptúra quia in multilóquio non effúgitur peccátum, et quia vir linguósus non dirígitur super terram.
5b943222a489a99f5fd3.english: The ninth step in humility is if a monk restrain his tongue from speaking so as to keep silence and not speak till questioned, the Scripture showing that: “In much speaking sin may not be avoided”; and that “the talkative man will not be guided aright in the world.”

36842629631eefc023cd.latin:
Sir 24:25; 39:17
In me grátia omnis viæ et veritátis, in me omnis spes vitæ et virtútis. Ego, quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum, fructificávi.
℟. Deo grátias.
℣. Sancta Dei Génetrix, semper Virgo María.
℟. Intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum.
36842629631eefc023cd.english:
Sir 24:25; 39:17
In me is all grace of the way and of the truth; in me is all hope of life and virtue; I have flowered forth like a rose planted by the brooks of water.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℣. Holy Mother of God, Mary, always a Virgin,
℟. Pray for us, unto the Lord our God.

88409c721aea39bbfb12.latin:
Sir 24:17-18
Quasi cedrus exaltáta sum in Líbano, et quasi cypréssus in monte Sion: quasi palma exaltáta sum in Cades, et quasi plantátio rosæ in Iéricho.
℟. Deo grátias.
℣. Speciósa facta es et suávis.
℟. In delíciis tuis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
88409c721aea39bbfb12.english:
Sir 24:17-28
I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree on mount Sion. I was exalted like a palm tree in Cades, and as a rose plant in Jericho.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℣. O holy Mother of God.
℟. Thou art become beautiful and gentle in thy gladness.

b25055b7b08797930461.latin: Ant. Quæ est ista, * speciósa sicut colúmba, quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum?
b25055b7b08797930461.english: Ant. Who is this, * fair as a dove, like a rose-tree planted beside the rivers of waters?

c22db55f090681fb25ac.latin: Ant. Quæ est ista, speciósa sicut colúmba, quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum?
c22db55f090681fb25ac.english: Ant. Who is this, fair as a dove, like a rose-tree planted beside the rivers of waters?

5f4910ae75bb312ed56b.latin: Ant. Virgo potens, * sicut turris David: mille clípei pendent ex ea, omnis armatúra fórtium.
5f4910ae75bb312ed56b.english: Ant. A virgin most mighty, * like the tower of David, whereon there hung a thousand bucklers, all the shields of valiant men.

4d74a6ec667e7d3ce700.latin: Ant. Virgo potens, sicut turris David: mille clípei pendent ex ea, omnis armatúra fórtium.
4d74a6ec667e7d3ce700.english: Ant. A virgin most mighty, like the tower of David, whereon there hung a thousand bucklers, all the shields of valiant men.

a2e1e43f32b1d7bf3e8a.latin: Ant. Ave, María, * grátia plena; Dóminus tecum: benedícta tu in muliéribus.
a2e1e43f32b1d7bf3e8a.english: Ant. Hail Mary, * full of grace, the Lord is with thee, blessed art thou among women.

20ffb35818daa53f472b.latin: Ant. Ave, María, grátia plena; Dóminus tecum: benedícta tu in muliéribus.
20ffb35818daa53f472b.english: Ant. Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee, blessed art thou among women.

befc48e2460c6b5530b5.latin: Ant. Vidérunt eam * fíliæ Sion vernántem in flóribus rosárum, et beatíssimam prædicavérunt.
befc48e2460c6b5530b5.english: Ant. The daughters of Sion saw her in her spring time, amidst the flowers of the roses, and called her most blessed.

04ac76f29fd891aeb3d8.latin: Ant. Vidérunt eam fíliæ Sion vernántem in flóribus rosárum, et beatíssimam prædicavérunt.
04ac76f29fd891aeb3d8.english: Ant. The daughters of Sion saw her in her spring time, amidst the flowers of the roses, and called her most blessed.

e04bff94bd7f16b6aefa.latin:
Sir 24:25; 39:17
In me grátia omnis viæ et veritátis, in me omnis spes vitæ et virtútis. Ego, quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum, fructificávi.
℟. Deo grátias.
℟.br. Post partum, Virgo, * Invioláta permansísti.
℟. Post partum, Virgo, * Invioláta permansísti.
℣. Dei Génetrix, intercéde pro nobis.
℟. Invioláta permansísti.
℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Post partum, Virgo, * Invioláta permansísti.
Hymnus
Te gestiéntem gáudiis,
Te sáuciam dolóribus,
Te iugi amíctam glória,
O Virgo Mater, pángimus.
Ave, redúndans gáudio
Dum cóncipis, dum vísitas;
Et edis, offers, ínvenis,
Mater beáta, Fílium.
Ave, dolens, et íntimo
In corde agónem, vérbera,
Spinas crucémque Fílii
Perpéssa, princeps mártyrum.
Ave, in triúmphis Fílii,
In ígnibus Parácliti,
In regni honóre et lúmine,
Regína fulgens glória.
Veníte, gentes, cárpite
Ex his rosas mystériis,
Et pulchri amóris ínclitæ
Matri corónas néctite.
Glória tibi, Dómine,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
℣. Regína sacratíssimi Rosárii, ora pro nobis.
℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
e04bff94bd7f16b6aefa.english:
Sir 24:25; 39:17
In me is all grace of the way and of the truth; in me is all hope of life and virtue; I have flowered forth like a rose planted by the brooks of water.
℟. Thanks be to God.
℟.br. After childbirth * thou still remainest a Virgin.
℟. After childbirth * thou still remainest a Virgin.
℣. Mother of God, pray for us.
℟. Thou still remainest a Virgin.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. After childbirth * thou still remainest a Virgin.
Hymn
The gladness of thy motherhood,
The anguish of thy suffering,
The glory now that crowns thy brow,
O Virgin-Mother, we would sing.
Hail, blessed Mother, full of joy
In thy consent, thy visit too;
Joy in the birth of Christ on earth,
Joy in him lost and found anew.
Hail, sorrowing in his agony
The blows, the thorns that pierced his brow;
The heavy wood, the shameful rood
Yea! Queen and chief of martyrs thou.
Hail, in the triumph of thy Son,
The quickening flames of Pentecost;
Shining a Queen in light serene,
When all the world is tempest-tost.
O come, ye nations, roses bring,
Culled from these mysteries divine,
And for the Mother of your King
With loving hands your chaplets twine.
We lay our homage at thy feet,
Lord Jesus, thou the Virgin's Son,
With Father and with Paraclete,
Reigning while endless ages run.
Amen.
℣. Queen of the most holy Rosary, pray for us.
℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

1327761d7aee3917c0bf.latin: Ant. Beáta Mater * et intácta Virgo, gloriósa Regína mundi, séntiant omnes tuum iuvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam sacratíssimi Rosárii solemnitátem.
1327761d7aee3917c0bf.english: Ant. Blessed Mother * and Inviolate Maiden, Glorious Queen of the World, may all that keep the solemn Feast of thy Most Holy Rosary feel the might of thine assistance.

c53582fbf0f9e36e815a.latin: Ant. Beáta Mater et intácta Virgo, gloriósa Regína mundi, séntiant omnes tuum iuvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam sacratíssimi Rosárii solemnitátem.
c53582fbf0f9e36e815a.english: Ant. Blessed Mother and Inviolate Maiden, Glorious Queen of the World, may all that keep the solemn Feast of thy Most Holy Rosary feel the might of thine assistance.

a61546d0ceb5c8b6079f.latin:
Te lucis ante términum,
Rerum Creátor, póscimus,
Ut sólita cleméntia
Sis præsul ad custódiam.
Procul recédant sómnia,
Et nóctium phantásmata;
Hostémque nostrum cómprime,
Ne polluántur córpora.
Glória tibi, Dómine,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
a61546d0ceb5c8b6079f.english:
Before the ending of the day,
Creator of the world, we pray
That with thy wonted favor thou
Wouldst be our guard and keeper now.
From all ill dreams defend our eyes,
From nightly fears and fantasies;
Tread under foot our ghostly foe,
That no pollution we may know.
All honour, praise and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-Born, to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father, and to Paraclete.
Amen.

254e3fc605bbf0fcf88d.latin: Ant. Dóminum, qui fecit nos, * Veníte, adorémus.
254e3fc605bbf0fcf88d.english: Ant. It is the Lord That hath made us : * O come, let us worship Him.

6635b3fc02342de30a29.latin:
Nox atra rerum cóntegit
Terræ colóres ómnium:
Nos confiténtes póscimus
Te, iuste iudex córdium.
Ut áuferas piácula,
Sordésque mentis ábluas:
Donésque, Christe, grátiam,
Ut arceántur crímina.
Mens ecce torpet ímpia,
Quam culpa mordet nóxia:
Obscúra gestit tóllere,
Et te, Redémptor, quǽrere.
Repélle tu calíginem
Intrínsecus quam máxime,
Ut in beáto gáudeat
Se collocári lúmine.
Præsta, Pater piíssime,
Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
6635b3fc02342de30a29.english:
The dusky veil of night hath laid
The varied hues of earth in shade;
Before Thee, righteous Judge of all,
We contrite in confession fall.
Take far away our load of sin,
Our soiled minds make clean within:
Thy sov’reign grace, O Christ, impart,
From all offence to guard our heart.
For lo! our mind is dull and cold,
Envenomed by sin’s baneful hold:
Fain would it now the darkness flee,
And seek, Redeemer, unto Thee.
Far from it drive the shades of night,
Its inmost darkness put to flight;
Till in the daylight of the blest
It joys to find itself at rest.
Almighty Father, hear our cry,
Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,
Who, with the Holy Ghost and Thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.
Amen.

b2cd895ee17b670fb73d.english: Ant. Thou hast redeemed the rod * of Thine inheritance.

32963f9fd6507718585b.latin: 73:1 Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem: * irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?
32963f9fd6507718585b.english: 73:1 O God, why hast thou cast us off unto the end: * why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?

ec6e40fac2f1c628a433.latin: 73:2 Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ, * quam possedísti ab inítio.
ec6e40fac2f1c628a433.english: 73:2 Remember thy congregation, * which thou hast possessed from the beginning.

690b0dc49bcd164ae74d.latin: 73:2 Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ: * mons Sion, in quo habitásti in eo.
690b0dc49bcd164ae74d.english: 73:2 The sceptre of thy inheritance which thou hast redeemed: * mount Sion in which thou hast dwelt.

53759a1a39e70dfce173.latin: 73:3 Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!
53759a1a39e70dfce173.english: 73:3 Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end; * see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.

86ad78f68b8f43de7f6b.latin: 73:4 Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.
86ad78f68b8f43de7f6b.english: 73:4 And they that hate thee have made their boasts, * in the midst of thy solemnity.

718daa40f891060e0e35.latin: 73:5 Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.
718daa40f891060e0e35.english: 73:5 They have set up their ensigns for signs, * and they knew not both in the going out and on the highest top.

f704fb1480c9cd700834.latin: 73:6 Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt iánuas eius in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia deiecérunt eam.
f704fb1480c9cd700834.english: 73:6 As with axes in a wood of trees, they have cut down at once the gates thereof, * with axe and hatchet they have brought it down.

3eaab913e572a3120fca.latin: 73:7 Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.
3eaab913e572a3120fca.english: 73:7 They have set fire to thy sanctuary: * they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name on the earth.

bb60fb80e1c4546272ac.latin: 73:8 Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.
bb60fb80e1c4546272ac.english: 73:8 They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together: * Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land.

d9bf380cc53a0d19f029.latin: 73:9 Signa nostra non vídimus, iam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.
d9bf380cc53a0d19f029.english: 73:9 Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet: * and he will know us no more.

3a73a9e862f90838eb3f.latin: 73:10 Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?
3a73a9e862f90838eb3f.english: 73:10 How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach: * is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever?

6c6e9515feb8f9842fe8.latin: 73:11 Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?
